rows.src: ⭐⭐⭐ «De Franceschi» IN THE 1825 PULA CONFIRMATION LISTS — at Premantura and Fažana, and NOT at Medulin, Ližnjan, Šišan or Vodnjan
rows.dest: Slaven Bertoša, «Puljska prezimena prema popisima krizmanika iz 1825. godine», Croatica Christiana Periodica 52 (2003), 107–117 · source: Državni arhiv u Pazinu, «Elenco Cresimati» 245, the four lists of 3, 4, 5 and 6 October 1825
rows.pages: All 11 pages read (pp. 107–117), every village list transcribed.
rows.what: Which surnames stood in each southern-Istrian village in 1825, from one dated archival source
rows.got:
**⭐⭐⭐ THE NAME IS IN TWO OF THE VILLAGES, AND BOTH ARE ALREADY ON THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN LANE.**

| village | surnames in 1825 | De Franceschi? |
|---|---|---|
| **Premantura** (Promontore) | 28 | ✔ **yes** |
| **Fažana** (Fasana) | 11 | ✔ **yes** |
| Medulin (Medolino) | 17 | ✘ no |
| Ližnjan (Lisignano) | 16 | ✘ no |
| Šišan (Sissano) | 12 | ✘ no |
| Vodnjan (Dignano) | 10 | ✘ no |

*The confirmations were given by Teodoro Loredan Balbi, last bishop of Novigrad, over four days in October 1825.*

**⭐⭐ IT INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATES TODAY'S MEDULIN READING.** *The 17 Medulin surnames are* Cukon (Zuccon), De Marin, Garbin, Gasparin, Grakalić, Jukopila, Kirac, Lavrić, **Lazarić**, Lorencin, Marinović, Mihaljević, Misdaris, Privrat, Radošević, Rakić, Vojnić. ***Every single one is a surname read off the Medulin death register this morning, and the list has no Defranceschi in it.*** *Two independent sources, one a register and one a confirmation roll, agree that there was no Defranceschi household at Medulin.*

**⚠ And the absence at Ližnjan is NOT a contradiction.** *These are lists of* **children being confirmed**. *A household with no child of confirmation age in October 1825 does not appear. [The 1815 groom](/liznjan/) was 21 at his marriage and died in 1839; his son Antonius was born in 1819 and would have been six.*

**⭐⭐ AND IT GIVES A CARNIAN DIAGNOSTIC THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT HAVE.** *Bertoša identifies incomers from Friuli and its north-west, **Carnia** — dialectally called* «**Krnjeli**» *in Istria — by surnames ending in* **-is, -as, -os, -es**, *naming* De Prato, Fabris, Fedel, Furlan, Gelmis, **Misdaris**. *The lists carry one surname registered as* «Karnija (Carnia)» *outright:* **Rais**.

**⚠⚠ WHICH MEANS CARNIANS WERE AT LIŽNJAN AND MEDULIN IN 1825.** ***Ližnjan's sixteen include* Fedel *and* Misdaris; *Medulin's seventeen include* Misdaris** — *all three on Bertoša's own Carnian list.* ***This does not make the southern-Istrian Defranceschi Carnian and is not used to.*** *It shows the channel existed: the Val di Gorto had people in these exact parishes. [The archive's Svetvinčenat lane already rests on Kandler's Carnian families](/lines/) — Lupieri, **Fiorencis**, **Fabris**, Crosilla — and two of those four carry the same ending.*
rows.next: ⚠ Two further Bertoša works are now wanted and are NOT in this archive: Miroslav Bertoša, «Etnička struktura Pule od 1613. do 1797.», VHARP XV (1970) 51–130 and XVI (1971) 51–89; and Slaven Bertoša, «Život i smrt u Puli» (Pazin 2002) and «Levantinci u Puli» (2003). Also: the DAP series «Elenco Cresimati» is a record type this archive did not know — confirmation rolls that name people by village.

rows.src: ⚠ Balkan Academia on Albanian and Morlach settlers — it is Carlo's own account retold, and this archive holds the original
rows.dest: Petrit Latifi, «Albanian and Morlach settlers in Istria in the 17th–18th century», Balkan Academia, 20 November 2025
rows.pages: Read in full.
rows.what: Whether it adds to the Seget estate's settlement history
rows.got:
**⚠ CHECKED FIRST, AND IT IS SUBSTANTIALLY ALREADY HERE — in better form.** *The article's spine is an English retelling of* **Carlo De Franceschi's own published account**, *which [this archive carries in the original Italian](/carlos-book/):*

> «Il capitanio di Raspo Alessandro Zorzi in data **15 Febbraro 1604** investiva il capitano **Vincenzo Cuchich da Sebenico** d'un corpo di terreni incolti della circonferenza di circa quattro miglia nel territorio di Umago, sul quale furono da lui trasportate **trenta famiglie da paesi turcheschi**. Il Cuchich vendette nel **1623** la tenuta, che ora chiamasi di **Seghetto e Giuba**, ai N. U. **Valier** di Venezia, dai quali più tardi l'acquistò la nobile famiglia de Franceschi, attuale posseditrice, **emigrata dall'isola di Candia dopo conquistata dai turchi nel 1669**.»

***The archive also holds the 1764 roll of colonists entire*** — *twenty-eight households, a hundred and eleven people counted by name with their home cities: Coron, Napoli di Malvasia, Napoli di Romania, Corinth, Arta. The article mentions six.* ***And it holds the chain by which that roll survives: Giambattista de Franceschi, Deputy of the Imperial Council, sent it to Carlo, who printed it.*** *The article's own cited source is the same — Kandler's* La Provincia *of 1873, with documents from Giambattista.*

**⭐ One useful confirmation:** *it reads the 1623 vendee as* **Valier**, *which is [the reading this archive moved to in September](/corrections/) after carrying Venier. That is now a fourth independent witness for Valier.*

**⚠ THREE THINGS IN IT ARE NOT IN THIS ARCHIVE, and all are weakly sourced:** *(1)* «47 Morlach families from Zeta» *transported after 1571; (2)* **«Other Morlach families were transported from Dalmatia to Istria, Orcevano near Medulin»** *in 1612; (3) eighteen Albanian families from Scutari at Monghebbo in 1611 with 1,239 fields — which is the same event [Pomara documents properly](/searched/) from the Venetian records.*

**⚠⚠ (2) IS WORTH CHASING AND IS NOT TAKEN AS FACT.** *Morlachs settled beside Medulin in 1612 would help explain why [the Medulin registers read this morning](/lines/) are a solid wall of Croatian patronymics with no Italian-surnamed household at all. **But the article gives no archival reference for it**, its onomastic argument is explicitly speculative, and it places Zeta* «in Albania», *which is wrong. Recorded as a lead to verify in the Provincial Archive of Istria, not as a finding.*
rows.next: Verify «Orcevano near Medulin», 1612, in the Provincial Archive of Istria or in Bertoša. If true it belongs on the Medulin entry.

rows.src: ⭐⭐⭐ FLORISTÁN 2025 — Morosini decided the refugees would go to the empty Adriatic, and the evacuation was no shipwreck
rows.dest: José Manuel Floristán, «La capitulación de Candía de 1669», Archivo de la Frontera / CEDCS, ISBN 978-84-690-5859-6
rows.pages: 25 pp., read in full.
rows.what: How the Cretan refugees actually left, and why they ended up on this coast
rows.got:
**⭐⭐⭐ THE HINGE THIS ARCHIVE HAS NEVER HAD.** *Floristán publishes the relation the Grand Master of Malta sent to the Viceroy of Sicily after the fall.*

> «En total abandonaron Candía unas **12.000 personas**. Algunos quisieron regresar movidos por los ofrecimientos que les hacía el gran visir, mas no pudieron hacerlo porque ***Morosini ya había decidido su asentamiento en lugares deshabitados del golfo Adriático***.»

***The refugees did not find their way to Istria and Dalmatia. Morosini chose it for them, and those who wanted to stay on the Vizier's terms were not allowed to.*** *And he did it while surrendering the city* **without the Senate's authorisation** *(Pérez Negrete).*

**⚠⚠ AND IT CORRECTS THIS ARCHIVE.** *[The Crete lane](/lines/) drew* «**Wrecked** · 1669 — the fleet is wrecked in a storm» *and called the lane* **documented**. ***The relation describes a negotiated embarkation over twenty-two days***, *the Grand Vizier granting extensions while his army waited* «con una quietud y una paciencia extraordinaria», *and offering to forward the luggage to Suda. Four other sources read the same day are silent on any wreck.* **[Corrected; the node is now «Taken off» and the wreck is an open question, not a fact.](/corrections/)**

*Other dates fixed: capitulation* **5 September 1669**, *Ottomans enter* **27 September**; *Morosini told his war council on* **27 August** *that the city must fall.*
rows.next: ⚠ Ask where the wreck tradition came from. Candidate: the Psara storm of 17–18 March 1648, 17 galleys lost, Grimani drowned.

rows.src: Three more on the Candia war — two useful for context, one about the besiegers and not this family
rows.dest: Pérez Negrete in «Francesco Morosini 1619–1694» (2019) · «L'Esercito veneziano e la difesa di Candia» (Ca' Foscari MA) · Kolovos in «The Eastern Mediterranean under Ottoman Rule: Crete 1645–1840» (2008)
rows.pages: All three text-extracted and searched for Franceschi, profughi, rifugiati, Zante, Istria, Parenzo, Sebenico, pensione, nobili, capitolazione, naufragio.
rows.what: Whether the war literature touches this family or its route
rows.got:
**Pérez Negrete** *(in the Morosini quatercentenary volume, Poligrafico e Zecca dello Stato 2019)*: *the war's shape — Ottoman landing* **24 June 1645**, *Canea lost 1645, Rethymno* **3 November 1646**, *Candia besieged* **22 years** *in two phases (1648–49, 1667–69); Köprülü came with nearly* **70,000** *men; France and Malta gave the island up in August 1669; Morosini surrendered on 6 September* ***without the Senate's authorisation***.

**⭐ The Ca' Foscari thesis** *gives the road:* «Da Venezia le navi… procedevano lungo la costa dalmata fino ad arrivare a Corfù, quindi verso **Zante**…» — ***Zante and Corfu were the two staging ports on the Venice–Candia route, and the Dalmatian coast was its first leg.*** *This family's Candia → Zante → Šibenik is not a wandering; it is the supply road walked backwards.* *It also records the* **Psara storm of 17–18 March 1648** *— 17 galleys lost, Grimani drowned — which is the only fleet wrecked in a storm in this war, and it is twenty-one years too early to be ours.* *And it notes Venetian families buying their way into the Senate to fund the war, which is the world a refugee family entering a noble council belongs to.*

**⚠ Kolovos, «A Town for the Besiegers»** *is about the Ottoman siege-town outside Candia, 1650–69 — the other side of the wall.* ***No refugees, no evacuation, no Franceschi.*** *A fine paper and nothing for this archive.*

rows.src: ⭐⭐ JACKSON 1887 — «thirty-five families» at Parenzo, 1669–1692, and it contradicts the sixty
rows.dest: T. G. Jackson, Dalmatia, the Quarnero and Istria, vol. III (Oxford 1887)
rows.pages: Full volume text (784,665 chars) searched for Franceschi, Seget, Seghetto, Candia, Crete, Umago, Cittanova, Parenzo, Capodistria, Greek, Zante, Sebenico, refugee.
rows.what: Whether a 19th-century authority confirms the post-Candia settlement at Poreč
rows.got:
**⭐⭐ IT DOES, AND IT GIVES A DIFFERENT NUMBER.**

> «Finally, **between 1669 and 1692** several refugees from Candia, after it was taken by the Turks, came to **Parenzo**, where **thirty-five families** received allotments of houses and lands.»

***Joksimović, from Camillo's 1952 monograph, says SIXTY families at the same town for the same event.*** **Thirty-five against sixty.** *Neither is obviously wrong; this archive records the disagreement rather than choosing, and notes that [the one study written from the Poreč council's own records](/seget/) — Camillo De Franceschi 1952 — is what would settle it.*

**And Jackson supplies the scale that makes the grant intelligible:** *Parenzo* «sank from three thousand in the fifteenth century to **less than one hundred in 1646**», *and the Senate restored it with colonists* «from Dalmatia, Candia and the Morea». ***A town of under a hundred people receiving thirty-five families was being refounded, not relieved.***

*Also: Montenegrins from Cernizza near Budua settled near Pola in* **1657**.

⚠ **Jackson is not an independent witness so much as a careful one:** *he cites* **Carlo De Franceschi's «L'Istria» (Parenzo 1879)** *seventeen times through the volume. The family's historians are underneath the standard English account of this coast as well.* ⚠ *No Seget, no Seghetto, and no De Franceschi of this line in the volume.*
rows.next: De Franceschi 1952 now has to settle a number as well as a question.

rows.src: ⚠ Joksimović, Tabula 17 (2020) — READ IN FULL, and it is the paper this archive already mined for the Camillo citation
rows.dest: Milena Joksimović, «Rediscovering the Greeks… from the Perspective of Istria», Tabula 17 (2020), 169–201
rows.pages: All 36 pages read.
rows.what: Whether the paper David sent adds to the Candia story
rows.got:
**⚠ CHECKED FIRST, AND IT IS NOT A DISCOVERY.** *[This archive has carried the* «De Franceschi 1952» *citation since September](/searched/), explicitly recorded as* «Found cited in Milena Joksimović, Tabula 17 (2020)», ***which is this very paper***. *It is already first on the acquisition list. Saying otherwise would have been [the re-run this archive has been caught in before](/method/).*

**What reading it in full DOES add**, *beyond the bare citation:* *(1)* **the sentence the footnote hangs on** — «in the period following the loss of Candia (1669) some **60 families** were granted houses in **Poreč**, while several families arrived in Pula»; *(2)* **the three-wave frame** — Nauplion/Monemvasia 1540, Cyprus 1571, Crete 1669, ~**4,000** Greeks into Istria in all; *(3)* ***Greeks and Cypriots were planted at Ližnjan, Šišan and Marlera*** — *the Flebra family settled Cypriots* «between Šišan and Ližnjan», *the Sozomeno were given land* «near Ližnjan», *and 1585 Cretans from Rethymnon settled* «near Šišan and at Marlera»; *(4)* **the collapse of the Istrian Greek community**, *from ~100 families under Bishop Barbabianca (1567–82) to* ***five people*** *under Bernardino Corniani (1664–89)* — *so a family arriving out of Candia in 1669 arrived when there was no longer a Greek community to join.*

**⚠ (3) is the one that bites.** *[/liznjan/](/liznjan/) carried nothing about Greek or Cypriot settlement, and this archive spent today reading Ližnjan's and Medulin's registers.*
rows.next: De Franceschi 1952 (AMSI n.s. 2, 57–115) is still unread and still the deciding document. Add Greek/Cypriot settlement to /liznjan/.

rows.src: Pomara, Diasporas 43 (2025) — how Venice actually planted refugees in Istria, with the numbers
rows.dest: Bruno Pomara, «An Attempted Albanian Settlement in Istria… (1610–1612)», Diasporas 43 (2025), 95–127
rows.pages: Read in full online.
rows.what: The mechanism behind the Seget land grant of 1604 and the post-1669 settlements
rows.got: **New to this archive — published 11 June 2025.** *⚠ It is about* **Albanians**, *not Cretans, and is used only for the machinery.* **Istria's population: ~60,000 (1610) → 36,000 (1625) → 30,000 (1630s)** — *a province losing half its people in a generation.* *Refugees were colonists on terms: a loan of* **500 ducats** *for tools and animals, repayable without interest from the third year; cash advances per household head; and land.* ***One group of eight families received 700 plots near UMAG***, *described as* «uncultivated, thorny and stony», *with the obligation to make them* «a perfect crop». *Friction with the existing population is documented, and prejudice in the* **Poreč** *area is traced from the late 17th century.* **That is the frame the Seget grant of 1604 and the Poreč sixty of 1669 both sit in.**

rows.src: Ortalli & Schmitt, «Balcani occidentali, Adriatico e Venezia» — the Šibenik leg had a Greek quay in 1533
rows.dest: G. Ortalli / O. J. Schmitt (eds.), Balcani occidentali, Adriatico e Venezia fra XIII e XVIII secolo, Schriften der Balkan-Kommission 50
rows.pages: 403 pages, text-extracted and searched for Candia, Creta, Zante, Istria, Parenzo, Capodistria, Franceschi.
rows.what: Whether the Candia→Zante→Šibenik route has independent support
rows.got:
**⭐ A notarial act of 1533 records Greeks from MONEMVASIA and ZANTE at ŠIBENIK**, *among them a* «papas grecus», *trading between that port and Split.* ***This archive's timeline has the family at Šibenik in 1674 by way of Zante, and could never say why Šibenik — the answer is that Šibenik had a Zante-fed Greek colony a hundred and forty years earlier.*** *It shows the road, not the journey.*

**And the ground was empty:** *at the end of the* «catastrophic war of Candia (1644–1669)» *the whole population of Dalmatia was* **48,000**, *Šibenik holding fewer people than in 1559.*

⚠ *The twelve* «Franceschi» *hits in this volume are all* **Carlo**, *cited as an authority on Istrian settlement and language — which this archive already knew. No new person of the name.*

rows.what: Every Defranceschi in the Medulin death register, read page by page rather than searched
rows.got:
**Twenty-nine frames read, covering deaths from 1801 to 1893.** *The register is ruled and columned — «Nomen, Cognomen et Conditio defuncti» is its own column — so every entry's surname was read, not sampled.*

**⭐⭐⭐ TWO DEFRANCESCHI, where the FamilySearch index lists none in this book:**

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **19 Dec 1833** | «Mathæus Defranceschi q. Ant. fil. **miles**» | 40 a., chronicus morb. |
| **16 Nov 1873** | «Maria (**Defranceschi**) Ant. Verinic uxor» | 78 a., mors ord. |

*Both are written up in rows of their own.*

**⚠ AND THE NIL IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE FINDING.** *Across twenty-nine frames and something over a thousand burials, those are the only two. Medulin's dead in this century are* **Radossevich** *(by far the commonest),* Lorenzin, Lazarich, Chirgo/Kirac, Gracalich/Grahalic, Zuccon, Priurat/Privrat, Giucapilla, Vojak/Vojnich, Demarin, Marinovich, Micalevich, Camerich, Clarich, Surian, Rumez, Laverich, Bakich, Matika, Ricato, Leverich, Jadrescè, Poscich *and thirty more of the same shape.* ***There is no Defranceschi HOUSEHOLD at Medulin in the nineteenth century — only a soldier who died here and a daughter who married in.***

**Incidental things the book gave up:** *Venetian lagoon sailors dying here in 1831–32 —* «Vincentius Penso nauta e Chiozza», «Angelus Penso», «Carolus Rosada nauta e Pelestrina»; *a note in 1854 on sailors* «ex America provenientes in mari suffocatos»; *a* **cholera outbreak in 1855**; *the parish priest Pietro Radolovich dying in 1831 aged 89, and his successor-but-one* «A.R.D. Jacovich Andreas, emeritus Parochus **Medolinensis**» *in 1893 aged 87 — another attestation of the place-name.*
rows.next: Read frames 32-40 to finish the book, and frames 1-2 which were skipped. Then births 1801-1890 (88 frames, 9R2H-HZ2) and marriages 1831-1899 (41 frames, 9R2H-444).

rows.src: ⭐⭐⭐ MEDULIN DEATHS 1873 — «Maria (Defranceschi) Ant. Verinic uxor», a Defranceschi DAUGHTER married into Medulin
rows.dest: Medulin «Liber Defunctorum» 1801–1899, waypoint 9R2H-HZ7 · HDA inv. br. 158 · frame 21, ark 3:1:3QSQ-G99X-KZBV, register page 33
rows.pages: Frames 3-21 of 40 read.
rows.what: The second Defranceschi in the Medulin deaths book, found while reading it end to end
rows.got:
**⭐⭐⭐ A DEFRANCESCHI DAUGHTER, MARRIED INTO MEDULIN.** *Page 33, the 1873 block, annual number 139:*

> «**Maria (Defranceschi) Ant. Verinic uxor**» — *aged* **78** *(the figure corrected in the ink), «mors ord[inaria]», **16 November 1873**.*

**⭐ The parentheses are the scribe's maiden-name convention, and the line immediately below proves it:** «Maria (Vrinic q. Nic.) vid. Georgii Lorenzin» — *Maria née Vrinic, widow of Georgio Lorenzin. The same page, the same hand, the same bracket.* ***So this is a woman born Defranceschi who married Antonio Verinic of Medulin.***

**Seventy-eight in 1873 means born about 1795** — ***the same generation as the Ližnjan groom of 1815 (born about 1794) and the soldier who died here in 1833 (born about 1793).*** *Three Defranceschi of one generation around these two villages.*

**⚠ What this does and does not show.** *It does* **not** *give her father, her birthplace or her parish of origin — the entry names only her husband.* ***It does show that the name reached Medulin by marriage*** *even though no Defranceschi household appears in the parish's own registers, which is exactly the [daughters' villages](/lines/) pattern this archive already tracks at Pomer, Krbune, Galižana and Labin.* **Her marriage should be in the Medulin marriages 1831–1899 (`9R2H-444`) if it happened here — but at 78 in 1873 she is likelier to have married about 1815–1825, before that book opens.**

rows.dest: Medulin «Liber Defunctorum» 1801–1899, waypoint 9R2H-HZ7 · HDA, Matična knjiga umrlih, inv. br. 158 · film frame 11, ark 3:1:3QS7-L99X-KCP6, register page 12

rows.pages: Frames 3-11 of 40 read so far; the entry is on frame 11, register page 12.
rows.what: The tree-only «Mattheus Defranceschi b. 1793 d. 1833» the roster places at Medulin
rows.got:
**⭐⭐⭐ THE NAME IS IN THE MEDULIN BOOK AFTER ALL, and the tree was right about him.**

*Medulin* «Liber Defunctorum», *page 12, the 1833 block, line 9, annual number 43:*

> «**Mathæus Defranceschi q. Ant. fil. miles**» — *Cath., **40. a.**, «chronicus morb[us]», died* **19 December 1833** *(the month a ditto of «Xbris» on the line above), subscribed by the administrator.*

**Forty in December 1833 means born about 1793** — *which is exactly the year [the family tree already carried for him](/who/mattheus-defranceschi/).* **And the register adds a fact the tree did not have: he is «miles», a SOLDIER**, *and «q. Ant.», the son of a dead Antonio.*

**⚠ THIS IS A VERIFICATION AND NOT A DISCOVERY, and the archive should say so.** *The roster row for this man already carried the ark* `3:1:3QS7-L99X-KCP6` — ***the very frame the entry is written on***. *The lead was in this archive's own data and nobody had opened it. It is precisely the case [check-leads.py was written for](/worklist/) ten hours ago.*

**⚠⚠ HE IS NOT THE LIŽNJAN MAN, AND THE TWO MUST NOT BE JOINED.** *[The «deto Marulin» groom who married at Ližnjan in November 1815](/liznjan/) was still alive to be buried at Ližnjan in **1839**, an* agricola. *This man was dead by December 1833, and a* soldier. ***Two men called Mattheus, each the son of an Antonio, in parishes four kilometres apart, both dying at forty, six years apart.*** *That is the exact shape of a false join and it is refused here.*

**⚠ AND THE MAGNIFICATION CHANGED THE READING.** *At page scale the cause of death read* «dissenteria»; *at native resolution it is* «chronicus morb.». ***The rule about reading a doubtful word only at magnification earned its keep on this entry.*** *The same scribe writes «Lorenzin», «Longovich» and «Radossevich» on the lines either side — [plated together so the hand can be judged against itself](/liznjan/).*
rows.next: Frames 12-40 of the deaths book are still to read, then births 1801-1890 (88 frames) and marriages 1831-1899 (41). The second tree-only Medulin person, «Antonio Defranceschi b. 1819», should be testable in the births book.

rows.what: Whether the Defranceschi are at Medulin before Ližnjan's books open in 1815 — the question «nata e Medolino» raised
rows.got:
**⭐⭐ THE WHOLE BOOK IS READ AND THE NAME IS NOT IN IT.** *Twenty-four frames, every one rendered at native resolution and looked at. The register runs baptisms 1677–1705 and marriages 1666–1704, bound out of order.* ***Not one Defranceschi, De Franceschi, Franceschi or Defranceski appears anywhere in it.***

**⭐ AND THE NEGATIVE IS THE FINDING, because of WHAT is there instead.** *Medulin in these years is a village of Croatian patronymics and nothing else:* **Radonovich** *(dominant — dozens of entries),* Micaglievich, Gracalich, Grubisich, Golemovich, Stefanelich, Marinovich, Surionich, Braicovich, Galavich, Loggenae, Camevich, Giuras, Sain, Godina, Lorenzin, Tanuda, Boglich, Radosevich, **Lazarich**, Voinich, Pribinovich, Micolich, Franulich, Boiach, Bosiscovich, Pettinovich, Goncalich, Sule, Guerilla, Sfarich, Miscich, Craneich, Garbin, Mucich, Baioch, Carlich. ***The only Italian names in the book are the clergy*** — *D. Pietro Binussi the long-serving pievano, D. Ant.o Zuanich, Pre Bortolo Chrulich the chaplain, P. Bernardino Corniani, Mattio Juliani — **and one gentleman godfather, «il sig.r Toscavin Filiaretto».** There is no Italian-surnamed household at Medulin in this book at all.*

**⭐⭐ THE PLACE-NAME QUESTION IS SETTLED, in the parish's own hand.** *The archive had to take on trust that* «nata e Medolino» *in the 1861 Ližnjan marriage meant this village. The book says so itself, four times over:* «**D. Pietro Binussi Piev.o di MEDULINO**» *(frame 12, the incumbent styling his own cure),* «**Gerol.mo Gracalich da MEDOLIN**» *(frame 11, a witness),* «**Io Piero, Pre di MEDOLIN**» *(frame 19, 23 November 1666)* *and again at 12 February 1674.* ***Medolino is Medulin, on the evidence of the parish that wrote it.***

**⭐⭐ AND LIŽNJAN IS ALL OVER THIS BOOK, from 1666.** *At least ten instances:* godparents «da Lisigna» *and* «da Lisignan» *(frames 5, 7 ×2, 12, 16, 17, 22 ×3, 23)*, *a bride* «Perca … Medosich da Lisignan» *married at Medulin on 26 December 1671, and the one that matters most —* **«Io Pre Ant.o de Lorenzin, PIEV. DI LISIGNAN» officiating a marriage recorded in the MEDULIN book, 9 October 1666.** *The two parishes' clergy served each other's altars.* ***That is a hundred and fifty years before the 1815 Ližnjan marriage this archive has been trying to explain, and it means traffic between the two villages is not a hypothesis but a documented habit.***

**⭐ LAZARICH IS A MEDULIN FAMILY.** *The 1861 Ližnjan bride is* «Fosca nata Lazarić … nata e Medolino». *Lazarich stands in this book twice as a Medulin name — a godmother in February 1701 and a godfather in April 1705.* ***Her surname belongs here, independently of her own entry.***

**⚠⚠ TWO OPENINGS OF THIS BOOK ARE IN GLAGOLITIC AND WERE NOT READ.** *Frame 21's right page and frame 22's left page are written in the Croatian liturgical script, not the Italian hand of the rest — four or five entries each, with ruled rubric lines.* ***This session cannot read Glagolitic and does not pretend to.*** *They are recorded as **unread**, not as nil. A name could be in them, rendered in Glagolitic letters, and nothing here would have caught it.*

**⚠ And frame 14's left page is not faint but GONE** — *the iron-gall has washed out completely, leaving two date headers (15 9bre 1693, one struck through) and about four lines of ghost. A contrast stretch over the 2nd–70th percentile recovered nothing further.*
rows.next: The Glagolitic openings on frames 21 and 22 need somebody who reads the script. The other three Medulin books are untouched: births 1801-1890 (9R2H-HZ2, 88 frames), deaths 1801-1899 (9R2H-HZ7, 40), marriages 1831-1899 (9R2H-444, 41). ⚠ Note the gap this book leaves: Medulin's births begin only in 1801, so a man born about 1794 — the 1815 Ližnjan groom — is in no Medulin birth register that survives.

rows.src: ⚠⭐ LIŽNJAN deaths 1839 — the 1815 groom's own burial, «d.to Marulin» a second time; AND the deaths scout's crop is found to have cut the bottom off every page
rows.waypointNote: Volume fixed by ark containment.
rows.pages: Frame 12, book page 93, the FULL page height read at last. ⚠ This row also records that frames 0–71 were previously scanned with a crop covering only y 0.09–0.46 — about the top 44% of each page — and the book is being re-scanned.
rows.what: Why the scout had not reported the death the archive's own lead XQM3-21M6 points at
rows.got:
**⭐⭐⭐ THE DEATH OF THE MAN WHO MARRIED IN 1815 — and the byname is on him twice.**

**Ližnjan** «Liber Defunctorum», **page 93, 1839**:

> «**Addì 20 Xbre 1839**» · **house 17** · «**Mattio Franceschi d.to Marulin, agr.**» · *Cattolico, Maschio,* «**ann. 40**»

***Mattio Franceschi detto Marulin, agricola, of house 17, died 20 December 1839, aged forty.*** *House 17 is [the house he married into in 1815](/liznjan/) and the house his children were born in — Antonio 1819, Mattia 1821, Gregorio 1822.*

**⭐ «d.to Marulin», again.** *[The 1815 marriage called him](/liznjan/)* «**Mario de Franceschi deto Marulin di Antonio**». *Here is the same byname at his burial, twenty-four years later, in a different book and a different hand.* ***Two independent witnesses to the name settle it:*** *it is a byname, not a place, and the reading that nearly made it* «Madolin» *is closed.*

**⚠ The age does not agree with the marriage.** *1815 gave his Ætas as* **21** *(born about 1794); 1839 gives* **40** *(born about 1799). Five years apart. Both are the parish's own figures and neither is corrected here — register ages are frequently round numbers, and [this archive records the discrepancy rather than splitting it](/method/).*

**⭐ And it closes a lead the archive had held and never taken up.** `register.json` *carried* `XQM3-21M6` — «**Mattio Francesch, b. 1799, d. 20 Dec 1839, Ližnjan**» — *uncited by any roster row. The date matches exactly and the derived birth year matches the age. [It was named as a candidate for Maddalena's «fu Matteo» yesterday](/who/maddalena-defranceschi-naskovic/) and left there because a date that fits is not a match.* **It is now read on the page.**

---

**⚠⚠ THE SCOUT OF THE DEATH REGISTER WAS CALLED «END TO END» AND IT WAS NOT. It read the top of every page and cut the bottom off.**

*The crop was* `y 0.09–0.46` *of the frame. Measured against the book, the page itself runs from about* `0.12` *to* `0.92`. ***So roughly the top 44% of every page was read and the rest was never seen.*** *Eleven people of the name were found, and they were real — but the claim that the book had been covered end to end was false.*

**[This is the crop-drift trap this archive has now hit five times](/method/)**, *and the previous four were all on the Pazin reels. It is the same failure: a crop that looks right on the frame you chose it with, and silently clips every frame after.*

**How it was caught.** *David asked whether* «Medolino» *was Medulin, and noted that Defranceschi seem to cluster there. Checking that sent this session back to a lead it had never taken up —* `XQM3-21M6`, «**Mattio Francesch, d. 20 Dec 1839, Ližnjan**» — *and asked why the scout had not reported that death.* **Because the entry sits at 0.52 of the page height, below where the crop stopped.** *A question about a place name exposed a systematic hole in a sweep.*

**The fix is one number.** *At the same magnification,* `y 0.09–0.95` *renders the whole page into a single 2048×2304 canvas that reads exactly as well as the old one. The deaths book is being re-scanned with it, and the marriage and birth helpers carried the same wrong y-range and are corrected before use.*
rows.next: Re-scan all 72 deaths frames at full page height; the marriage and birth helpers carried the same wrong y-range and are corrected before use.

rows.what: Origin — David asked that anything showing where the Ližnjan Defranceschi come from be watched for
rows.got:
**⭐⭐⭐ THE MARRIAGE OF [FUSCA NÉE LAZARIć](/who/fusca-defranceschi-lazaric/) — and it gives her birthplace, which is the first plain statement of origin the scout has found.**

**Ližnjan** «Liber Copulatorum», **page 22, entry 168**:

> «**1 Junii 1861**» · **house 59** · *SPONSUS* «**Antonius Defranceski q. Matthæi, agr.**», *catholic, Ætas* **41**, ***Viduus*** · *SPONSA* «**Fosca nata Lazarić q. Simeonis, V[idu]a q. Antonii Mohorić agr., nata e Medolino**»

**⭐ «NATA E MEDOLINO» — she was born at MEDULIN**, *the next parish down the cape. [Her burial of 1888](/who/fusca-defranceschi-lazaric/) *gave* «nat. 30/4 1821» *and an age of 67; this gives the place to go with the date.*

**⭐ AND BOTH OF THEM WERE WIDOWED.** *He is* «**Viduus**»; *she is* «**vidua q. Antonii Mohorić**» — ***a second marriage on both sides***. *That is why she appears in no earlier Defranceschi entry: before 1861 she was a Mohorić.*

**⭐ And he is the son of the man who married in 1815.** «*Antonius Defranceski* **q. Matthæi**» — *son of the late Matthæus — aged 41 in June 1861, so born about 1820.* **[The baptism book has an Antonio born 15 September 1819 at house 17](/liznjan/)**, *to* «Mattio De Franceschi» *and* «Madalena Percovich» — ***the couple of the 1815 marriage***. *The age fits to within months and the patronymic fits exactly.* **⚠ It is not proved identical here** — *no entry says so in one breath — but three generations now stand in a row from the parish's own books:* **Antonio → Mattio/Mario detto Marulin (m. 1815) → Antonius (b. 1819, m. 1861)**.

**⚠⚠ AND IT CORRECTS SOMETHING THIS ARCHIVE SAID THIS MORNING.** *The commit that finished the death register called the 1896 burial* «**the first spelled with the modern -ski**». ***It is not.*** *Here is* «**Defranceski**» *in the marriage register in* **1861**, *thirty-five years earlier, in a different book and a different hand. [Corrected](/corrections/).*
rows.next: Marriage frames 17–35, then the births book. And Medulin's own registers, which this archive has never opened — Fosca Lazarić was born there and the 1831 entry «della Carniola di Madolin» shows the parish traffic runs both ways.

rows.pages: Frames 3–10 of 36, both pages of each opening, SPONSUS and SPONSA name columns read at native resolution; the 1815 groom's cell re-rendered at nine times magnification to settle one word. ⚠ PART OF A SCOUT IN PROGRESS — frames 11–35 not yet read, and the births book not begun.
rows.what: Where the Ližnjan Defranceschi come from — David asked for origin to be watched for specifically
rows.got:
**⭐⭐⭐ THE EARLIEST DEFRANCESCHI EVENT IN ANY LIŽNJAN BOOK — the marriage that starts the parish's line.**

**Ližnjan** «Liber Copulatorum», **page 1, entry 2**, *the second marriage the book ever records:*

> «**12 Novembre 1815**» · **house 17** · *SPONSUS* «**Mario de Franceschi deto Marulin di Antonio**», *catolico, Ætas* **21**, *celibes* · *SPONSA* «**Maddalena Percouich di Antonio**», *catolica, Ætas* **27**, *celibes* · *TESTES* «Giacomo Bubich di Iseppo», «Antonio Clunich di Stefano», «Gregorio Iucopila»

**Aged twenty-one in November 1815, so born about 1794. His father is Antonio.** *And this is the couple whose children fill house 17 in the baptism book — Antonio 1819, Mattia 1821, Gregorio 1822 — all to* «Mattio Franceschi di Antonio» *and* «Mandalena Pecouichi».

**⭐ HE CARRIES A BYNAME:** «**deto Marulin**» — *detto Marulin, «called Marulin».*

**⚠ And the byname was nearly read as a PLACE.** *The same book, sixteen years later, writes a groom as* «**Giacomo Micalouich figlio di Giorgio della Carniola di Madolin**» — *Carniola, and Madolin for Medulin, the next parish. Against that,* «ma—rulin» *looked like it might be* «Madolin», *which would have made it an origin rather than a nickname.* **[It is not](/method/):** *at nine times magnification the letter has no ascender, and this scribe gives every* **d** *a tall one —* «di Antonio», «de Franceschi», «deto» *itself, all on the same line. It is an* **r**. *The hand decided it, not the plausibility.*

**⚠ NO PLACE OF ORIGIN IS GIVEN, and that is worth stating carefully.** *The book does record origins when it wants to —* «della Carniola di Madolin» *proves it —* ***but that entry is from 1831, in a later and far more verbose format***. *The 1815 page is terse: four columns, no* `Conditio` *for the spouses, no parents named. **So the silence here is weak evidence at best, and no conclusion is drawn from it.** [A nil names the terms tried](/method/): what was looked for was a* «di» *or* «della» *phrase in the Nomen cell, and there is none beyond the patronymic.*

**⭐ A second marriage, and a daughter going out.** *Page 15, entry 113:* «**23 Febbrajo 1848**», *house 41 —* «**Martino Mocovich**» *and* «**Maria figlia Matteo Defranceschi**», *with* «**Defranceschi**» *written again in the* `Genitori della sposa` *column. A daughter of a Matteo, marrying out in 1848.*
rows.next: Marriage frames 11–35, then the births book (83 frames). The byname «Marulin» has not been looked for anywhere else; if it is a Carnian or Venetian form it may be the origin thread the place-name is not giving.

rows.pages: ALL 72 FRAMES, 0–71. The NOMEN DEFUNCTI column of BOTH pages of every opening rendered at native resolution via Deep Zoom tiles and read for the surname, with every doubtful word magnified. ⚠ A SCOUT, NOT A WALK: the Morbus, Ætas and Anagrafe columns of non-Defranceschi entries were not read, and no year was transcribed end to end. walked:false for that reason.
rows.what: Every person of the name in the Ližnjan death register, 1815–1900
rows.got:
**⭐⭐⭐ THE WHOLE BOOK, FRAME BY FRAME — 72 frames, 1815 to 1900, every opening looked at.**

*Not a transcription: the* `NOMEN DEFUNCTI` *column of* ***both pages of every opening*** *was rendered at native resolution and read for the surname, with every doubtful word magnified. [That is a scout, not a walk](/method/), and the row says* `walked:false` *for that reason.*

**ELEVEN people OF THE NAME are buried in this book.** *Four were already documented here this week; two are new; one is still unverified.*

| frame | date | house | the entry |
|---|---|---|---|
| 17 | **6 Jan 1849** | 17 | «Maddalena fu Matteo Defranceschi» · *read 16 Oct 2026: aged 61; widow or daughter of Matteo — not settled* |
| 18 | **16 Jan 1850** | 17 | «Matteo figlio di Matteo Defranceschi» — ⚠ *misread: the page says «Mattio figlio di **Antonio** Defranceschi», 9 days old; read at full size 16 Oct 2026* |
| 26 | *1861* | — | «Gregorius Defranceschi…» — **⚠ not yet verified** |
| 31 | 6 Jul 1870 | 3 | «Fusca filia Mathæi Defranceschi» · *[read](/who/tusca-defranceschi/)* |
| 37 | 22 Feb 1875 | 61 | the twins **Maria** and **Anastasia** · *[read](/who/maria-defranceschi/)* |
| 38 | 19 Sep 1875 | 71 | «Joannes fil. Justinæ Defranceschi» · *[read](/who/joannes-defranceschi/)* |
| 49 | **11 Oct 1884** | 82 | «**Maria Defranceschi**» · ***closes one of the seventeen*** |
| 53 | Mar 1888 | 82 | «Josephus Defranceschi, Gregorii et Maria Vojnić» · *[read](/who/josephus-defranceschi/)* |
| 54 | 17 Aug 1888 | 75 | «Fusca uxor Antonii Defranceschi nata Lazarić» · *[read](/who/fusca-defranceschi-lazaric/)* |
| 58 | 18 Feb 1891 | 3 | «Mathæus Defranceschi, Mathæi et Annæ Skoko» · *[read](/who/math-us-defranceschi/)* |
| 64 | **21 Dec 1896** | 3 | «**Josephus Defranceski, Matthæi servi**» · ***new*** |

**⭐ SEVEN MORE are children of Defranceschi DAUGHTERS who married out** — *the surname is in the mother's place, which is why no search for the name as a principal would ever have found them:*

| frame | year | the entry |
|---|---|---|
| 33 | 1872 | Mathæus **Ruman**, *Josephi et Mariæ Defranceschi* |
| 35 | 1873 | a child of *Antonii et Magdalenæ Defranceschi* — **Našković** |
| 35 | 1873 | Joannes Baptista, *Josephi et Catharinæ Defranceschi* — **Jelčić** |
| 41 | ~1879 | Gregorius **Sandalj**, *Joannis et Luciæ* |
| 42 | 1880 | Magdalena **Ruman**, *Josephi et Mariæ Defranceschi* |
| 46 | 1883 | Josephus **Ruman**, *Josephi et Mariæ Defranceschi* |
| 50 | 1885 | Josephus, *Josephi et Catharinæ de Franceschi* — **Jelčić** |

**⚠ None of those seven is in this roster.** *They are recorded here as what they are — entries read on a page, not people minted — because each needs its own reading before it becomes a record.*

**⭐⭐ AND THE LAST ENTRY OF THE NAME IN THE BOOK CHANGES THE SPELLING.** *21 December 1896, house 3:* «**Josephus Defranceski, Matthæi servi**», *twenty months old, dead of* «angina». ***The -ski ending the family uses today, written in the register in 1896*** — *every earlier entry in this book spells it* «Defranceschi». *And his father is a* **servus**, *where [the Matthæus of the same house 3 was an* ***agricola*** *in 1870](/who/tusca-defranceschi/). [He is minted](/who/josephus-defranceski/).*

**What the scout also establishes, which a hit list cannot:**

- **The register's content runs frames 3–66.** *Frame 0 is the HDA title card, 1 a resolution target, 2 the marbled cover with its label* «Ližnjan — Mat. knjiga umrlih od 1815 do 1900 god.»; *67 is* «END OF ITEM», *68* «KRAJ» *and reel 23, 69–71 targets.*
- **Two frames are RE-SHOOTS with loose documents laid across the page.** *Frame* **16** *repeats frame 15 with a German* «**Tauf-Schein**» — *Diözese Seckau, Steiermark, a baptismal certificate of* **1916** — *lying on it; frame* **60** *repeats 59 with a* «**Certificato d'ispezione cadaverica**». *[The same thing the Gologorica reels do](/gologorica-line/), and it means* ***72 frames is not 72 openings***.
- **The book carries ANAGRAFE references** — «p. 325 III.5», «II. 85» — *against its entries from about 1870, [just as the baptism book does](/liznjan/).*
- *Frame 29's right page carries a long Italian narrative entry of several lines, unlike anything around it. It was not read.*

**⚠ WHAT THIS SCOUT DOES NOT CLAIM.** *It read the* `NOMEN DEFUNCTI` *column. It did* **not** *read the Morbus, Ætas or Anagrafe columns of entries that carry no Defranceschi, and it did not transcribe a single year end to end. A woman of the name entered only by her husband's surname, with no* «nata», *would not be caught by it. One candidate — frame 26, 1861 — remains unverified.*
rows.next: Frame 26 (1861) still wants verifying. The seven married-out children each want their own reading. And the births (83 frames) and marriages (36 frames) are not yet scouted.

rows.src: ⭐⭐ FamilySearch — LIŽNJAN deaths 1875: a twenty-two-day-old child whose entry names his MOTHER and no father, and a second Justina Defranceschi
