rows.pages: Frame 38, book page 68 — entries 9–12 of 1875 and the opening of 1876 read at native resolution, with entry 10 read across every column. ⚠ NOT a walk of the register.
rows.what: Joannes Defranceschi, 1875–1875 — carried by the roster with no detail, and flagged by check-leads as having an unlinked lead
rows.got:
**Page 68, entry 10 of 1875**, **house 71**, *Anagr.* **II. 2**:

> «**Mortuus die 19 Sept., Sepult. 21 ejusdem, 1875**» · «**Joannes fil. Justinæ Defranceschi**» · «**dies 22**» · «**nat. 28/8 75**» · «**ordinaria**» · *D. G. Smak, parochus*

***Born 28 August 1875, dead 19 September, buried the 21st, aged twenty-two days*** — *and the arithmetic agrees with the register's own figure for once, which it did not for [the twins](/liznjan/).*

**⚠ THE ENTRY NAMES HIS MOTHER AND NO FATHER.** *Every other entry on the opening names both:* «filia Antonii et Antoniæ Fedel», «filia Joannis et Luciæ Perković nata Josephi Klunić», «filia Antonii et Annæ Fedel». ***That contrast is what the register says, and nothing beyond it is asserted.*** *This parish's death register carries no legitimacy column — the baptism register does — so the shape of the entry is the only evidence there is.*

**⚠ A SECOND JUSTINA.** *His mother is* **not** *[Magdalena Justina](/who/justina-defranceschi/), who was born in 1879, four years after this child died. Another Justina Defranceschi stood at Ližnjan in 1875 and this archive holds no record of her at all.*

**He is the third child of the name buried at Ližnjan in 1875.** *[The twins](/who/maria-defranceschi/) went together on 22 February; he followed in September. Three of the parish's Defranceschi children in one year.*

**And he clears a flagged lead.** *[The gate's new](/worklist/)* `check-leads` *had him as one of six people the roster already held with an unlinked lead* (`XQM3-118S`). *Linked, and read. The count falls* **6 → 5**.
rows.next: The second Justina Defranceschi — a mother at Ližnjan in 1875, in no file here — wants the baptism of this child on 28 August 1875, which would say what the burial does not.

rows.src: ⚠ FamilySearch — LIŽNJAN baptisms 1857: the Mattheus pair NOT settled, and a Defranceschi daughter with seven children found instead
rows.waypointNote: Volume fixed by ark containment, not by a year range that fitted.
rows.pages: Frame 32, book pages 68–69 (Annus 1857). BOTH pages read down the Parentes columns, every entry — about eighteen. ⚠ The Patrini and Infans columns were not transcribed, and frames 31 and 33 were not opened.
rows.what: Whether «Mattheus Defranceschi b. 1858» (tree) and «Mathæus Defranceschi b. 1857» (index) are one child
rows.got:
**⚠ WHAT WAS LOOKED FOR AND NOT FOUND — the exact terms, because [a nil that names no terms is an assertion about a list nobody kept](/method/).**

*The target was the* **Mattheus 1858 / Mathæus 1857 pair** — *the roster holds both, one from the tree and one from the index, and the register was to settle whether they are one child.*

*The index record that put a Defranceschi birth on this frame is* «**Matteo Defraceschi · Maria Primus**», 1857. **Both pages of the opening were read down the** `Parentes` **columns, every entry** — *page 68 and page 69, about eighteen entries.* ***No birth to a Defranceschi father and a Primus mother is on this opening.*** *The fathers on page 68 are Fedel, Giuseppe, Bucovich, Millasevich, Costip…, Bolsun, Carmin; on page 69, Voinich, Nascovich, Clinich, Mocorich, Baldessi, Legovich, Sebetich, Millosevich.*

**So the pair is NOT settled**, *and the 1857 Defranceschi birth is somewhere other than where the frame number put it — most likely the facing frames 31 or 33, which were not opened.*

**But the opening gave something it was not asked for.** *Page 69, second entry,* `Parentes`:

> *Pater* «**Antonio Nascovich fu Giovanni**» · *Mater* «**Maddalena Defranceschi fu Matteo**»

***A Defranceschi daughter married out, and a Matteo already dead by 1857.*** *She is* **not** *[the Maddalena this archive holds](/who/maddalena-defranceschi/), who died in 1849. [She is in the roster now](/who/maddalena-defranceschi-naskovic/).*

**⭐ And she had a household of seven.** *The harvested index carries* **seven** *Našković children to a* «Maddalena Defranceschi» *at Ližnjan — Euffemia 1852, Cattarina 1855, Cattarina 1856, Cattarina 1857, Antonius 1859, Joannes 1869, Josephus 1873 —* ***three daughters given the same name, which usually means the first two died***. **None of the seven is in this roster and none has been read.** *Leads, not people.*

**⚠ Her father is not asserted.** *The entry says* «fu Matteo». *This archive's* `register.json` *holds lead* `XQM3-21M6` — «**Mattio Francesch, b. 1799, d. 20 December 1839**» — *which fits, and which* **no roster row has ever taken up**. ***A date that fits is not a match***, *so it is named as a candidate and left there.*
rows.next: Frames 31 and 33 for the 1857 Defranceschi/Primus birth. And lead XQM3-21M6 — Mattio Francesch, d. 20 Dec 1839 — wants the 1839 burial page, which would test whether he is Maddalena's «fu Matteo».

rows.src: ⭐⭐⭐ FamilySearch — LIŽNJAN 1888 finished: the Josephus pair settled, the TREE beat the INDEX, and the anagrafe proves a household across a change of house
rows.waypointNote: Volume fixed by ark containment, not by a year range that fitted.
rows.pages: Frames 53 and 54, book pages 98–101 — the 1888 sequence read in order across entries 3–8 and 13–30. ⚠ Entries 1–2, 9–12 and 17–21 were NOT read, so 1888 is not walked; the Defranceschi entries in it are accounted for, the year is not.
rows.what: Josephus Defranceschi, d. 1888 — the pair the previous session opened and could not settle
rows.got:
**Page 99, entry 7 of 1888** — *and the scribe wrote the name in the left margin as well as in the column:*

> «**Josephus Defranceschi**» · «**Mort. — Martii, Sep. — ejusdem, 1888**» · **house 82** · **Anagr. p. 305, III. 9** · «**Josephus Defranceschi, Gregorii et Maria Vojnić**» · «**an. 1, mens. 11**» · «**nat. 15/4 86**»

**Born 15 April 1886, dead in March 1888 at a year and eleven months** — *the age and the birth agree with each other, and the day/month/year form of* «15/4 86» *is the one this book uses throughout* («nat. 2/5 851» *against an age of* «ann. 23, m. 8, d. 26»).

**⚠ THE DEATH DAY IS BLANK IN THE REGISTER ITSELF.** *The scribe wrote* «Mort. — Martii» *and* «Sep. — ejusdem» *and never filled the days in. That is the book's gap, not a failure of reading, and no day is invented here.*

**⚠⚠ TWO ROWS, ONE CHILD — and this time the TREE was right and the INDEX was wrong.** *This archive held* `josephus-defranceschi-1887` *from the index* («b. Mar 1887») *and* `josephus-defranceschi-1886` *from the family tree* («1886»). ***The register says 15 April 1886.*** **The tree had it; the index did not.** *That is the exact reverse of [the Mathæus duplicate settled the same week](/corrections/), where the index was right and the tree a year out — and it is a useful corrective to assuming an index outranks a tree.*

**⭐ And the anagrafe reference ties the household together ACROSS A MOVE.** *This entry cites* **Anagr. p. 305, III. 9**; *[Magdalena Justina's baptism](/who/justina-defranceschi/) cites* **p. 305, III. 7** — *same page, same family, different person number —* ***though she was entered at house 61 in 1879 and he at house 82 in 1888***. *The house number moves; the anagrafe family does not. [That makes the anagrafe the better key for this parish than the house number](/liznjan/).*

**The household of Gregorius Defranceschi and Maria Vojnić now stands at four children buried small:** *the twins Maria and Anastasia (20–22 February 1875), a Maria of 1878 still unread, Magdalena Justina (1879–1952, who lived), and this Josephus.*
rows.next: Two suspected pairs left at Ližnjan: Mattheus 1858/1857 and Antonio 1848/1846. And the anagrafe itself — p. 305 family III — has never been located.

rows.src: ⚠⚠ LIŽNJAN — a WIFE of the name found in the 1888 burials, and a count of how much this archive was already holding and had never taken up
rows.dest: Ližnjan «Liber Defunctorum», waypoint 9R2Z-4WG · and this archive's own register.json
rows.waypointNote: Volume fixed by ark containment, not by a year range that fitted.
rows.pages: Frames 53–56 scanned by the NOMEN DEFUNCTI column to place the years 1887–1889, then frame 54 (book pages 100–101) read at native resolution. ⚠ NOT a walk of the register; the 1888 sequence was not read end to end and the Ætas column of entry 23 was not reached.
rows.what: Josephus Defranceschi, d. 1888 — a suspected duplicate; and what else the 1888 burials hold
rows.got:
**The suspected Josephus pair was NOT settled** — *the 1888 sequence was not read to its end and he was not reached. [Said plainly rather than left to look like a nil](/method/).*

**But page 101, entry 23 gives a person of the name this archive did not hold at all:**

> «**Mort. 17 Augusti, Sep. 19 ejusdem, 1888**» — **house 75** — «**Fusca uxor Antonii Defranceschi nata Lazarić**»

***A wife of Antonius Defranceschi, born Lazarić***, *dead 17 August 1888 and buried on the 19th. [Now in the roster](/who/fusca-defranceschi-lazaric/) —* **with no birth year**, *because the index's* «1821» *can only come from an age at death that this session never reached.*

**⭐⭐ The pattern behind all of this week's Ližnjan work, now counted.**

*Three separate times in two days, a Ližnjan person turned out to be sitting in this archive's own* `register.json` *as an* ***indexed lead nobody ever took up***, *while the roster carried the tree's version of the same person — or nothing at all:*

1. **[Fusca, 1870](/who/tusca-defranceschi/)** — *both halves of her life held as two leads, parents identical, never joined; the roster took the tree and the wrong spelling.*
2. **[Mathæus, 1890–1891](/who/math-us-defranceschi/)** — *held from the burial index with the right year, and duplicated by the tree with the wrong one.*
3. **[Fusca née Lazarić, d. 1888](/who/fusca-defranceschi-lazaric/)** — *a* **wife of the name**, *held as lead* `XQM3-P992` *and* ***never in the roster in any form***.

**So the files were counted.** `register.json` *holds* **24** *leads placed at Ližnjan.* **15 of them are cited by no roster row at all.**

*Three of those fifteen are people documented from the page this week — Fusca 1870 and the twins Maria and Anastasia of 1875 — whose roster rows now cite the* ***register image*** *rather than the index lead, so the lead still reads as unused. That is a bookkeeping artefact and is said so here rather than counted as a gap.*

**The rest are genuinely untaken**, *and most are children of Defranceschi daughters who married out — Ruman, Perković, Jelčić, Našković — plus* «Mattio Franceschi, 1799 – 20 Dec 1839» *and* «Giovanni Defranceschi, 1845 – 11 Nov 1846», *who are of the name outright.*

**⚠ The lesson is not that the index is good.** *It is that* ***this archive kept finding things it already had***. *The register settles what the index garbles —* «Antonii Defranceschi Or Lazarić» *is a flattened parent list that the page resolves instantly into* «**uxor Antonii Defranceschi nata Lazarić**» — *but the lead was the thing that should have sent somebody to the page years ago.*
rows.next: The 1888 sequence still owes its end, and with it the Josephus 1886/1887 pair. Twelve genuinely untaken Ližnjan leads remain, most of them children of daughters who married out.

rows.src: ⚠⚠ FamilySearch — LIŽNJAN deaths 1891: a tree-only child turns out to be one this archive ALREADY HELD under another id, and three more pairs look the same
rows.waypointNote: Volume fixed by ark containment, not by a year range that fitted.
rows.pages: Frames 57–60 scanned at low resolution to place the years, then frame 58 (book page 108, 1891) read entry by entry at native resolution. ⚠ NOT a walk.
rows.what: Mattheus Defranceschi, b. 1891 d. 1891 on the family tree and nothing else
rows.got:
**Page 108, entry 7 of 1891, house 3:**

> «**mort. 18 Febr., sepul. 19 ejusdem, 1891**» — «**Mathæus Defranceschi, Mathæi et Annæ Skoko**» — *cathol., mascol.,* «**nat. 25/1 90**».

***Born 25 January 1890, dead 18 February 1891.*** **The tree said born 1891.**

**⚠ And this archive already held him** — *as* `math-us-defranceschi-1890`, *from the burial index, with the right year.* ***Two rows, one child.*** *[Ids are frozen](/method/), so both stand and the join is written on each; nothing was deleted.* [Recorded as a correction](/corrections/).

**⚠ And it is not one row. Comparing all thirteen remaining tree-only Ližnjan people against the register-sourced ones of the same name and neighbouring years turns up FOUR pairs that look like the same child entered twice** — *once from a document, once from the tree, a year or a spelling apart:*

| tree-only row | record-sourced row | |
|---|---|---|
| Mattheus b. **1891** d. 1891 | Mathæus b. **1890** d. 1891 | **✔ PROVED one child, 12 Oct** |
| Josephus b. **1886** d. 1888 | Josephus b. **1887** d. 1888 | *probable — unread* |
| Mattheus b. **1858** | Mathæus b. **1857** | *probable — unread* |
| Antonio b. **1848** | Antonio b. **1846** | *weaker — unread* |

**Only the first has been read on the page. The other three are recorded as SUSPECTED and nothing has been merged**, *because a year's difference between a tree and an index is exactly what a register exists to settle, and guessing would put the archive back where the tree left it.*

**House 3 is also [Fusca's house](/who/tusca-defranceschi/)**, *and her father was a Mathæus Defranceschi too — by Maria n. Primus, where this child's mother is Anna Skoko. Same man by a second wife, or his son of the same name: **not settled, and not asserted**.*
rows.next: Three suspected pairs to settle on the page — Josephus 1886/1887 (deaths 1888), Mattheus 1858/1857, Antonio 1848/1846.

rows.src: ⭐⭐⭐ FamilySearch — LIŽNJAN baptisms 1879: the Ližnjan baptism book carries DEATH MARGINS and ANAGRAFE page references, and one of them dates a 1952 death to the day
rows.waypointNote: Volume fixed by ark containment, not by a year range that fitted.
rows.pages: Frame 72, book pages 56–57 (1879, into 1880). The left page read entry by entry down the Infans and Genitores columns at native resolution. ⚠ NOT a walk of the register.
rows.what: Justina Defranceschi, carrying only «1879–1952» from the family tree
rows.got:
**Page 56, entry 22 of 1879, house 61**, *baptised by D. G. Smak, paroch.:*

> «**Magdalena Justina** — nat. 3. Octobr. curr., **hora circ. 3 pomer.**» — *of* «**Gregorius Defranceschi**», *fil. Gregorii q. Georgii et Agathæ, and* «**Maria Vojnić**», *n. Perkovič, agric.*

**Her name in the book is MAGDALENA JUSTINA**; *the tree gave only* «Justina». *Born 3 October 1879 at about three in the afternoon — the register gives the hour.*

**⭐⭐ AND THE MARGIN DATES HER DEATH**, *in Croatian, in a later hand beside the baptism:*

> «**Umrla u Ližnjanu dana 18. V. 1952** (mat. knj. umrlih str. 36 d. 2/52 Ližnjan.)»

***Died at Ližnjan 18 May 1952***, *with the death register's own* **page 36, entry 2/52** *cited. The tree's bare* «1952» *is now a date — and the reference points at a register this archive has not opened.*

**⭐ A SECOND STRUCTURAL FIND ON THE SAME PAGE: every entry carries an ANAGRAFE reference.** *A small column beside each date reads* «Anagr. p. 305 III.7», «p. 153 III.7», «p. 174 IV.3» — ***page and family number in a Status Animarum***. **Ližnjan's anagrafe therefore exists and the baptism register indexes it, entry by entry.** *That is a finding aid nobody here knew about.*

**⭐ She is the sister of the twins.** *Same parents, same house 61 as* [Maria](/who/maria-defranceschi/) *and* [Anastasia](/who/anastasia-defranceschi/), *who were born 20 February 1875 and died together on the 22nd.* **Gregorius Defranceschi and Maria Vojnić buried twin daughters four years before this one was born.**

**Four of the seventeen are now done.**
rows.next: The margin cites Ližnjan deaths page 36, entry 2/52 — a 1952 register, outside Deaths 1815–1900 and not among the three Ližnjan volumes on FamilySearch. And the anagrafe the baptisms index has not been located at all.

rows.src: ⭐⭐⭐ FamilySearch — LIŽNJAN deaths 1875: two more of the seventeen, and the register braces them together because they were TWINS
rows.waypointNote: Volume fixed by ark containment against the full ark list of every Ližnjan book, not by a year range that fitted.
rows.pages: Frame 37, book pages 66–67 — the 1874 tail and the opening of 1875 read in order to entry 6, at native resolution via Deep Zoom tiles. ⚠ NOT a walk of the register.
rows.what: Anastasia and Maria Defranceschi, both carrying only «1875–1875» from the family tree
rows.got:
**Entries 5 and 6 of 1875, and the scribe wrote them as ONE entry with a brace** — *the parents, the cause and the priest written once across both rows:*

> «**mortua die 22 Febr., sepulta die 23 ejusdem, 1875**» — **house 61** — «**Maria**» *and* «**Anastasia**», *of* «**Gregorii Defranceschi**» *and* «**Mariæ Vojnić**», ***agr.***

**Both rows carry the same two figures:** «**nat. 20/2 75**» *and* «**dies 3**». *Cause for both,* «**ordin.**».

***Born the same day, dead the same day, buried the same day, braced on the page — they were twins.*** *This archive held them as two unrelated children who happened to share a year, because the tree gave a year and nothing else.*

**⚠ The arithmetic is left as the register wrote it.** *Born the 20th and dead the 22nd is two days; the scribe put* «dies 3» *against each — counting inclusively, or counting to the burial. Recorded, not smoothed.*

**The date format was confirmed on the page rather than assumed:** *entry 4, two rows above, reads* «**nat. 2/5 851**» *against a man whose age is* «ann. 23, m. 8, d. 26» — *born 2 May 1851, which only parses as day/month/year.*

**Three of the seventeen are now done** — *[Fusca](/who/tusca-defranceschi/) on 1870, and these two.*
rows.next: Gregorius Defranceschi and Maria Vojnić of house 61 have more children in the index — Maria b. 1878 and Justina b. 1879, both in Births 1816–1883 — and Justina is herself one of the seventeen.

rows.src: ⭐⭐⭐ FamilySearch — LIŽNJAN baptisms and deaths 1870, read at the page: a tree-only child documented at BOTH ends of a six-month life, and her name corrected
rows.waypointNote: Volume confirmed by ARK CONTAINMENT, not by a date range that fitted: this archive's own image arks were matched against the full ark list of every Ližnjan book. Deaths are 9R2Z-4WG, frame 31.
rows.pages: Baptisms frame 51 (book page 15, Annus 1870) and deaths frame 31 (book page 54), both read in full at native resolution via Deep Zoom tiles. ⚠ NOT a walk of either register — two openings read, located from the index.
rows.what: Whether the seventeen Ližnjan people resting on the family tree and no document can be reached in the registers
rows.got:
**«Tusca Defranceschi, 1870–1870» was [one of seventeen Ližnjan people standing on the MyHeritage tree and nothing else](/liznjan/). She is now documented at both ends of her life — and she was never called Tusca.**

**BAPTISM**, *page 15, Annus 1870, first entry:* «**9ⁿᵃ Januarii 1870**», **house 3**, *baptised by D. Gregorius Smak, coop. par.:* «**Fusca, nata hodie**» — *catholic, female, legitimate — of* «**Matthæus Defranceschi**», ***agricola***, *and* «**Maria n. Primus**».

**BURIAL**, *page 54:* «**mortua 6. Julii, sepult. 8 ejusdem**», **house 3 — the same house** — «**Fusca filia Matthæi Defranceschi q. Matthæi et Mariæ n. Primus q. Paschalis**», *aged* «**6 mens.**», *of* «**debilitas**».

**Born 9 January, dead 6 July: five months and twenty-seven days.** *The age column says six months, and the two books agree with each other on house and parents without being asked — the corroboration this archive wants and rarely gets.*

**⚠ AND THE ARCHIVE WAS ALREADY HOLDING BOTH HALVES.** `register.json` *carried* `XQM3-PZYY` «Fusca · b. 9 Jan 1870» *and* `XQM3-GSVF` «Tusca · d. 6 Jul 1870», ***with identical parents***, *as two unjoined leads — while the roster took neither and copied the tree. [Recorded as a correction](/corrections/).*

**The name is FUSCA.** *[A hand is only legible against itself](/method/): the burial page's* ***own first entry***, *same hand, reads* «*e di* **Fosca**». *Fosca/Fusca is a name in use in this parish; Tusca is not a name.*

**Two grandfathers gained:** «*q. Matthæi*» *and* «*q. Paschalis*», *a Primus.*
rows.next: Fifty indexed Ližnjan records for the name are now harvested and tied to their books by ark. The remaining tree-only people — Antonio 1848, Justina 1879, Anastasia and Maria 1875, Paschalis (index says 1867, tree says 1863) — are located and unread.

rows.src: ⚠⚠ DAPA ZM34K-214 — the 1826 «Nrus. Domus» column: two pages a house-number pair cannot explain, and three Defranceschi house numbers
rows.film: DAPA ZM34K-214 — Gologorica Status Animarum 1826, the «Nrus. Domus» column of M01069315–M01069435
rows.waypointNote: No FamilySearch waypoint: DAPA microfilm, read from the family's own copy of the reel.
rows.pages: The «Nrus. Domus» cell and first name-line of each frame tiled six to a sheet across M01069315–M01069435, and read IN SAMPLE for the structure of the column. ⚠ Not the end-to-end harvest the item asks for; walked:false.
rows.what: **[Worklist 191](/worklist/) — one column across 119 pages, to build [the renumbering concordance row 171 has been assembling](/worklist/).** *[On 6 October this archive settled that both figures in the cell are house numbers and that the upper is the live one.](/worklist/)*
rows.got:
**⚠⚠ THE FIRST OF THOSE DOES NOT SURVIVE THE COLUMN.**

> *M01069349:* «**21**» *over a rule over* «**48**» · «Joannes Opassich haeres Runco»
> *M01069350:* «**23**» *over a rule over* «**48**» · «Joannes Rythno def. Josephi»

***The same lower figure under two different uppers, on two pages, against two households.*** **A house-number pair cannot do that** — *one old house is not two new ones unless it was split, and a split gives adjacent numbers, not 21 and 23 with a household between.*

*Three possibilities, and these frames cannot choose: one* «48» *is misread; the lower figure is not a house number but a page, section, conscription or* pagina *reference; or the renumbering was not one-to-one.* ⚠ ***The 6 October conclusion is not withdrawn — the confidence in it is***, *and [the concordance may not be built on it until this is settled](/worklist/).*

✔ *The third question stands: the* **upper figure is live**, *because the book is bound in its order.*

**✔ AND THE SAMPLE GIVES THREE HOUSE NUMBERS THIS ARCHIVE WANTED:** «**Franciscus Xaverius Defranceschi**» *with* «Clotilda n. Ortis» *at* **house 7**; «**Joannes Sestan**» *with* «**Sancta uxor**» *at* **house 9**; «**Leonardus Defranceschi**» *at* **house 34**. ➕ *Also read with their numbers: Crismanich 13, Marecich 14 and 17, Udovicich 19, Gasparich 25, Terdoslavich 8, Rabar-Santoteth 1, Palman 11, Rabar 15, and* «Domus Ecclesiae» *at 20/27.*

⚠⚠ ***THIS IS A SAMPLE, NOT THE HARVEST.*** *A real pass needs the* **row rules visible**: *without them a crop cannot tell a pair stacked inside one cell from two numbers in consecutive rows — which is exactly the ambiguity that produced the* «48» *problem in the first place.*
rows.next: *The end-to-end harvest, with a crop that includes the row rules. And one household whose two numbers are* ***independently*** *known, which is still what [the concordance needs](/worklist/) and which this sample did not supply.*
ev: The column, the anomaly, and the three house numbers

rows.src: ⭐⭐⭐ DAPA ZM34K-214 — the baptism book's MARGINS are a substitute for both registers these reels do not hold: deaths to 1954, and «Extr. za ženidbu» marriage certificates
rows.film: DAPA ZM34K-214 — Gologorica baptisms 1784–1880, the «Infans» column of M01069014–M01069181
rows.waypointNote: No FamilySearch waypoint: DAPA microfilm, read from the family's own copy of the reel.
rows.pages: The «Infans» column tiled six frames to a strip across M01069014–M01069181 and read in sample, to establish WHAT the margins contain rather than to transcribe them. ⚠ Not a harvest, and the row says walked:false for that reason.
rows.what: **[Worklist 176](/worklist/) — raised 5 October on death dates written into baptism entries by a later hand, and called** «*a death register hiding inside a baptism register*». *[Its first step was completed the same day](/worklist/) with no new death found.* ***The question here was what else the column holds.***
rows.got:
**⭐⭐ A SECOND KIND OF MARGIN, AND IT IS A MARRIAGE.** *M01069142, under a child baptised in the 1860s:* «***Extr. za ženidbu 14/11 89 br. 68***» — ***an extract issued for marriage, 14 November 1889, protocol number 68***. *The parish recorded in the baptism entry that it had issued the certificate that let the person marry.* **[The Gologorica marriage register on these reels stops in February 1788](/gologorica-line/#mariannaburial)**, *and every marriage date gathered this week came from a census column.* ⚠ *It dates the* **certificate**, *not the wedding.* ***The phrase appears nowhere else in this archive's data, in any spelling.***

**✔ AND THE DEATH MARGINS RUN TO 1954.** «† 27.VIII.1923» · «† 4/11 1919» · «† 10/12 99» · «† 20.XII.1917» · «† 20.8.1918» · «† 24/2 901» · «† 23.X.1913» · «† 10/VIII 1920» · «† 27/2 1935» · «† 21/12 1905» · «**† 23/IV/1954**». **[The death register ends 23 January 1880](/errands/).**

> ***So both books missing from these reels have a partial substitute written into the margins of the book that survives.***

✔ *And this archive has used it twice without noticing:* **[Franciscus Xaverius † 4 Jan 1893](/who/franciscus-xaverius-joseph-defranceschi/)** *and* **[Maximilianus † 6 Aug 1910](/who/maximilianus-antonius-defranceschi/)** *are both margin readings of deaths after the register ends.*

⚠⚠ **THIS IS NOT A HARVEST AND MUST NOT BE READ AS ONE.** *The annotations run into the hundreds across 168 frames, mostly for families this study does not follow; the* «Infans» *column gives a* **forename only**, *so each margin needs the* Genitores *column opposite to attribute it; and* ***a fixed crop will not do it*** *— the table shifts between gatherings, [a trap that has had to be caught three times today](/gologorica-line/#sa1894done).* **[The item is restated, not closed.](/worklist/)**
rows.next: *A proper pass, with the* «Infans» *and* Genitores *columns read together and the crop re-checked every few frames. It is a day's work and it would produce a parish death list for 1880–1954 and a set of datable marriages — [exactly the two things the letter to Pazin asks for](/errands/).*
ev: What the margins hold, and what they substitute for
The letter — the substitute argues for it, not against it

rows.src: ⭐⭐⭐ DAPA ZM34K-214 — «GRAH-ŽIPAN» confirmed in a clear hand: the second element is an OFFICE, and Marianna is «Grah-Missan»
rows.film: DAPA ZM34K-214 — Gologorica baptisms 1784–1880, the Mater and Patrini columns of M01069136–M01069153 (1861–1880)
rows.waypointNote: No FamilySearch waypoint: DAPA microfilm, read from the family's own copy of the reel.
rows.pages: COMPLETE. M01069136–M01069153 — the «Nomen et Cognomen Matris» and «Patrini» columns, 1861 to 1872 — read in full. ⚠ The column band had to be re-cut twice: this book shifts its table between gatherings, and a crop that held for eight frames was catching the wrong columns entirely by M01069144.
rows.what: **[The second element of the Grah compound could only be settled by the same name in another hand](/gologorica-line/#mariannaburial)** — *and [the earlier Patrini sweep stopped at M01069135](/searched/), leaving 1861–1880 unread for this surname.* ***That is exactly where both women were standing.***
rows.got:
**⭐⭐⭐ BOTH COMPOUNDS, ONE HAND, ONE PAGE.** *Page 126 (M01069140), Patrini, 1864:* **7 Maji** «Joannes Bubich» *and* «***Marianna n. GRAH-MISSAN***»; **22 Septembris** «Josephus Udovichich» *and* «***Rosa GRAH-ŽIPAN***». ***Three months apart, by one clerk.***

**✔ THE SECOND IS NOT «JOPAN».** *At eight times magnification it is a tall looped capital and then* **i-p-a-n**: «**ŽIPAN**», *the Croatian* **župan**, ***a village headman***. *[An hour earlier this archive raised that as a guess and said twice that nothing established it](/corrections/).* ***It is now a reading***, *and [it joins the* «Suppanus Joannes Grach» *already held at Gračišće](/direct-line/).* ⚠ *The form is certain; identifying this household with that one is not.*

**⚠⚠ AND THE ATTRIBUTION WAS MINE TO FIX.** *The register gives Marianna* ***twice*** — *as a* **mother** *(M01069137: «Joannes Bubich, agr.» · «Mariana Grah-Missan») and as a* **godmother** *(M01069140, same husband).* ***She is «Grah-Missan»***, *and [the 1862 reading of her as a* «-pan» *form is withdrawn](/corrections/).*

**✔ So the Grah women of Gologorica are THREE:** *Marianna and Rosalia, both* **Grah-Missan**, *and* «**Rosa Grah-Žipan**» — *new, and of the headman's house.*

➕ ⚠ *One more of my own statements withdrawn:* «she bore no child this archive has found» — ***she bore one***, *and that baptism is the only reason her maiden surname survives at all.*

---

**✔ THE STRETCH IS FINISHED: FIVE GRAH ENTRIES IN EIGHTEEN FRAMES**, *where [the whole rest of the book gave one](/searched/).* «**Mariana Grah-Missan**» *as a mother at M01069137 and again at M01069138 —* ***two children*** *— and as a godmother at M01069140; «**Rosa Grah-Žipan**» as a godmother on the same page; and at M01069151 «**Franciscus Bubić**, agla» with «***Rosalia nata grah-Missan***». ***So Rosalia is in the baptism register under her maiden name too***, *as a mother, with the husband [the 1862 census gives her](/gologorica-line/#twograhwives).* **Four attestations of** «Grah-Missan» **and one of** «Grah-Žipan»; *the two forms never blur.*

⚠ *No further Grah in the stretch.* ➕ ⚠ **And the typewritten 1920 act of the Commissariato Generale Civile lies across folio 142 here** — «la grafia originale del cognome … è *de Franceschi* … il suo proavo **Leonardo de Franceschi nato a Luincio dd. 23/6 1626**». ***This archive found and transcribed it on 5 October ([worklist 179](/worklist/)).*** *It is named here only to record that this pass re-met it;* ***nothing is claimed by it.***
rows.next: *Nothing on these frames. The identification of* «Grah-Žipan» *with [the Gračišće* «Suppanus Joannes Grach»*](/direct-line/) still needs [the marriage register that is not on these reels](/errands/).*
ev: Both compounds, and what the office means

rows.src: ⭐⭐⭐ DAPA ZM34K-214 — the Grah wife's BURIAL entry found, and the reels hold NO Gologorica marriage register after February 1788
rows.film: DAPA ZM34K-214 — Gologorica deaths 1784–1880 (M01069287, page 115); Cerovlje Status Animarum (M01068796, M01068797, M01068801)
rows.waypointNote: No FamilySearch waypoint: DAPA microfilm, read from the family's own copy of the reel.
rows.pages: M01069287 (deaths, pages 115–116, the year 1870) read in full and the entry magnified. Cerovlje Grah houses 18, 19 and 23 (M01068796, M01068797, M01068801) read.
rows.what: **[The second element of «Grah-?pan» can only be settled by the same name in another hand](/gologorica-line/#grahsecond).** *Two were reachable: the Cerovlje book, and Marianna's own death entry — she died 19 August 1870, inside the death register.* ***Both were checked.***
rows.got:
**✔ THE BURIAL ENTRY IS THERE.** *Page 115 (M01069287):* «**1870 Augusti 19ⁿᵃ** · *h.* **25** · ***Marianna Bubić, agla***, *munita SS. Sacramentis, et sepulta die 20. hujus* · **35** · *Hydropisia*» — **Blasius Zwölber, Parochus**. ***Thirty-five in August 1870 closes on her birth of 19 September 1834***, *and the register adds her cause, her house and her priest.*

**⚠ BUT IT GIVES HER HUSBAND'S SURNAME.** *She is* «Marianna **Bubić**». *[A married-in woman is filed under her husband in the death book exactly as in the household index](/gologorica-line/#twograhwives), so* ***the one register that might have named her father does not*** — *and the 6 October walk of this book would have passed her as a Bubić.* ✔ *The Cerovlje hand is no better: [its Grah of houses 18, 19 and 23 are plain* «Grah» *with no second element](/gologorica-line/#grahsecond).*

**⭐⭐⭐ AND THE SEARCH FOR HER MARRIAGE FOUND A GAP NOBODY HAD RECORDED.** *Her wedding of* **22 January 1861** *would name her father. [The frame map holds exactly one Gologorica marriage register](/parish-books/), inside the composite at M01068953–M01069007:* «Notatio Personarum Matrimonio junctarum a 1ᵐᵃ Julij **1770**», *running to* **February 1788**.

> ***There is no Gologorica marriage register after February 1788 on either reel.*** **A hundred and thirty years of marriages are off-film.**

⚠ *Not abstract: nearly every marriage date found this week came from a* **Matrimonii** *column in a census, never from a marriage entry.* ***A census gives the DATE; a marriage entry gives the PARENTS of both parties*** — *which is what this archive keeps running out of.* **[It is now the fourth request in the letter to Pazin.](/errands/)**
rows.next: ⚠ ***Answered within the hour, and this row's conclusion was wrong.*** *[She DID bear a child](/gologorica-line/#grahzipan): M01069137 enters her as a mother,* «**Mariana Grah-Missan**» — *so the baptism register carries the maiden name the burial register withheld, and it also [withdraws this archive's reading of her as a* «-pan» *form](/corrections/). What still needs [the marriage register off these reels](/errands/) is her father's forename, and whether the Gologorica* «Grah-Žipan» *is the Gračišće headman's house.*
ev: Her burial entry, and the marriage-register gap

rows.src: ⚠⚠ DAPA ZM34K-214 — two Grah follow-ups: «Grah-Jopan» WITHDRAWN to a question, and Cerovlje house 12 is an Opašić house
rows.film: DAPA ZM34K-214 — Gologorica Status Animarum 1862 (M01069464) and Cerovlje Status Animarum (M01068790–M01068791)
rows.waypointNote: No FamilySearch waypoint: DAPA microfilm, read from the family's own copy of the reel.
rows.pages: M01069464 re-read at nine times magnification for one word, against the same scribe's capital J in «Joannes» twice on the same page. M01068790 and M01068791 (Cerovlje houses 12 and 13) read in full.
rows.what: **Two leads opened by [the two Grah wives of the 1862 census](/gologorica-line/#twograhwives)** — *the new compound* «Grah-Jopan», *and Rosalia's stated origin* «e Cerovglie N.º 12». ***Both were followed, and both corrected what had been published rather than extending it.***
rows.got:
**⚠⚠ «GRAH-JOPAN» IS WITHDRAWN.** *It was read off a four-frame tile at page scale and never magnified. Re-read at* **nine times**, *against this scribe's own* **J** *in* «Joannes» *twice on the same page — which loops wide at the top left and descends with a leftward tail —* ***the letter after the hyphen has a straighter, taller ascender and does not match it***. *And the word* **runs off into the column rule**. *What the page securely gives is* «**Grah-**» *and a second element with a tall ascender.* **[Corrected.](/corrections/)**

**⭐⭐ AND WHAT OPENS IS BETTER THAN WHAT CLOSED.** *[This archive already holds* «**Mattia uxor *Suppani* Joannis Grach**» *at Gračišće](/direct-line/) — the wife of* **Suppanus** *Joannes Grach, the* ***village headman***, *a word itself recovered from a misreading.* ***If the second element reads* «Žopan» *the compound is not a second family but* «Grah the headman's house»***, *and it points at the Gračišće Grah who held the office.* ⚠ ***Nothing establishes it.*** *It is recorded because the letter is ambiguous and the office is attested for this surname one parish away — and because [the argument that made* «Grah-Mišan» *a two-family name rested on both halves being Slavic](/gologorica-line/#sa1921grah), which does not survive if the second half is a title.*

**✔ AND CEROVLJE HOUSE 12 IS AN OPAŠIĆ HOUSE.** *M01068790:* «**Opašić Thomas def. Antonii**», *n. 21 Dec 1846, with* «Margaritha n. Dujanić»; *his son* «**Opašić Benjamin**» *with* «Dominica n. Gržić». *House 13 likewise.* ***The lead closes.*** *[The earlier sentence — that the Gologorica census preserves a Cerovlje Grah household that Cerovlje's own book does not show — was stronger than it should have been](/corrections/): that book's households begin with men born in the 1840s, were drawn long after Rosalia left in 1869, and these parishes renumbered their houses.* ✔ ⚠ *The families do meet —* **[Opašić is one of the six surnames the Cerovlje Grah daughters married into](/gologorica-line/#cerovljegrah)** — *but that is a connection between families, not a claim about a house.*
rows.next: *The second element can only be settled by the same compound in another hand — the Gračišće or Cerovlje books, or [the registers still to come from Pazin](/errands/). The Cerovlje house numbering of the 1860s is not recoverable from the surviving book.*
ev: Both follow-ups, and what each corrected
The withdrawn reading, and the overstated sentence

rows.src: ⭐⭐⭐ DAPA ZM34K-214 — the 1894 Gologorica register SWEPT END TO END: three marriages the archive did not have, and a register of LAST RITES where the death book is missing
rows.film: DAPA ZM34K-214 — Gologorica Status Animarum 1894, register frames M01069580–M01069749 (the Repertorium at M01069750–M01069824 was read on 11 Oct and is not re-read here)
rows.waypointNote: No FamilySearch waypoint: DAPA microfilm, read from the family's own copy of the reel.
rows.pages: COMPLETE. The «NOMEN ET COGNOMEN» column of the LEFT page of each opening, M01069580–M01069740 — the register proper, to where the Repertorium begins. 161 frames, 43 tiles at four frames each. ⚠ The column band was re-cut mid-sweep: a fixed crop was clipping the first letters of surnames on some openings (M01069612 read as «ubić»), which for a surname sweep is fatal — every tile was regenerated wider and the already-read ones re-checked.
rows.what: **[This archive judged these the lowest-value frames on worklist 218 line 3](/gologorica-line/#sa1862done)** — *reasoning that the book's person-level Repertorium already sees married women, so the Grah nil was soundly bounded without a sweep.* ***That reasoning was right about the nil and wrong about the book.***
rows.got:
**⚠⚠ THE 1894 BOOK IS NOT A HOUSE LIST. IT IS A GENEALOGY.**

*Under each head it sets out* «**Filii**», «**Filiae**», «**Fratres**», «**Sorores**», «**Parentes**» *and — where the wife had married before —* «**Liberi … ex I/II thalamo**», *her children by each earlier husband.* ***Twenty-eight frames in it has already produced four things.***

**⭐⭐ HECTOR GETS HIS PARENTS.** *[Minted yesterday from a bare line in the 1862 name index](/gologorica-line/#sa1862done), his row had to say* «*a house and a year and nothing else: no parents, no day, no death*». *M01069590:* «**Defranceschi Antonius, III vir Rosae n. Salamon**» · *Filii:* Ferdinandus Romanus · Aloysius Joannes · «**Hector**». ***Son of [Antonius and Ruža née Salamon](/gologorica-line/#rosasalamon), by her third marriage.*** ➕ *And* «**Ida-Rosa**» *is a further daughter, new.*

**⭐⭐ A HUSBAND NAMED.** *[The 1862 book gave Beatrix Hermenegildis a husband truncated to* «za Ang. Val.»*, published as* «a lead, not an identification»](/gologorica-line/#house4_1862).* *M01069585:* «***Clotilda, Maria, filia Valentini MARCOLINI e Beatricis n. Defranceschi***», *n.* **15 Januar 1894**. ***Husband and daughter both new.*** ⚠ *The* «Ang.» *is still unexplained and is left standing.*

**✔ LEONARDUS'S TWO FAMILIES SORTED.** *[The 1862 book gave two sons by his second marriage](/gologorica-line/#leonardus2wives); this gives* **five** *— Leopoldus Antonius, Petrus, Romanus, Victor, Aemilius Ernestus — and assigns every loose* `golo` *row to a marriage.*

**⚠⚠ AND IT CAUGHT A DUPLICATE OF MINE.** *[Yesterday I minted* «Maria Aloysia Defranceschi», *b. 12 Sept 1880](/corrections/).* ***This archive already had her***: «Maria **Luigia** Defranceschi», *b. 1880, d. 1909,* «Gračišće, Istria», *a MyHeritage row with an empty note.* **I did not check before minting.** ✔ *The two sources corroborate each other — the register has her* «nata a Gollignana» *and the tree places her at Gračišće, neither knowing of the other* — *and* «Luigia» *is simply the Italian of* «Aloysia». ***Both ids kept and frozen, the join written on both rows.***

**No Grah in the frames read so far.**

---

**✔✔ SWEPT END TO END, AND THESE WERE SUPPOSED TO BE THE LOWEST-VALUE FRAMES ON THE LINE.** *They have produced more joins than any other book on either reel.*

**⭐⭐ THREE MARRIAGES, NONE OF THEM ON THE ROSTER.** **[Aloysius Arturus](/who/aloysius-arturius-defranceschi/)** *× «**Albina n. Lovrinović**» (M01069671), with daughters* **Norina** *and* **Elda-Maria** — ***which closes [yesterday's inference](/gologorica-line/#golo87) that the* «Aloysius» *whose daughters are entered* «fil. Aloysii» *is this man***; **[Lambertina Lina](/who/lambertina-lina-defranceschi/)** *× «**Celentich Josephus**», ***ludimagister*** (M01069687), with* **Gemma Maria** *and* **Alice Clotildis Carolina**; *and* **[Estella Ida](/who/estella-ida-defranceschi/)** *× «**Sečešić Andreas**» (M01069735), with four children.* ➕ *A fourth,* «Defranceschi Ferdinandus» *× «Catharina n. Gašparić», is a* ***join rather than a find*** — *both were already on the roster and nothing said they were married.*

**⭐⭐⭐ AND THE BOOK CARRIES AN «EXTREMA UNCTIO» REGISTER.** *M01069740, ruled:* Nrus domus · NOMEN ET COGNOMEN · Pagus · ***Nativitatis*** · «***EXTREMA UNCTIO***» · Confessus · Communicans. *Last rites by year —* **1907** *(eleven),* **1908** *(ten),* **1909** *(two) — each with a house, a hamlet and a* ***full date of birth***. ***[The death register ends 23 January 1880 and Vol. IV is on neither reel](/errands/); extreme unction is given at the point of death, so this is the nearest death-adjacent source the archive has for those years.*** ⚠ **No Defranceschi is in it** — *the twenty-three are Rabar, Androšić, Ivić, Opašić, Stojšić, Sestan, Udovičić, Križmanić, Gržan, Želesko, Ančić, Bubić, Marčić, Runko, Savetić.* ***The instrument is the finding, not the content.***

✔ **Two documents turn out not to be one-offs.** *[The* «Senes» *list of 1909](/gologorica-line/#threecensuses) is a* ***series*** — «Annus 1899» *onward, each dated to the preceding 31 December, with Maximilianus in every one and Aloysius from 1903.* ***A name's disappearance from an annual list of the aged dates a death.*** *And a numbered* **succession of the parish's incumbents** *(M01069737–39), thirty-one names, of whom* ***number 11 is*** «**Defranceschi Mathias Joan.**», ***parochus***.

**✔ THE GRAH NIL HOLDS**, *and [Rosalia née Grah-Missan](/gologorica-line/#twograhwives) is in the book at M01069612 with* **four children** *where [the 1862 book gave one](/gologorica-line/#twograhwives). ⚠ *Near-misses set aside:* «Gržan», «Gržić», «Gržević», «Gržetić», «Graber», «Gašparić», «Grbavac», «Crosgnach».
rows.next: *Nothing. [Worklist 218 line 3 is finished](/worklist/) — all four* status animarum *and the baptism book's Patrini and Mater columns are swept. What remains for the Grah is [off these reels](/errands/).*
ev: The 1894 book as a genealogy, and what it corrected
The finished sweep, the three marriages, and the unction register

rows.src: ⭐⭐⭐ DAPA ZM34K-214 — the 1862 Gologorica register SWEPT END TO END: two Grah wives the index cannot see, two household BYNAMES, and a marriage this archive carried as a death
rows.film: DAPA ZM34K-214 — Gologorica Status Animarum 1862, M01069436–M01069579 (144 frames)
rows.waypointNote: No FamilySearch waypoint: DAPA microfilm, read from the family's own copy of the reel.
rows.pages: COMPLETE. All 144 frames, M01069436–M01069579, to the film's «KRAJ» target. The «NOMEN ET COGNOMEN» column of BOTH pages of each opening — this book carries a complete table on each page, unlike the 1826, 1894 and 1921 books — rendered as a dedicated column crop, three frames to a tile, 48 tiles. Includes the reel-214 recap and the 214/215 join, the book's genealogical recap at M01069550–551, its later name index, and the loose «Ordo alfabeticus familiarum» slip.
rows.what: **[Worklist 218 line 3](/worklist/) — the 144 register frames the 1862 index slip cannot speak for.** *[The slip indexes* **families***](/gologorica-line/#threecensuses), *so a Grah* ***wife*** *is outside it, and [the 1826 census found exactly that — a* «Marianna Grah» *entered as a wife](/gologorica-line/#sa1826grah). The register itself had to be read.*
rows.got:
**⭐⭐⭐ THE SWEEP PAID: TWO GRAH *WIVES* IN ONE OPENING (M01069464), IN TWO BUBIĆ HOUSEHOLDS FACING EACH OTHER.**

> «**Franciscus Bubić**», *rusticus, n. 31 Julii 1842, m. 18 Junii 1869, ob. 7 April 1908* · «***Rosalia ux. n. GRAH-MISSAN***», *n.* **13 Maji 1845** · *Adnotatio* «***e Cerovglie N.º 12***»
> «**Joannes fil. Joannis et Dominicae**», *n. 14 Maji 1833, ob. 15 Febr. 1909* · «***Marianna ux. n. GRAH-JOPAN***», *n.* **19 Sept. 1834**, *m.* **22 Jann. 1861**, *ob.* **19 Agost. 1870**

***This is precisely the class of person the book's own index slip cannot reach***, *and the reason the 144 frames had to be read.*

**⭐⭐ «GRAH-JOPAN» is a compound this archive had never met** — *a second second-element beside* «Grah-Mišan», *so a search for the one misses the other.*

**⭐⭐⭐ And Rosalia is [the 1894 Repertorium's* «Grah - Missan Rosalia, house 29, 1845»*](/gologorica-line/#threecensuses)**, *which gave a name, a house and a year and nothing else. She now has a birth to the day, a husband, a wedding, a son — and an origin:* ***Cerovlje, house 12***.

⚠⚠ **House 12 is NOT in the Cerovlje book.** *[That sweep found the Grah at 18, 19, 23, 38 and 53](/gologorica-line/#cerovljegrah) and married its daughters into Držetić, Dujanić, Šepuka, Opašić, Krošnjak and Lušetić —* ***not Bubić***. *No contradiction: those households run from a man born 1837 to children of the 1960s, and Rosalia left in 1869 before they were drawn.* ***So the Gologorica census preserves a Cerovlje Grah household that Cerovlje's own surviving book does not show, and names the surname it married into.***

> **Method.** *A woman who leaves a parish vanishes from its* status animarum *and appears in her husband's.* ***For a married-in surname the receiving parish is where you find her, and it is the receiving parish that records where she came from.***

---

**⚠⚠ FIRST, A SHORTCUT THAT WOULD HAVE PRODUCED A FALSE NIL.** *Much of this book is blank — the film even carries a* «**BLANK PAGES · NEISPISANE STRANICE**» *target. An ink-density pass over all 144 frames was written to find the written ones and skip the rest; it put* **M01069560 in the «blank» band**. *That frame carries about twenty-five names, [including* «**Defranceschi Henricus**»*](/who/henricus-jacobus-defranceschi/).* ***A sparsely written page scores the same as an empty one, because the printed rules dominate the measurement.*** **The threshold was abandoned and every frame is being read.**

**⭐⭐⭐ AND FOUR FRAMES IN, HOUSE 4 IS THE WHOLE OF CARLO'S BROTHER'S HOUSEHOLD.**

> «**Franciscus Defranceschi**, *filius Josephi et Lambertinae*» · «**possidens**» · *n.* **17 Feb 1816** · *m.* **10 Octob. 1859** · *d.* **4 Jan 1893**
> «**Clotilda uxor n. Ortis**» · *n.* **12 Octob. 1834** · «e Novatico»
> *and* ***fourteen children***, *grouped by sex rather than birth order*

⚠ ***Most of it is verification and this row says so***: *thirteen of the fourteen are already on the roster, most read out of the baptism register this month.* **[The* «gemini» *brace over the twins is corroboration, not discovery — the baptism book already had them, and better, with* «prius nata»*.](/who/maria-henrica-defranceschi/)**

**⭐⭐⭐ WHAT IS NEW: THE YEAR LINA'S BAPTISM WITHHELD.** *[Her row carried an explicit refusal](/who/lambertina-lina-defranceschi/) — the baptism gives* «die 23. Februarii nata» *with* ***no year***, *and the archive declined to choose between a contextual* **1876** *and the tree's* **1875**. *The census gives* «**Lambertina, Lina · 23. Febr. 1876**», *and at seven times magnification against the same clerk's* «1872» *and* «1868» *two rows below the final digit is the closed bowl of a* **6**. **[Corrected.](/corrections/)**

**⭐⭐ AND TWO MARRIAGES NEITHER DAUGHTER'S ROW HAD:** **Beatrix Hermenegildis**, *m.* **26 Nov 1887**, «***za Ang. Val.***»; **Clotildis Adelaidis**, *m.* **11 Oct 1890**, «***za Rud. Star.***». ⚠ *Both husbands' names are* ***truncated by the column*** *— leads, not identifications.*

✔ ***And the* Adnotatio *column tracks daughters OUT of the parish***, *in Croatian in a Latin book:* «**Kersanum**», «u **Š. Ivan**», «u **Šterni**», «u **Keršanu**». ***That makes this census a finding aid for exactly the class of person its own index slip cannot see.***

➕ *Also: the infant Victor Josephus carries* «**vixit 4 a. 4 m. 20 d.**», *and [Franciscus Xaverius — who had no note at all — gets his first document](/who/franciscus-xaverius-joseph-defranceschi/).*

**No Grah in the frames read so far.**

---

**⭐⭐ AND TWO FRAMES ON, LEONARDUS THE WEAVER MARRIED TWICE.** *M01069447:* «Maria **n. Flegar**» *d.* **28 Sept 1882**; «**Maria Udovičić · II. uxor**» *m.* **3 April 1883**; «**Antonius Leopoldus filius · ex II. votis**» *n.* **29 Jan 1884**; *and* «Rosa filia» *born and dead on* **1 April 1886**. ***This archive held all four people and none of the joins*** — *[Maria Udovičić](/who/maria-udovicic-defranceschi/) and [Antonius Leopoldus](/who/antonius-leopoldus-defranceschi/) each sat on the roster with an* ***empty note***, *and the phrase* «ex II. votis» *appears nowhere else in this archive's data.* **[Told here.](/gologorica-line/#leonardus2wives)**

✔✔ **AND THE STRUCTURE THAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED IS NOW READ.** *M01069446 carries three consecutive Defranceschi households in which a* «Rosa … n. Salamon» *appears each time, the husbands labelled* «**I. vir**», «**II. vir**», «**III. vir**». ***Read at magnification, the clerk says it himself***: «**Defranceschi Antonius** … ***Antonii, III. vir Rosae n. Salamon***», *and her own* Matrimonii *cell carries three numbered dates —* **I. 18 Febr. 1878 · II. 5 Febr. 1883 · III. 26 Oct. 1887** *— matching the marriages of three brothers on the facing page.* **[Ruža née Salamon (1854–1898) married Joannes Baptista, then Franciscus, then Antonius](/gologorica-line/#rosasalamon)**, *widowed twice before thirty-four.* ***She was not on this roster under any spelling***, *and two of her children sat on it as MyHeritage rows with empty notes and no parents.*

**⭐⭐⭐ AND THE SAME OPENING STATES THE FAMILY'S ORIGIN.** *The father,* «**Defranceschi Antonius**» *(1814–1893), carries* «***Ex Italia (Carnia)***» *in his* Adnotatio, *and his wife* «**Francisca ux. n. Defranceschi**» *carries* «***Gallignanensis***». ***This archive has argued the Carnian origin from surname geography and from Carlo's own writing; here a parish clerk writes it as a fact about a named man.*** ⚠ *One* Adnotatio, *one household, no town named.*

➕ *Also: their daughter* **Theresia** *(1843–1882) is entered* «***sordo-muta***» — *the only disability this archive has found recorded in these books; their daughter* **Maria** *is followed* «ad Lindarum N.º 13»; *and the book* ***cross-references its own pages*** *(«pag. 15», «pag. 16», «ad pag. 27», «ex p. 14», «vide infra»), so a reader can walk a family across the volume. That is a finding aid nobody had noted.*

---

**⭐⭐ AND THE REEL LISTS ITS OWN CONTENTS ON THE WAY OUT.** *Between* **M01069490 and M01069498** *reel 214 repeats every title card it has carried:* **3.3** *(births 1770–1781, deaths and marriages 1770–1789),* **5.1** *(deaths 1646–1806),* **5.2** *(deaths 1784–1880),* **7.1** *(Status Animarum 1826),* **7.2** *(Status Animarum 1862). Then* «**KRAJ**» *at M01069499.* **[Told here.](/gologorica-line/#reelrecap)**

⚠ **It also corrects [the film map](/direct-line/)**, *which said the 1862 tail* «carries no title card of its own». ***Reel 215 restates it at M01069503.*** *The boundary was right; the reason given for it was not.* **[Corrected.](/corrections/)**

⭐ **The card for signatura 5.2 advertises an index** — «***NA KRAJU KNJIGE NALAZI SE KAZALO IMENA***» — *which is [the index this archive established this morning stops at page 71 of a book written to page 135](/gologorica-line/#deathsindexstops).* ***The catalogue promises it and does not qualify it.***

➕ **And the film names its own making:** «SNIMLJENO U SREDIŠNJEM FOTOLABORATORIJU **HRVATSKOG DRŽAVNOG ARHIVA U ZAGREBU**, Kamera br. 1, Snimatelj: **Vrban Božidar**, 21.10.04». ***The books are held at Pazin; the filming was done in Zagreb on 21 October 2004.***

---

**✔✔ THE BOOK IS FINISHED — and the nil holds.** *Across all 144 frames the forms looked for were* **Grah · Grach · Gracco · Grah-Mišan · Grah-Jopan**. ***The two wives at M01069464 are the only bearers of the name in the book***, *and both are invisible to its family index.* ⚠ *Near-misses set aside, all present here:* «**Gržan**», «**Gržić**», «**Gržetić**», «**Gržević**», «**Graber**», «**Gašparić**», «**Crosgnach/Grosgnach**», «**Grbavac**».

**⭐⭐ TWO HOUSEHOLD BYNAMES.** *Above the heading of* «Defranceschi Antonius» *(M01069446) — the couple marked* «Ex Italia (Carnia)» *and* «Gallignanensis» — *a byname written diagonally across the rule:* «***Osvaldo***». *And on the index slip (M01069577), beneath* «Defranceschi-Carmel Ant. et Franca», *a second:* «***Defranceschi-Tito***». ***Both are new to this archive.***

**⚠⚠ AND A CORRECTION OF MINE THAT WAS WITHDRAWN BEFORE PUBLICATION.** *At seven times magnification the slip's* «Carmel» *carries a* ***dot above its minims***, *which would make it* «**Carniel**» — *the Carnian — on the very couple the register marks* «Ex Italia (Carnia)». *It was drafted as a correction to this archive's transcription.* ***It is withdrawn and the original reading stands***: *the bynames around it,* «Osvaldo» *and* «Tito», *are* **personal names**, *which is how an Istrian household byname is ordinarily formed — Carmelo belongs to that set and Carniel does not.* **[Told here.](/gologorica-line/#sa1862done)** ⚠ *The dot is recorded rather than explained away.*

**⭐⭐⭐ AND THE PHANTOM DEATH DATE IS A WEDDING.** *[Earlier today this archive withdrew* «died 25 November 1870» *from Aloysius Defranceschi as unexplained](/corrections/) — no burial entry had ever been found for it. M01069542 gives* «**25. Nov. 1870**» *in the* ***Matrimonii contracti*** *column, braced across* «Aloysius Defranceschi, mercator» *and* «Joanna n. Udovičić». ***The tree recorded his wedding day as the day he died.*** *[Filed.](/corrections/)*

**⭐⭐ The book keeps its own genealogy** *(M01069550–551), setting out each man's children, siblings, and his wife's children by each previous husband under* «Liberi … ex I/II thalamo». ***It corroborates both of today's households in the clerk's own structure*** — *[Ruža's three marriages](/gologorica-line/#rosasalamon), [Leonardus's two](/gologorica-line/#leonardus2wives) — and adds* **Leonardus's first marriage date, 20 February 1871**, *and the marriages of his sisters Maria (11 Feb 1873) and Rosa (28 Feb 1876).*

⚠ *It also corrected a reading of mine from this morning:* «Maria **Luizia**» *is* «**Maria-Aloysia**». *[Mine, and filed as such.](/corrections/)*

➕ *And one name is new outright:* «**Hector Ruggierus Defranceschi**», *house* **7**, *born* **1896** *(M01069555).*
rows.next: *Nothing on this book. [What is left of worklist 218 line 3](/worklist/) is the* ***register frames of the 1894 census*** *(246), where the person-level Repertorium was used instead of a sweep — and that index, unlike the 1862 slip, does see married women under their own surnames, so its Grah nil is already soundly bounded. These are the lowest-value frames remaining on the line.*

rows.src: ⭐⭐⭐ DAPA ZM34K-214 — the Gologorica baptism book's PATRINI and MATER columns SWEPT: one Grah in 99 frames, and the register puts her EX GALLIGNANA
rows.film: DAPA ZM34K-214 — Gologorica baptisms 1784–1880 («IV. Liber Baptisatorum»), M01069008–M01069181
rows.waypointNote: No FamilySearch waypoint: DAPA microfilm, read from the family's own copy of the reel.
rows.pages: COMPLETE. The «Nomen et Cognomen PARENTUM» (father and mother) and «Nomen et Cognomen PATRINORUM» columns of M01069037–M01069135 — all 99 frames of the target range, 1799 to 1860 — rendered as a dedicated column crop at near full resolution, two frames to a tile, 50 tiles. The column band was re-cut mid-range because the table shifts between gatherings and the book changes format about 1829; the re-cut was checked frame by frame, not assumed.
rows.what: **[Worklist 218 line 3](/worklist/) — the columns no index can reach.** *[The baptism book itself was walked end to end on 5 October](/searched/) and [its index read on 10 October](/gologorica-line/#mkrindex), but both were* ***Defranceschi*** *passes: the index files a married woman under her husband, and the walk named* «Grah» *in its scope for the opening folios and the last twenty only. The middle of the book — roughly folios 25 to 121 — had never been read with this surname in view.*
rows.got:
**✔✔ SWEPT END TO END. EXACTLY ONE GRAH IN NINETY-NINE FRAMES.**

**⭐⭐⭐ AND THE CONDITIO IS THE FINDING.**

> *25 January 1805, house 70 (M01069047), at the baptism of* «Dominica Selesco ex Doll.»:
> «**Joseph: Baddetich fil: q. Johan**» · *conditio* «**gollogʒ.**»
> «***Theresia grach Defranceschi uxor Joh: Baptistæ***» · *conditio* «***ex galligʒ.***»

***This is [Theresia née Grah](/person/theresia-defranceschi-nee-grach-gologorica/), the one Grah who married the direct line*** — *[married 9 June 1774 as* «filia Antonij Grah **ex Parochia Cherbune**»*](/gologorica-line/#marriage1774).* **It is her sixth recorded godmother appearance and eighteen years later than any other**, *and [the frame had never been cited](/searched/).*

**⚠⚠ In 1784 the register called the couple** «***ambo ex hac Parochia***». **In 1805 it calls her** «***ex Gallignana***» — ***Gračišće***.

*The reading was tested as this archive requires: the two place-words stand* ***one above the other in a single cell, one hand, one magnification*** — **g-o-llo-g** *against* **g-a-lli-g** — *and neighbouring openings write it unabbreviated,* «ambo **Gallignanenses**», «ex **gallignana**», «ex **Gallignana**» *(M01069050, M01069063).*

⚠ ***What it is not.*** *One* Conditio Patrinorum *tag does not move a person's residence, and nothing else in this archive places her at Gallignana. It is published because it is the first thread running the right way between [the Gologorica casa 31 household](/gologorica-line/) and [the second Defranceschi population at Gračišće, houses 4 and 5](/worklist/) — and the thread is the Grah.*

➕ *Also out of these frames: Defranceschi godparents on almost every opening —* «Batta Defranceschi», «Catharina Defranceschi ejusdem filia», «**Mathia uxor Leonardi Defranceschi**» *(repeatedly, and always* «hujates» *or* «ex hoc loco»*),* «Maria Rosalia Defranceschi»; *and two baptisms of* «**Dnus Josephus De Franceschi**» *and* «**Domina Lambertina ejusdem uxor nata Pesle**» — **Carlo's parents** — *one with* «**Eugenia Peschle Voloscensis, Dni Mathiæ filia**» *standing godmother (M01069058).*

⚠ *A near-miss worth recording for anyone sweeping this surname:* «**Joannes Grob Cherbunensis**» *(M01069054). Grob, not Grah.*

---

**✔ THE NIL, AND THE EXACT TERMS IT COVERS.** *Across all 99 frames the forms looked for were* **Grah · Grach · Gracco · Grah-Mišan** *in the father, mother and godparent columns.* ***[The 25 January 1805 entry is the only one.](/gologorica-line/#theresia1805)***

⚠ ***The forms that are NOT Grah and would trap a careless sweep*** — *all of them present in these frames, repeatedly:* «**Crosgnach**» *(a common Gologorica surname, on many openings; also written* «Crosgnach», «Grosgnach»*),* «**Grob**» *(Joannes Grob Cherbunensis, M01069054),* «**Hrabar**» *(Joannis Maria Hrabar Novacensis, M01069074),* «**Gherson/Ghersan**», «**Gasparich**», «**Graber**». ***A nil for this surname is worth nothing unless it says which near-misses were set aside, and these are they.***

**⭐⭐ AND THE DECREE ANNOTATIONS ARE IN THIS BOOK TOO, not only the census.** *Above the first entry of M01069131, over* «Antonius Opassich»: «**= Opassi: D.P. 15/VI-30 N.º 142**» — *Decreto Prefettizio, 15 June 1930, number 142.* ***[That extends the decree finding from the status animarum to a second register series](/gologorica-line/#sa1921grah)***, *and it means a surname search of the baptism book for the 1920s–30s must read the space above the line as well.*

➕ *The sweep also put eyes on every* **Defranceschi godparent** *in sixty years of the book — and they are on nearly every opening:* «Batta Defranceschi», «Catharina Defranceschi ejusdem filia», «Maria Rosalia Defranceschi», «Pietr'Ant. Defranceschi», «Josephus Defranceschi textor», «Maximilianus Defranceschi», *and above all* «**Mathea/Matthea uxor Leonardi Defranceschi**», *who stands repeatedly from the 1790s to the 1820s and is* ***always*** *entered* «hujas», «hujates» *or* «ex hoc loco». ⚠ ***That is the contrast that gives the Theresia entry its force***: *this clerk and his predecessors marked the Defranceschi of this parish as local, every time, and marked Theresia as of Gallignana.*
rows.next: *The baptism book is now swept for this surname across its whole span: [the opening folios and the last twenty had Grah in scope on 1 and 5 October](/searched/), and the middle — folios 25 to 121 — is done here.* **What is left of [worklist 218 line 3](/worklist/) is the *register frames* of the 1862 and 1894 censuses, where the indexes were used instead of a sweep.*
ev: Theresia at Gallignana, and what the Conditio does and does not prove
Her row, with all her appearances

rows.src: ⚠⚠ DAPA ZM34K-214 — the Gologorica DEATHS index STOPS AT PAGE 71 (about 1830) while the register runs to page 135 (1880)

rows.waypointNote: No FamilySearch waypoint: DAPA microfilm, read from the family's own copy of the reel.
rows.pages: M01069301 (letter D, both halves — the right half is the blank «E» page) and M01069306 (letter R), read at magnification for the PAGE-NUMBER column rather than the names.
rows.what: **Checking a nil before leaning on it.** *[Today's withdrawal of Aloysius Defranceschi's 1870 death year](/corrections/) said this register holds no such entry. Before letting that stand, the question was which source the statement actually rests on — the [end-to-end walk of 6 October](/searched/) or the book's own index.*
rows.got:
**⚠⚠ THE INDEX IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR THE BOOK, AND NOBODY HAD WRITTEN DOWN WHY.**

*The index was read on 6 October and gave this archive a lot — [forty-eight households mapped to house numbers](/gologorica-line/), the* «Extranei» *column, the* «alias» *bynames.* ***What was never recorded is where its page references stop.***

*Checked block by block today:* **not one page number anywhere in the index passes 71.**

| block | pages cited |
|---|---|
| «**Defranceschi Joseph · N. 17**» | 3, 5, 8, 11, 12, 12, 15, 25, 30, 39, 58, 62, 66, **67** |
| «**Defranceschi Joanes Bapta defti Leonardi · N. 12**» | 3, 8 |
| «**Defranceschi Leonardus · N. 10**» | 21 |
| «**Deprato Leonardus · N. 6**» | 1, 1, 9, 20, 24, 32, 39, **50** |
| «**Rabar Baron … N. 84**» | 18, 44, 47, 51, **52** |
| «**Rabar Sghemen · N. 72**» | 5, 9, 10, 35, 36, 37, **51** |
| «**Rabar alias Tomelincich · N. 31**» | 3, 5, 8, 17, 17, **18** |
| «**Rabar Tulla · N. 102**» | 7, **71** |

***The register is written to page 135.*** **Page 67 is 1826–27; page 135 is 23 January 1880.** *The index covers the first forty-odd years of a ninety-six-year book and was* ***abandoned around 1830***.

> ⚠ **A nil taken from this index is a nil to about 1830 and no further.**

**✔ AND IT IS WHY THE WALK MATTERED.** *The two death years this archive corrected by decades on 6 October are* ***both outside the index***: **Clementina, page 114** *(10 March 1870)* *and* **Josephus Lambertus, page 132** *(22 December 1878).* ***Neither could ever have been reached through the index.***

⚠ *So today's Aloysius nil is restated to rest on the* **walk**, *which read every entry, and not on the index's silence. [The correction now says so.](/corrections/)*

➕ *Contrast [the baptism book's index](/gologorica-line/#mkrindex), which is complete and handed over twelve siblings with page numbers. Two indexes in two books of one parish; only one can be trusted to the end.*
rows.next: *The index's* **S–Z** *was read on 6 October; nothing here changes that. What this bound does change is any future nil: for anything after about 1830 in this parish's deaths, the index cannot be cited — the walk must be.*
ev: Where the deaths index stops, and why the walk mattered
The Aloysius nil, restated on the walk

rows.src: ⭐⭐⭐ DAPA ZM34K-214 — the 1921 Gologorica Status Animarum swept END TO END: a clean nil for the Grah, and the register CITES THE DECREES that renamed the parish
rows.film: DAPA ZM34K-214 — Gologorica Status Animarum 1921, M01069826–M01069942 (117 frames)
rows.waypointNote: No FamilySearch waypoint: DAPA microfilm, read from the family's own copy of the reel. ⚠ Filing note: the two local folders split at M01069501, NOT at the reel boundary, so frames the frame map assigns to reel 214 sit in the folder named ZM34K-215.
rows.pages: All 117 frames read: M01069826–M01069942, to the «END» target and the next parish's title page. 95 numbered houses across some 25 hamlets — Gologorica, Piljani, Juratići, Šidreli, Posinci, Strapci, Trdoslavići, Zovići, Gospodi, Jakolići, Rićmanjica, Baroni, Lukačići, Šepeci, Kamenik, Radetići, Gržani, Kočebari, Želeski, Šepčići, Zgemenišće-Hanaja.
rows.what: [Worklist 218, line 3](/worklist/) — the last of the four *status animarum*, and the only one with no finding aid. **[24 of its 117 frames had been read; the other 93 had not.](/searched/)**
rows.got:
**✔ EVERY FRAME OF THIS BOOK WAS OPENED AND READ** — *all* **117**, *M01069826 to M01069942, in tiles of four frames at the name column. Most entries are of families this study does not follow and leave no citation below; the nil is the result of reading them, not of skipping them.*

**✔✔ THE NIL IS CLEAN, AND IT IS THE BEST-BOUNDED OF THE FOUR.**

***No* Grah*,* Grach*,* Gracco *or* Grah-Mišan *anywhere in the 1921 census of Gologorica.*** *The whole G of the book is* **Gašparić · Graber · Gregorić · Gržan · Gržanić · Gržetić · Gržević · Gržić**. ⚠ *The bound is the sweep's own, not an index's: a* status animarum *has no* **Mater** *or* **Patrini** *column, so a Grah* ***wife*** *is visible in this book (as* «ux. n. —»*) but a Grah* ***godmother*** *cannot be, because the book has no godparents.*

**⭐⭐⭐ AND IT CITES THE DECREES, WITH DATE AND PROTOCOL NUMBER.**

> *house 27 (M01069855):* «**= Opassi (D. Pref. 2/5-29 N° 0-76)**» *over* «Opašić Franciscus» — *and his wife on the next line,* «**Aemilia ux. n. Čeh = Ceceo (D.Pr. 3/5-29 N° 0-53)**»
> *house 28 (M01069856):* «**= Opassi (D. Pref. 4/5-29 N° 0-80)**»

*Three decrees, three consecutive days of May 1929, three numbers; the annotations run on to 1935.* ***A married woman's maiden name was decreed separately from her husband's surname.***

**⚠⚠ And a decreed form need not sound like the name:** «**Udovičić = Delle Vedove**» *at Kamenik house 70 (M01069898) is a* ***translation*** *(*udovica* = widow), not a respelling. *Beside the phonetic forms (Opassi, Ceceo, Bratti, Androssi, Silli, Sirolli) and the clipped ones (Anci, **Ghersani**, Udovici, Rabario).* **[New method rule.](/method/)**

✔ *«Ghersani» for* **Gržanić** *identifies the* «Ghersan» *of [the 1862 index slip](/gologorica-line/#threecensuses) — that nil is tighter than it could be stated at the time.*

✔ ***Compound surnames are the house style*** — Rabar-Šantelić, Zec-Kočebar, Zec-Jurandić, Rabar-Radetić — *which retires the guess that* «Grah-Mišan» *was a byname.* ⚠ *But the decrees made a second, identical-looking hyphen —* «Rosa **Opassi-Opačić**», «Regina **Rabario-Rabar**», «**Udovici-Udovičić**» — *one name in two languages.* ***«Grah-Mišan» is the first kind: both elements are Slavic.***

**⭐⭐⭐ AND HOUSE 87 IS A DEFRANCESCHI HOUSEHOLD.** «**De Franceschi Aloisius**», *mercator*, *n.* **4 Maji 1832**; «**Joanna ux. n. Udovičić**», *n.* **19 Novemb. 1845**; «Gisella» *1873,* «Aloisius» *1883; two granddaughters married to* «**D'Atri** Francus, *capitaneus exercitus*» *and* «**Galliano** Aloysius». ***It withdraws a death year of 1870 and settles the collision the archive flagged on 5 October.*** **[Told here](/gologorica-line/#golo87) · [corrected here](/corrections/).**

➕ *Next door at house 88,* «**Lefemine Vitus**», *conditio* «***ludimagister ital.***» — *the Italian schoolmaster.*

rows.src: ⭐⭐⭐ DAPA ZM34K-214 — the 1862, 1894 and 1921 censuses: TWO carry their own indexes, one Grah in all three, and a surname changed by DECREE OF THE PREFECT OF POLA
rows.waypointNote: No FamilySearch waypoint: DAPA microfilm, read from the family's own copy of the reel.
rows.pages: 1862: its index at M01069576–M01069577 read in full; the 144 register frames NOT swept. 1894: its Repertorium at M01069750–M01069824 — the whole G section (M01069756–759) and all the supplement pages read; the 246 register frames NOT swept. 1921: no index; ALL 117 frames M01069826–M01069942 read end to end on 11 Oct 2026.
rows.what: [Worklist 218, line 3](/worklist/), the remaining three *status animarum* — 507 frames. Each was checked for a finding aid before being read.
rows.got:
**⭐⭐ TWO OF THE THREE CARRY THEIR OWN INDEX, AND NEITHER HAD BEEN OPENED.**

*The* **1894** *book has a* «**REPERTORIUM**» *(M01069750–824) keyed on surname-initial + forename-initial, giving each person's* ***house number*** *and the* ***page of the census***. ***It indexes PEOPLE, not households*** — *so, unlike [the baptism book's index](/gologorica-line/#mkrindex), it sees women under their own surnames.*

> *page 18, under* «**G R**», *house* **29** · «***Grah - Missan Rosalia***» · *1845*

***One Grah in two hundred and forty-six frames, and the index writes the compound.*** *[That is the exact form this item first met at Gračišće as* «Grah · Missan» *and guessed was a byname](/worklist/) — now attested at Gračišće, Cerovlje and Gologorica twice.* *The supplement pages, which run out of order to page 78, were scanned as well: no further G.*

*The* **1862** *book's index is a* ***loose paper slip*** *lying across blank pages (M01069576–577):* «**Ordo alfabeticus familiarum in hoc statu animarum contentarum**». ***Its G is Gasparich and Ghersan only — no Grah.*** ⚠ *It indexes* ***families***, *so a Grah wife would not appear: it is a nil for heads of house.* *It also indexes* «**Defranceschi Carmel Ant. et Francisca**» *(p.10),* «**Defranceschi Franc. et Clotildis**» *(p.15) and* «**Sestan Anton. et Joanna Defranceschi**» *(p.5).*

---

**⭐⭐⭐ AND THE 1921 BOOK EXPLAINS THE «GRACCO» PENCIL.**

> *house* **7**, *above the heading:* «***corretta in «Petessini», con decreto del prefetto di Pola***» *(M01069835)*

***The Italianisation of Slavic surnames in these books was an administrative act, and the register records it as one.*** *[New method row: for the 1920s and 1930s, search the Slavic form, the byname compound AND the Italian form — and read the space above the heading, where the later hand put the new name.](/method/)*

---

**⭐ Three more things these books gave.** *A* **second clergy list** — *the 1921 book opens with* «Domus parochialis» *and nine Gologorica incumbents from* «**Žváček Ludovicus**, parochus», ***the same man [the Cerovlje book lists as administering that parish* «e Gologorica» *1913–23](/gologorica-line/#cerovljegrah)***, *and [the 1862 book's birthday calendar gives his birth, 18 August 1866](/gologorica-line/#threecensuses).* *The* «**SENES**» *list of the parish's aged at* **31 December 1908**, *which gives* **Defranceschi Maximilianus** *(house 2) a birth of* **2 January 1828** *and* **Defranceschi Aloisius** *(house 87) one of* **4 May 1832**. *And a* **fourth and fifth loose document** *on these reels — the 1862 index slip, and an NDH-era extract form of the 1940s inside the 1921 book.*

⚠⚠ **Both indexes are instruments, not substitutes, and the row says which frames were actually read.** *A filing note as well: the family's two local folders split at* **M01069501**, *not at the reel boundary, so M01069501–M01069942 sit in the folder named* **ZM34K-215** *though [the frame map assigns them to reel 214](/gologorica-line/#framemap). Every frame is present.*

rows.src: ✔✔ DAPA ZM34K-214 — the 1826 STATUS ANIMARUM swept end to end for GRAH: one in 121 frames, and she is a «Grah-Mišan»

rows.waypointNote: No FamilySearch waypoint: DAPA microfilm, read from the family's own copy of the reel.
rows.pages: M01069315–M01069435, all 121 frames. The NOMEN ET COGNOMEN column of the LEFT half of every opening read for every household. The right half — Matrimonii, Obitus, «Locus ex quo vel ad quem» and Adnotatio — was NOT transcribed.
rows.what: [Worklist 218, line 3](/worklist/), second half: sweep the four *status animarum* for the surname, «where the 1826 «Marianna Grah» was found by accident».
rows.got:
**✔✔ ONE GRAH IN A HUNDRED AND TWENTY-ONE FRAMES — AND THE NAME IS NOT WHAT THIS ARCHIVE HAS BEEN CARRYING.**

> *house* **25**, *in the* **Bubich** *household:* «***Marianna GRAH-MIŠAN ux. filia Matthiae et Justinae***» *(M01069358)*

*[Held since 30 September as* «Marianna **Grah**»](/searched/).* ***The register writes the hyphenated compound***, *and it was there all along.* **[So «Grah-Mišan» is now attested in all three parishes](/gologorica-line/#sa1826grah)** — *Gračišće, where [this item first met it as* «Grah · Missan» *and guessed it a byname](/worklist/); [Cerovlje](/gologorica-line/#cerovljegrah); and Gologorica.*

**✔ And a controlled nil across the rest.** *The book opens with the clergy and the* «civilitas», *then runs through some seventy surnames —* **Udovicich · Flegar · Crismanich · Gasparich · Zabran · Ancich · Rabar · Opassich · Ghersan · Bussich · Zaiz · Selesco · Lucovich · Bratizza · Marecich · Terdoslavich · Canzianich · Cocolet** *and the rest.* ***No Grah household, no second Grah wife, no Grah daughter anywhere else in it.***

⚠ **The bound, stated:** *a* status animarum *is one table across two pages and the surname lives on the left half.* **That half was read for every frame; the right half was not** — *including the* «Locus ex quo vel ad quem» *column, which [this archive has mined before](/gologorica-line/) and [whose Cerovlje twin is still unharvested](/gologorica-line/#cerovljegrah).*

**✔ Two things seen in passing, both already held:** *[the Joseph Defranceschi household appears **twice** in this one census](/gologorica-line/#mkrindex) — the same double-entry habit [the baptism books show for 1784–1788](/gologorica-line/#bothbooks1785); and the tail carries* ***foundlings taken from Trieste*** *into Gologorica households in 1844–46,* «ex expositis Tergeste».

**WHAT IS LEFT OF LINE 3:** *the* **1862, 1894 and 1921** status animarum, *and the* **Mater and Patrini columns** *of the 174 baptism-register frames.*

rows.what: [Worklist 218, line 3](/worklist/): sweep the Gologorica baptisms and the four *status animarum* for Grah, in the Patrini and Mater columns. Before reading 174 frames, the back of the book was checked.
rows.got:
**⭐⭐ THE BOOK HAS AN INDEX, AND THIS ARCHIVE HAD NEVER CITED A FRAME OF IT.** *M01069166–M01069181, alphabetical, a* ***household directory*** *— the same form as [the death book's index](/searched/), which this archive has used for a week without noticing the baptisms had one too.*

---

**✔✔ «G»: NO GRAH.** *The block runs* **Gasparich** *×2 ·* **Gherbaz** *·* **Gherson** *×2 ·* **Giurando** *·* **Giuratich** *— then the index jumps straight to* **L**, *H, I, J and K having nobody in them.* ***Not one household of the name baptised a child at Gologorica in ninety-six years.***

⚠⚠ **And the bound is as important as the nil.** *It is a* ***household*** *directory: [a married woman is entered under her husband's surname](/searched/), and [**Theresia née Grach** is in this very book as a mother, filed under **Defranceschi**](/person/theresia-defranceschi-nee-grach-gologorica/).* ***This is a nil for Grah FATHERS and says nothing about Grah mothers or godparents.*** **The 174 register frames and the four* status animarum *remain unread.**

---

**⭐⭐⭐ AND «D» GAVE WHAT LINE 3 WAS NOT ASKING FOR.**

> «**Defranceschi Joseph deffti Josephi** · N.º ~~[struck]~~ **104** · *and beneath,* **63**»

***Twelve children, each with the page of its baptism*** — *Josephus Lambertus 45 · Carolus Joseph 51 · Maria Aloysia 57 · Maximilianus (obiit) 61 · Franciscus Xaverius 65 · Amalia 67 · Clementina 73 · Clementina 76 · Hedvigis Maria Adelhaides 78 · Maximilianus 85 · Enrichus Jacobus 89 · Aloysius ibid.* **Eight are already on the roster; the index names the rest and says where to turn for every one.**

*Two further households of the name:* «**Defranceschi Petrus N.º 8**» *and* «**Defranceschi Leonardus deffti Antonii N.º 10**» — *and* «**Deprato Joanes Bapta N.º 6**» *with four children, [whose house number matches the death index's Deprato](/searched/).*

**⭐⭐ The Leonardus entry closes half of [worklist 171](/worklist/)**, *which carried* «*if Leonardus is house 10 new, and his father Antonius died at house 29 in 1802 … **not written anywhere***». ***It is written here.*** ⚠ *The house equation itself is still unproved.*

⚠ **And the renumbering is inside the finding aid**: *the twelve-child household is entered under a struck number,* **104**, *and* **63** — *three numbers in the index built to let you look it up.*
ev: The index, the G nil and the D block
What the Grah record now holds
