**A sixth man of the name, and he is invisible to the index.** «**il sig.r Marcio de Franceschi**» stands godfather twice in seven weeks, 26 December 1709 and 6 February 1710, each time with a title. **The index is arranged by the child's forename, so no adult who is only a godparent can ever appear in it.** Everything the index says about who lived in the castle is therefore a floor, not a count. The forename is written **«Marcio»** — probably this clerk's *Marzio*, possibly his *Marco*; this archive prints what is on the page and does not choose. *(doc for the entry, inf for the normalisation.)*

**«D. Nadal Defraneschi»** — the *Nadal* the index gives as father of two Pieros — stands godfather on 12 July 1732 **with the honorific D.** *(doc.)*

**And the trap is on that same page.** Four entries below him, a godmother is entered as *«Maria mog. di Nadal **Venir**»*. **Two Nadals, one leaf, one of them not this family.** Anyone who reads the first half of a name and stops has just invented a wife for Nadal Defranceschi.

**Giacomo acquires a patronymic in 1733, and that is evidence about somebody else.** The 1728 entry calls him plainly *«Giacomo de Fran.chi»*; the 1733 entry calls him *«**Giacomo Defranceschi di Pietro**»*. **A clerk adds a patronymic when there are two men of the name to tell apart.** So the register is quietly reporting a second Giacomo at San Vincenti in the 1730s — and giving the first one a father, **Piero**, who is the same forename as the Piero fathering Marina in 1710. *(inf.)*

---

**Two more leaves, and between them they untangle the wives.**

**Carta 76 verso, frame 89 left — «23 Novembre 1731».** *«**Battistina Figliola Legitima del S.r Gio: Battista de Franceschi e di Maria jugali**, nato li 18 sudetto»*, baptised by **D. Piero Antonio Dall'Orto**, godmother *«D. Franceschina moglie del S.r Mattio Stankovich»*. **The index dates this «23 Xbre» — December. The leaf says Novembre**, and the child was born on the 18th. **And the mother is Maria, not Anzoletta.** *(doc.)*

**Carta 26, frame 36 right — and the entry the index puts there is not there.** The leaf runs **18 April to 22 June 1716** and carries **no Defranceschi at all**; its verso opens on 18 July. The index's *«Maria di Batta Defranceschi, 13 Luglio 1716 — c. 26»* cannot be on carta 26. **That is the third of the index's citations to fail in one afternoon** — a wrong carta (Marina, c. 6 for c. 16), a wrong month (Battistina, Xbre for Novembre), and now a citation with nothing behind it.

**The wives resolve, and they resolve into two men who each married twice:**

| | first wife | second wife |
|---|---|---|
| **Gio Battista «Batta»** | **Anzoletta** — Maria 1715, Cattarina 10 Feb 1728 | **Maria** — Battistina 23 Nov 1731 |
| **Giacomo di Pietro** | **Elena** — Maria 11 Feb 1728 | **Anzoletta** — Maria 4 Nov 1733, Gasparo 1737 |

**«Anzoletta» sits in both households, twenty years apart, and that is the whole of the confusion.** It is a common name at San Vincenti, not a clerk's slip and not one woman. **The index made the two households look like one because an index carries a father's forename and nothing else about him.**

**One consequence for this archive's own data.** The roster has carried a **Maria** as *«Giacomo's first wife, mother of Domenico Gasparo, baptised 9 April 1731»*. **Maria is demonstrably Gio Battista's wife seven months later**, and Giacomo's wife in 1728 is Elena. The attribution is [flagged rather than rewritten](/corrections/): the 9 April 1731 baptism has not been read off the leaf here, and this archive does not correct one unread record with another. *(inf.)*

**Carta 32 verso, frame 43 left — and on the very day the index promises a son of Batta, Batta is standing as somebody else's godfather.** The leaf runs **22 July to 15 August 1718**. Under *«Adi 10 Agosto 1718 Mercordi»* the only Defranceschi on it is in the witness line of another family's baptism: *«Maria fig.a legitima d'Ant.o Percovich e di Giovanna sua Consorte, nata li 6 del corrente… **Compari furono Batta de Franceschi e Elena** [Sepchie]»*. **No Gasparo di Batta is on this leaf, and none is on the facing carta 33**, which runs 22 September to 2 October 1718 and carries nobody of the name.

**That is worth stating carefully.** It does **not** prove the index invented Gasparo — a leaf this reading has not opened may still hold him. What it shows is that **the one date the index gave for him lands on a leaf where his father is a witness and not a father**, which is exactly the kind of collapse that produces a phantom child. *(doc for Batta as godfather; the Gasparo entry remains unlocated.)*

rows.src: England & Wales censuses 1841–1921 — «an old Cardiff family», tested
rows.what: Whether anybody of this surname was ever enumerated in Glamorgan, 1841 to 1921
rows.got:
**A Cardiff paper wrote «an old Cardiff family» in 1896. The censuses do not contain that family under this name — and they do contain it under the wife's.**

**The negative first, because it is clean.** Findmypast's census, land and survey records for Great Britain, restricted to births 1815–1895:

| query | Great Britain | Glamorgan |
|---|---|---|
| `Defranceschi` | **0** | **0** |
| `De Franceschi` | **0** | **0** |
| `Defrance*` | 205, all *de France* or modern | **0 census records** |
| `Franceschi*` | — | **1**, and it is a **Franceschini** |

**Nobody of this surname, in any spelling, is enumerated anywhere in Glamorgan in any census from 1841 to 1921.** The one historic Cardiff hit on `Franceschi*` is *Andre Franceschini*, born 1873, at St John in 1901 — **a different surname**, and a warning to anyone who searches on a stem and reads the count instead of the rows.

**Now the other side of the marriage, and this is the find.** **Emerico De Franceschi married Marietta Cosulich at St Peter's, Roath, on 26 July 1876.** Search *Cosulich* in Wales and the censuses answer at once:

| census | where | who |
|---|---|---|
| **1871** | **St Thomas, Swansea** | T. S. Cosulich, b. 1844 |
| **1881** | **St John, Cardiff** | **Giuseppe b. 1829 and Giulia b. 1831**, with **Richiard b. 1860**, **Teny b. 1863**, **Enrico b. 1866** |
| **1891** | **St John, Cardiff** | Emilio b. 1854 · Jesse b. 1864 |
| **1921** | **Barry, Cardiff** | Giulio A. b. 1860 · Bridget b. 1877 · Irene 1897 · Felix 1902 · Doris 1905 · Mabel 1907 · Bernard 1916 |
| **1939** | Rhyl, Flintshire | Bernard S., b. 1916 |

**«An old Cardiff family» is the Cosulich.** They are in South Wales by 1871 at the latest, keeping house at St John in 1881 and 1891, and still at Barry fifty years later. *(doc.)*

**And Marietta is not in any of them.** No Cosulich with a forename beginning *Mar-* appears in any British census. **She married in July 1876 and was gone before April 1881** — which is exactly what a master mariner's wife does, and the *Aquilone* cleared the Bute Docks for Guadeloupe **seventeen months after the wedding**. *(inf.)*

**What this does to the 1896 phrase.** It does not break it; it relocates it. A Cardiff paper in 1896 calling *Signorina Defranceschi* one of «an old Cardiff family» was writing about somebody whose family had been in the town for a generation — and **the only family of that marriage with a generation in Cardiff is her mother's**. **The Signorina is most likely Emerico and Marietta's daughter, Cardiff by her mother's people and Austrian by her father's**, which is also why she took her degree at Vienna. *(inf — and testable: the 1881 St John household's composition would name Marietta's siblings, and the GRO birth index for Cardiff in the late 1870s would name the daughter.)*

rows.src: United States Passport Applications — the images, not the transcripts
rows.what: The birth towns the index reduced to «Italy»
rows.got:
**The row said thirteen birthplaces and the transcripts carried «Italy». The images carry the towns, and two of them are now read.**

> **Louis De Franceschi**, passport **148535**, *[Form for Naturalized Citizen]*, issued Washington **18 December 1919**:
> *«I solemnly swear that I was born at **Sequals, Province of Udine, Italy** on **3rd November 1873**; that my father, **Pietro De Franceschi**, was born in Italy and is now residing at **Deceased**; that I emigrated to the United States, sailing from **Havre, France**, about **February 1907**; that I resided 12 years uninterruptedly in the United States, from 1907 to 1919 at **Washington, District of Columbia**; that I was naturalized… before the **Supreme Court of the District of Columbia** at Washington on **October 4, 1915**.»* Domiciled at **309 14th Street NW**; occupation **cement decorator**. *(doc.)*

> **Giovanni DeFranceschi**, passport **109256**, *[Form for Naturalized Citizen]*, issued Washington **6 January 1922**:
> *«…born at **Castronovo, Italy** on **Dec. 10, 1876**; that my father, **Francesco DeFranceschi**, was born in Italy and is now residing at **deceased**; …sailing from **Havre** about **April 1903**; …from 1903 to 1922 at **Torrington, Conn.**; …naturalized before the **Superior Court of Litchfield County** at **Winsted** on **Feb. 14, 1911**.»* State of **Connecticut**, County of **Litchfield**. *(doc.)*

**And the loop closes on Tobias.** His own 1922 application is the *[Form for Native Citizen]* — *«I was born at **Washington, D.C.** on or about the **15** day of **June 1912**; my **father Louis De Franceski** was born in **Italy** and is now residing at **Washington D.C.**»*, the surname corrected in the margin to **«—Franceschi»**. **The son's paper gives «Italy». The father's paper gives Sequals.** *(doc.)*

**Why the index was not wrong, and why it was useless.** The passport form asks the father's birthplace in a single blank labelled **«(Country.)»** — so «Italy» is the complete and faithful transcription of that field. The **applicant's own** birthplace is a free line, and that is the only place a town can appear. **On the native-citizen form there is no foreign town to give at all.** So the rule is not *«indexers were lazy»*; it is **«the index is faithful to the form, and the form asks a different question of the father than of the son»**.

**Sequals is Friuli, and it is the province Carnia is in.** Sequals sits in the Val Meduna, then **province of Udine**, about forty kilometres south-west of the Val di Gorto this archive's own line comes out of — the **same province, a different valley**. Its trade is **terrazzo and mosaic**, which is exactly what *«cement decorator»* means in a Washington directory, and Sequals men carried that trade around the world. **This is a Friulian population of the name and not this archive's own.** *(inf on the relationship; doc on the town.)*

**Castronovo is not Friuli at all**, and the record gives no province, so **it is not pinned**: *Castronovo di Sicilia* in Palermo and *Castronuovo di Sant'Andrea* in Basilicata both answer to it. **A southern Italian population of the surname, and the first this archive has documented.**

rows.src: The route into a subscription image viewer, when the images are FamilySearch's
rows.what: Reading Findmypast's record images without the viewer
rows.got:
**A Findmypast transcript id for these collections is a FamilySearch film and frame, written out in full.**

    /transcript?id=US%2FUS_PASSPORT_APPLICATIONS%2F007572652%2F00658%2F001670911
                                              ^^^^^^^^^ film   ^^^^^ frame

From there the images are ordinary FamilySearch images and none of the viewer is needed:

1. `https://www.familysearch.org/search/film/<film>?i=<frame-1>` — **the ark is in the document title**, `…/ark:/61903/3:1:<ARK>?cc=2185145&wc=… – Film # <film>`.
2. `https://sg30p0.familysearch.org/service/records/storage/dascloud/das/v2/3:1:<ARK>/dist.jpg` — the full plate, 3,600 × 3,000 or so, which a canvas crop reads comfortably.

**That turns «eighteen images inside a viewer» into eighteen ordinary image loads** — no filmstrip, no paging, no zoom controls, and the crop recipe already used for the parish registers works unchanged. The transcription on these sets is credited *«used by permission of FamilySearch»*, which is the tell that the plate will be there.

rows.src: The Chicago Soundex card — read off the plate, not the index
rows.what: What the naturalisation index card actually carries for Giovanni of Chicago
rows.got:
**The card is open, and it does not give the comune — but it gives the number that will.**

Film **004640985**, frame **97**, reached from the Findmypast record id `US/NATUR/004640985/00097` by the [film-and-frame route](/searched/). A U.S. Department of Labor **Form No. I-1 P**, Soundex code **D 165**:

> Family name **DeFranceschi** · Given name **Giovanni**
> Address **2336 W. Superior St., Chgo.**
> Certificate no. **P. 151190  CN. 4249300**
> Title and location of court **U.S. Dist. Ct., Chgo.**
> Country of birth or allegiance **Italy**
> When born **Jan. 16, 1895**
> Date and port of arrival in U.S. *(blank)*
> Date of naturalization **May 5, 1937**

**Three things this archive did not have.** An **exact birth date** where it carried only a year; a **Chicago street address**; and — the one that matters — a **petition number, P. 151190**.

**The errand was already written down; now it has a citation.** This archive already said *«the petition behind the Soundex index names the comune and is an errand»*. **It is the same errand, but it is now a request for a numbered document from a named court** rather than a search: *Petition for Naturalization 151190, U.S. District Court, Northern District of Illinois, Chicago, 5 May 1937.*

**And the form settles the question for this record type.** The card asks *«Country of birth or allegiance»* and nothing finer. **No amount of reading the index images will ever produce a town**, because the index does not have a field for one. *(doc.)*

rows.src: Which of the 307 American records can answer «is this one ours» — counted
rows.what: Where the birthplace actually lives, dataset by dataset
rows.got:
**Three hundred and seven American travel-and-migration records carry this surname, and they are not one kind of thing.** Counted on 21 September, all sixteen pages:

| record set | rows |
|---|---:|
| United States, Passenger and Crew Lists | **270** |
| United States Naturalization Petitions | 13 |
| Italians to America | 11 |
| United States, Canadian Border Crossings | 6 |
| Illinois, Northern District, Naturalization Index | 2 |
| United States Passport Applications | 2 |
| British & Irish Roots Collection | 2 |
| Passenger Lists Leaving UK 1890–1960 | 1 |

**And the order of work is the opposite of what was assumed.** The work list said to start with the 277 passenger records because their transcripts name the town of last residence. **The naturalisation petitions carry a «Birth place as transcribed» field in the transcript itself** — no image, no order, one navigation — and that field is the whole question. **Thirteen records answer «is this one ours» outright; two hundred and seventy need a plate each.**

**What the thirteen say.** *Joseph Defranceschi*, **«Gallignana, Austria»**, Brooklyn 1912 — already held here, and he is [the first of the Eleven to go](/the-eleven/). *Peter De Franceschi*, **«Basel, Switzerland»**, 12 January 1902, New York 1931. *Bruno De Franceschi*, 12 August 1907, with **Gerda** (15 January 1913) and **Richard** (2 December 1932) at Brooklyn in 1939, and recorded in 1942 under the alias **«de Franceschi or Seedorf»**. **All three households were already in this archive.** *(doc.)*

rows.src: The 270 passenger transcripts, tested against the sweep this archive already ran
rows.what: Whether reading them one at a time would add anything
rows.got:
**The work list wanted 270 passenger transcripts read for the town of last residence. The transcripts do carry it — and the question they would answer has already been answered better.**

**The field is real.** A passenger transcript gives *Residence* outright, with no image: *«Domenico De Franceschi, 23, born 1898, Italian, **Residence Ponte Alpi Italy**, 1921, departure port Trieste, arrival New York, ship **Argentina**»*, and beside him his father *Dom* and a cousin *Giuseppe Misseli* at the American end. So the plan was sound.

**But this archive has already read 1,400 arrivals.** [The Statue of Liberty–Ellis Island sweep](/searched/) took **429 recorded last residences** and found **exactly two Istrian** — *G. Pedena* and *G. Gallignana*, who are Antonio and Albina on the *Conte Rosso* of 9 September 1922 and are already here. Everything else was **Veneto and Friuli**: Castelgomberto and Cornedo in Vicenza, **Ponte nelle Alpi in Belluno**, Pederobba in Treviso, and Sequals, Lestans and Pinzano in Pordenone. **Findmypast's 270 are a subset of those same arrivals.** Reading them one at a time would re-derive, more slowly and from a third of the evidence, a map this archive already has.

**Today's three men are an instance of it, not an exception.** *Angelo* (27, wife **Elisa De Moliner**), *Domenico* (23, father Dom) and *Emanuele* (21, father Ant) **all of Ponte nelle Alpi**, all on the **Argentina** out of **Trieste** in **1921**, with a cousin *Funicelli* and an aunt *Giuseppina Minelli* waiting. A village party under a surname that formed independently in that village. **The names and the relations are new here; the cluster is not.** *(doc.)*

**And there is no query that shortens it.** `keywordsplace` matches **departure and arrival ports only** — *Trieste* returns 8, *Naples* 3 — and **not the residence field**. The proof is Domenico: his transcript reads *«Residence Ponte Alpi Italy»* and a search for **«ponte alpi» returns zero**. **So «Fiume: 0» and «Istria: 0» are not negatives**, they are a field that was never indexed. Anyone who runs those two queries and stops has learned nothing — which is the third time in one day this archive has met that shape.

**Recommendation: re-scope the item.** The 270 should not be read exhaustively. What is worth reading is the **1949–1956 arrivals**, which the Ellis Island database does not reach at all and where the Istrian *esodo* sits.

rows.src: The Irish, Scottish and English parish and civil sets — opened at last
rows.what: The three national sets the trials never reached
rows.got:
**Three sets, and between them they hold exactly one person this archive did not have.**

**Ireland is a different surname.** `Defrance*` across the Irish parish and civil sets returns **11**, and every one of them is **de France, Defrance or de Frances** — Edvardum baptised at St James and Templetown in Fern in 1820, Mariam there in 1822, a Defrance baptism at Newbridge in 1789, James born and John dead at New Ross. **That is the Huguenot name, not this one.** Nil.

**Scotland is one row and it is not ours either** — *Constance Defrance*, 1939, Quarter, Lanarkshire, in the probate index. Nil.

**England and Wales, on the exact spelling, gives five — and one of them is new.**

| who | what | where |
|---|---|---|
| **Laura Defranceschi** | **died Q4 1931, aged 83, born about 1848** | **Croydon, Surrey — GRO 2A/520** |
| Emerico de Franceschi | marriage 1876 | St Peter, Roath — already held |
| three later marriages | 1964, 1975, 1994 | living, and named here only |

**Laura is the only person of this exact surname in the entire England and Wales death index**, and she was born about **1848** — in the Austrian Littoral years, before any of this archive's emigrations. Nothing connects her to the Cardiff household except the surname and the century, and **this archive does not connect her.** **The certificate would**: Croydon, fourth quarter 1931, volume 2A page 520, which would give her exact age, her address and the informant. *(doc for the index entry; the identification is open.)*

rows.src: Svetvinčenat births 1764–1791 — the 1780 leaves, the year of Antonio's exemption
rows.what: Antonio Defranceschi's household, in the year the Atti says he led the castle
rows.got:
**The 1780 leaves are open, and Antonio is on them — but as a husband, not a father.**

Film **005497885**, the second births volume, frames **81, 82 and 83**, covering **21 April to late October 1780** — the year *Atti* 48 says **Antonio Defranceschi** led the castle households to their exemption from armed service.

| carta | date | what it says |
|---|---|---|
| **80** | **1 May 1780** | *«Patrini ad sacrum fontem fuere Michael Roubaglich ex Parrochia Sanvincentina et **Matthea uxor Antonij Defranceschi**»* — godmother to Joannes, son of Gregorio Matias |
| **80** | 21 Apr 1780 | Helena Percich; no one of the name |
| **81** | Aug–Sep 1780 | eight baptisms; **none of the name** |
| **82/83** | 17 8bris 1780 | *«Patrini ad sacrum fontem fuerunt **Dominico Defranceschi**, et Joanna filia Francisci Zebiza»* |

**So Antonio's wife is Matthea**, named in the exemption year itself, and **Dominicus Defranceschi** stands godfather in the same autumn — the second time that year, after 16 April. **No child of the name is baptised in any of these leaves.** Antonio's and Dominicus's own children are elsewhere in the volume, and the read continues. *(doc.)*

**A faster way to scan, and the trap it creates.** A single crop of **both pages at once** — `__Q(0.268, 0.495, 0.060, 0.545)` — puts the whole opening in one 880×720 canvas, which halves the cost of a page-by-page read from four calls a frame to two. **It is safe for finding a candidate and never for confirming one.** On carta 82 the words *«Maria Catarina filia legitima **Dominici Dassanich q. Laurentij**»* read, at spread scale, exactly like *Dominici Defranceschi* — same length, same shape, same position in the formula. It was about to be written down as a new child of the name. **Magnified, it is Dassanich.**

**That is the third time in one day.** *Defranzieri* on the index page, *Nadal Venir* four entries below *D. Nadal Defraneschi*, and now *Dassanich*. **In this parish the surname has at least three near-twins, and the rule is absolute: no candidate is a finding until it has been magnified.**

rows.src: Svetvinčenat 1780–1782 — seven spreads, and the shape of the silence
rows.what: Whether Antonio's and Dominicus's children are in the exemption years
rows.got:
**Seven spreads read, and in all of them the name appears only in the witness line.**

Images **81, 82, 83** (April–October 1780) and **93, 94, 95** (31 December 1781 – February 1782), plus image **84**, which turned out to be [1763 and not 1781](/corrections/). Every Defranceschi on them is a **godparent**:

- **Matthea uxor Antonij Defranceschi**, godmother, 1 May 1780
- **Dominico Defranceschi**, godfather, 17 8bris 1780
- **Jusca uxor Dominici Defranceschi**, godmother, 31 December 1781

**Not one baptism of the name in any of them.**

**That absence has a shape, and it redirects the search.** A man who stands godfather is an established adult; a wife who stands godmother is a matron. **If Antonio and Dominicus were heading households in the castle in 1780 and none of their children is being baptised in 1780–82, their children were born earlier.** The generation to look for is **1750–1775**, which is the *end of the first volume* and the *opening of the second* — not the years around the exemption at all. *(inf, but it is the kind of inference a register is built to support.)*

**Two names stopped being suspicious along the way.** *Jusca* appears on image 94 as a **child's given name** (*Jusca filia legitima Joannis Budesich*) and again on image 95 (*Jusca filia Matthei Prohia*); *Fosca* appears on image 95 as another man's wife. **Both are ordinary names in this parish**, which is why the register can write one woman both ways without anyone at the time being confused — and why a reader three centuries later should not take either spelling as a slip.

rows.src: What the Svetvinčenat index already says about 1735–1763
rows.what: Whether the index has already answered the question the page-by-page read is asking
ev: The index, read end to end
rows.got:
**Before reading forty-seven more frames, it is worth asking what the volume's own index has already ruled out — and the answer narrows the hunt to eight forenames.**

The index at images 196–211 was [read end to end last night](/searched/). It is arranged **by the child's forename**, it runs **B to P and no further**, and it yields **seven Defranceschi entries in the whole volume** — Maria 1709, Marina 1710, Maria 1716, Maria 1728, Maria 1733, and two Pieros, 1725 and 1734.

**Every one of them is 1734 or earlier.** The volume runs to **1763**. So for the twenty-nine years from 1735 to 1763 the index records **not one child of this name**.

**That leaves exactly three possibilities, and the middle one is the interesting one:**

1. There were no Defranceschi children at San Vincenti between 1735 and 1763 — which sits badly against Antonio and Dominicus heading households there in 1780.
2. **Their children's forenames fall in the index's gap.** The letters it never had are **A** and **R–Z**: *Antonio, Andrea, Anzolo, Rocco, Simon, Tomaso, Vito, Zuanne*.
3. The index is simply incomplete for those years.

**And possibility 2 has a name in it.** *Atti* 48 says the man who led the castle households to their exemption in 1780 was **Antonio**. A man of standing in 1780 was born somewhere around 1720–1750 — **inside the window the index cannot see** — and *Antonio* is the first forename the index drops. **An Antonio baptised at San Vincenti in those years would be invisible to the only finding aid the volume has.**

**So the page-by-page read is not looking for any Defranceschi baptism. It is looking for one whose child is called Antonio, Andrea, Anzolo, Rocco, Simon, Tomaso, Vito or Zuanne** — and the index has already done the rest of the work. *(inf, and it is the cheapest inference available: it costs nothing and removes most of the search.)*

rows.src: The esodo arrivals, 1947–1957 — and the transcripts go thin exactly where they are wanted
rows.what: The post-war American arrivals the Ellis Island database cannot reach
rows.got:
**Fifty-five arrivals of the exact spelling between 1947 and 1957 — and this archive's plan for reading them was wrong.**

This window was [carved out this morning](/worklist/) as the part of the American passenger record worth reading, because the Statue of Liberty database stops long before it and the **Istrian *esodo*** sits squarely in it. The count is real: `defranceschi`, United States travel and migration, event year 1952 ± 5, returns **55**.

**But the transcripts change shape after the war.** The 1900s–1920s series gives *«Residence: Ponte Alpi Italy»* — an actual town. The 1947–57 series gives **«Birth place: Italian»**, which is a nationality:

> **Riccardo Defranceschi**, age **60**, born **1889**, *«Birth place Italian»*, arrived **New York, 1949**, ship **Atlantico** — NARA T715 roll 7738, film **002296450**.
> **Livio Defranceschi**, *«Birth place Italian»*, arrived **New York, 1957**, ship **C O N S T I T U T I O N** — NARA T715 roll 8833, film **002322278**.

**So the question these fifty-five were going to answer is not in their transcripts.** The town is on the manifest itself. **Each transcript does carry a FamilySearch film number**, so the plate is reachable by the [film-and-frame route](/searched/) already written down — which means the item costs **fifty-five images**, not fifty-five navigations, and it is **blocked until the FamilySearch session is signed in again**.

**What can be said now.** Riccardo is new to this archive — **a man of sixty crossing in 1949**, which is a refugee's age and a refugee's year. Livio is not: [a Livio born at Pola in 1925 stands in the Arolsen IRO files](/searched/), displaced in 1947. **A Pola man in a displaced-persons file in 1947 and a Livio landing at New York in 1957 are the right shape for one life — and this archive is not joining them**, because the manifest gives neither a birth year nor a town and the only thing the two records share is a forename. *(doc for both arrivals; the identification is open.)*

rows.src: Svetvinčenat marriages 1762–1815 — opened, and the first entry of the name is a father already dead
rows.what: The marriage register, opened for the first time
ev: The births of the same parish
rows.got:
**The marriage register has never been opened by this archive, and the first Defranceschi entry in it names a man who was already dead.**

> **«Adi 9 Febraro 1766. S. Vicenti»** — *«**Mattio figlio di q[uondam] Michiel Sandalezza**, nativo dal Territorio **d'Albona** ma per il suo domicilio d'anni **15 c[irc]a** in questo Distretto di S. Vicenti, fà admesso da questa Sp[eciа]le Cura… ha contratto il matrimonio per verba de presenti con **Elena figlia di q[uondam] Mattio de Franceschi, nativa di questo Castello**, confessati, comunicati e loro ammaestrati ne dogmi della S.ta Fede…»* Carta 11. *(doc, read at magnification.)*

**Three things come out of one entry.**

**A ninth man of the name at the castle — and a dead one.** *«q. Mattio de Franceschi»*: **Mattio was in his grave before February 1766.** The castle's roll now reads Nardo, Piero, Batta, Giacomo, Nadal, Marcio, Antonio, Dominicus and **Mattio**.

**A daughter, and she is marrying out of the parish's own stock.** **Elena de Franceschi**, *«nativa di questo Castello»*, marries a man of **Albona** — Labin, thirty kilometres east — who had been living in the district about fifteen years. **The first marriage of the name this archive has ever read at Svetvinčenat.**

**And a date that sits exactly in the gap.** A bride of 1766 was born around the 1740s, in the twenty-nine years **the volume's index cannot see**, and her father died before she married. **This is the generation [the godparent reading redirected to](/searched/), and the marriage register reached it in one leaf where the baptisms had taken seven spreads to say nothing.**

**A catalogue correction, from the film's own title card**: *«MATIČNA KNJIGA VJENČANIH **1762–1815**»*, item 2, microfilmed at the Hrvatski državni arhiv, Zagreb, 17 June 1997. **The catalogue says 1762–1858.**

rows.src: Marie Defranceschi in Lorraine — the succession table run back to the birth act
rows.what: AD54: Bénaménil 1936 and Thiébauménil 1911 censuses, Thiébauménil decennial table 1873–1932, and the 1910 birth register
rows.got:
**The record David sent could not be matched to anybody here, so it was worked backwards through two censuses and a decennial table until the act itself turned up — and the act spells the name differently.**

The lead was a *Table des successions et absences* for **Marie DEFRANCESKI**, widow of **Louis Alphonse LABAYE**, died **4 April 1940 at Bénaménil (Meurthe-et-Moselle)**, husband born about 1868.

**The 1936 census of Bénaménil** *(6 M 33/60, 240 rows read in full)* has **no Labaye and no Defranceski**. What it does have, at row 231, is *«Labaye Marthe, 1910, Thiébauménil»*, wife of *Larger Ernest, peintre*. That birthplace was the whole of the redirection.

**The 1911 census of Thiébauménil** *(6 M 33/519, all 240 individuals read)* has **no Labaye either** — the family had gone within a year of the birth. One right-hand page is covered by a loose mairie certificate of 27 March 1911; the same page is re-shot on the following image, so nothing is actually lost.

**The decennial table settled it in two pages.** *2 E 519/TD 2* is not handwriting at all but a table **typed and printed on 27 November 1995**, alphabetical, one line per act. Births 1900–1912, page 004:

> `* LABAYE Henriette amelie   ! 8 ! THIEBAUMENIL 54 ! 11/07/1908`
> `* LABAYE Marthe louise      ! 1 ! THIEBAUMENIL 54 ! 30/01/1910`

**Acte n° 1 of 1910** *(2 E 519/7, image 170)* names the mother in the clerk's own hand: **«Marie Defranceschi, âgée de vingt-neuf ans, sans profession, son épouse»**, wife of **Louis Alphonse Labaye, maçon**, whose age the mayor first wrote as fifty and then corrected, in the margin and over his signature, to **forty-one**.

**So the succession table's «Defranceski» is the registrar of 1940 writing down what he heard; the registrar of 1910 wrote «Defranceschi».** Both are the same woman, born about 1880–81, and this archive now carries her under the spelling the earlier clerk used.

**What is still missing is the marriage.** The Thiébauménil marriage table for 1903–1912 goes straight from *Humbert* to *Leybach*, and has no Defranceschi under her own name. Her parents and her birthplace — the only things that could join her to a line — are in another commune's register.

rows.src: Svetvinčenat marriages, images 8–25 — a de Franceschi marriage in 1772, and the father dead the winter before
rows.what: Svetvinčenat marriage register 1762–1815, film 005497885, images 8–14 and 21–25 read in full
rows.got:
**Eighteen more frames of the marriage register, and the first Defranceschi wedding in it.**

Images 8–14 and 21–23 gave nothing: forty-odd weddings of Justinovich, Marzan, Gulcich, Xivolich, Millovan, Bercan, Sandalesa and the rest, 1763 to 1771. **The register changes language in 1770** — Italian *«Adì … contrasse il matrimonio per verba de presenti»* becomes Latin *«Tribus premissis denunciationibus … matrimonio juncti sunt»* — so anything after that frame is being searched for **Franceschi**, not *de Franceschi*.

**Image 24, carta 20, 23 November 1771.** Not a Defranceschi wedding — a Defranceschi *in the room*. Michael Predan married Elena, daughter of the late Vito Giurzan, and the entry closes:

> *«…sunt, addita Benedictione. **Testibus Vincentio Vemir, ac Jacobo q. Jacobi de Franceschi** alijsq. Arch.»*

**Image 25, carta 21, 10 June 1772.** Seven months later the same man is the groom:

> *«**Anno Domini 1772, 10 Junij. Giacobus filius Giacobi de Franceschi**, et **Nicolina filia Nicolai Teserati**, juncti sunt per verba de presenti per me D. Martinum Luciani ex comissione Parochi, tribus premissis denunciationibus, testibus D.no Michaele Luciani et Vicentio Vemir alijsque pluribus, addita benedictione. Ego autem Arch. Jo: Pittan testor ita esse veritatem.»*

**Two men, not one.** The November entry writes **«q. Jacobi»** — *quondam*, the father already dead; the June entry drops the *quondam* and writes only *«filius Giacobi»*. The first is the careful form and the second the hurried one, seven months apart in the same volume and, on the November page, in the same priest's hand. **So Giacomo de Franceschi the elder was dead before 23 November 1771**, and his son Giacomo married at the castle on 10 June 1772. *(doc.)*

**Neither is merged with anyone.** This archive already carries a **Giacomo De Franceschi born 1731** and a **Giacomo born 1706** at Svetvinčenat, either of whom could be the father, and the son — marrying in 1772 — would have been born in the 1740s, inside the stretch the baptism index does not cover. A forename and a death-before date is not enough to join a person to a person; the same rule that was applied to [Mattio, dead before 1766](/who/mattio-de-franceschi/). *(inf, for the identification.)*

The bride's surname is the one word on the page this reading will not guarantee: **Teserati**, possibly *Teseveti* or *Tesereti*. It is not a Svetvinčenat name that has come up before.

**Still unread for the pre-1780 Antonio the work list wants: images 26–43.**

rows.src: Antonio de Franceschi found alive at Svetvinčenat in 1773 — six times over, with a grown son and a dead brother-in-name
rows.what: Svetvinčenat marriage register 1762–1815, film 005497885, images 26–27 (cartae 22–23, the year 1773)
rows.got:
**The work list has wanted a pre-1780 Antonio for weeks. Two frames of the marriage register produced him six times in ten months *(revised 28 Sept 2026: a dozen entries, Jan 1773 – Apr 1775)*, and gave him a son.**

Images 26 and 27 cover cartae 22 and 23, the whole of 1773. **Antonio de Franceschi is not marrying in any of them — he is standing witness**, almost always beside the same man, Joannes Sain:

| Date | Whose wedding | How he is entered |
|---|---|---|
| **25 Jan 1773** | Michael Crisman × Fusca, dau. of Thomas | *«testibus **Ant.º de Franceschi** et Jo: Sain»* |
| **27 Jan 1773** | Martinus, son of Antonio Macich × Victoria, widow | *«testibus **Ant.º de Franceschi** et Joanne Sain»* |
| **27 Jan 1773** | Andreas, son of Antonio Macich × Eufemia Petrovich | *«testibus **Ant.º de Franceschi** et Jo: Sain»* |
| **2 May 1773** | Jacobus Scanduli × Maria, dau. of the late Andrea Xuntich | *«testibus **Ant.º de Franceschi**, et Vincentio Vemir»* |
| **5 Aug 1773** | Mathias Petrovich × Maria Bulesich | *«testibus **Ant.º de Franceschi**, et Stephano Petrovich»* |
| **31 Oct 1773** | Simon Mazzar × Lucia, dau. of the late Vito Guerlich | *«testibus **Ant.º de Franceschi** et Joanne Sain»* |

**A man asked for six times in one year is a man the parish trusts and, more to the point, a man who lives there.** *(doc.)*

**And on 4 February 1773 his son stands instead of him.** At the wedding of Michael Sarcovich and Maria Crisman the witnesses are *«Jo: Sain, et **Victorio de Franceschi filio Antonij**»* — Vittorio de Franceschi, **son of Antonio**. It is the first document this archive has that names a father and son of the name in the same breath at Svetvinčenat. **A son old enough to witness in February 1773 puts Antonio's own birth back to about 1730 at the latest.** *(doc for the relationship; the date is inferred.)*

**The third thing on the same two pages is a death, told sideways.** On **30 March 1773**, with a dispensation to marry in Lent:

> *«Joannes Volge, et **Maria relicta q.m Gasparis de Franceschi**, dispensatione obtenta a tribus denunciationibus et facultate celebrandi … matrimonium etiam tempore quadragesimae…»*

**Gasparo de Franceschi was dead before 30 March 1773, and his widow Maria married again that day.** The haste — a Lenten dispensation, all three banns waived — is the kind a widow with a household to keep asks for. *(doc.)*

**What this archive will and will not join up.** The [Gasparo dossier](/who/gasparo-de-franceschi/) already holds **two** men who fit: **Gasparo, son of Giacomo De Franceschi and Anzola, baptised 26 December 1737**, who would have been thirty-five in 1773; and **Domenico Gasparo, son of Giacomo, baptised 9 August 1732**, alive and standing godfather in February 1764, who would have been forty-one. **Two candidates is no candidate**, and the 1773 entry names neither a father nor an age. It also holds a **Vittorio Defranceschi, 1758–1812**, the only Vittorio at the castle, who would have been fifteen in February 1773 — young for a witness but not impossible, and the clerk's *«filio Antonij»* is exactly how a young man is distinguished from his father. **Neither is merged.** *(inf, and flagged as such.)*

**The shape that is starting to show** — and it is a shape, not a fact — is one household: **Giacomo de Franceschi, dead before November 1771**, with a son or sons called **Gasparo** (one of the two of that name, dead before March 1773) and **Giacomo** (married June 1772); and, separately, **Antonio**, born by about 1730, with his son **Vittorio**. Nothing in the register says they are one family. *(inf.)*

**Still unread: images 28–43.**

rows.src: The Svetvinčenat marriage volume read to the end — Antonio's marriage is not in it, and he turns out to be the bell-ringer
rows.what: Svetvinčenat marriage register 1762–1815, film 005497885 — images 28–43, completing images 6–44
rows.got:
**Every frame of the 1762–1779 register has now been read, and the question the work list asked has a clean answer: no.** Antonio de Franceschi did not marry at Svetvinčenat between 1762 and 1779.

**The arithmetic said so before the reading finished.** Antonio has a son old enough to witness a wedding in February 1773, so he married around 1750–1756 — and this volume opens in **1762**. His marriage falls inside the 1623–1762 hole in the parish's marriage books. Only a remarriage could have been here, and there is none. *(doc, for the negative: thirty-eight frames read line by line.)*

**What the last sixteen frames did give:**

**A second daughter of the dead Mattio, and so a sister for Elena.** Carta 24, 17 October 1773:

> *«Mar[c]-Antonius Jacomini filius Andreae … et **Fusca filia q. Mathiae de Franceschi** Parochiana huius Ecclesiae, dispensatis a denunciationibus … **Testes D. Antonius de Franceschi**, ac Mathias Santalera.»*

Elena married in 1766 as *«figlia di q. Mattio de Franceschi»*; Fusca marries in 1773 as *«filia q. Mathiae de Franceschi»*. **Same dead father, same parish, seven years apart — the first sibling pair of the name this archive has at Svetvinčenat**, and Antonio stands witness at the younger one's wedding. *(doc for both entries; that the two Mattios are one man is inf, though it is hard to make them two.)*

**Antonio's trade, which changes what his six 1773 appearances mean.** Three entries of 1774–75 style him with an occupation, and one of them puts the word first, where it cannot be misparsed:

> *«…e del **Campanaro Antonio Defranceschi**. Testimonj»* — 25 September 1775
> *«…& **Ant.º Defranceschi Campanaro**, ed altri»* — 27 February 1775
> *«…d'**Ant.º Defranceschi Campanaro**, Pasquich di Michael ed altri Testimonj»* — 29 October 1775

**He was a bell-ringer.** Read letter by letter at full resolution: C-a-m-p-a-n-a-r-o. **This archive had written, that same afternoon, that a man asked for six times in one year «is a man the parish trusts». The truer explanation is duller and better: he worked at the church.** The priest reaching for a witness reached for whoever was already in the building. *(doc.)*

**And it is not a title he holds alone.** *«Zne Sain Campanaro»* appears in February and July 1776 and January 1777 — four months after Antonio last carries it. Either the office changed hands, or Svetvinčenat had more than one bell-ringer among its several churches. **No claim of sole tenure is made here.** *(inf.)*

**A fourth forename, in the next generation.** Carta 36, **29 November 1777**, twice in one day: *«alla presenza mia di Simon Manzoni e **Dom.co Defranceschi**»* and *«presenza di **Dom.co Defranceschi** e di Simon Manzoni»*. **Domenico** now stands where Antonio stood, beside the same Simon Manzoni. Antonio is not named again after 1775. *(doc.)*

**The whole volume, counted.** Thirty-eight frames, 1762 to 1779:

| | |
|---|---|
| Marriages **of** the name | **1** — Giacomo son of Giacomo × Nicolina Teserati, 10 June 1772 |
| Brides of the name | **2** — Elena (1766) and Fusca (1773), sisters |
| Deaths recorded sideways | **3** — Mattio (bef. 1766), Giacomo the elder (bef. Nov 1771), Gasparo (bef. Mar 1773) |
| Witness appearances | **14** — Antonio ×11, Vittorio *filio Antonij* ×1, Giacomo ×2, Domenico ×2 |
| Occupations recorded | **1** — Antonio, *campanaro* |

**Five forenames of the name are alive or lately dead at Svetvinčenat in these eighteen years — Mattio, Giacomo, Gasparo, Antonio, Domenico — plus Vittorio and the two sisters. Not one of them is joined to another except Antonio→Vittorio and Elena↔Fusca.** The joins are in the volume this parish has lost.

rows.src: Vittorio's father was in this archive all along — and the baptism is not where the arithmetic said it was
rows.what: Svetvinčenat baptisms 1709–1764, film 005497885, images 155 and 171–185 — and this archive's own burials.json
rows.got:
**The job was to find Vittorio's baptism. It is not found. What was found instead was already in this archive's own files, unread, and it answers the question the baptism was wanted for.**

**The burial names the father.** `burials.json` has carried this row since the graves work:

> **Vitorio Defranceschi** · born 1758 · died and buried **8 November 1812** · **aged 54** · Svetvinčenat · **kin: Antonio**

The 1773 marriage register gives *«Victorio de Franceschi **filio Antonij**»*. The 1812 burial gives a Vittorio of the same parish whose recorded kin is **Antonio**. **Two independent records, thirty-nine years apart, give the same man the same father.** This archive published that identification this morning as *«probable, left open»* while holding the corroboration in its own data. *(doc.)*

**And the naming pattern signs it.** Vittorio's own children are in the same file: **Antonia** (1804–1808), **Giovanni Pietro** (1809), **Antonio** (1811) and **Gioanni Maria** (d. 1813). **A man whose first-recorded son is called Antonio, in a parish that names the first son for the paternal grandfather, is a man whose father was Antonio.** That is not proof; it is the third thing pointing the same way. *(inf.)*

**So the descent now runs three generations:**

> **Antonio** *(bell-ringer, witness 1773–75)* → **Vittorio** *(witness Feb 1773; d. 8 Nov 1812 aged 54)* → **Antonia, Giovanni Pietro, Antonio, Gioanni Maria** *(1804–1813)*

**Where the baptism is not.** Nineteen frames of the baptism register 1709–1764 were read for it, on anchors fixed by probing: **image 155 = January 1750, image 175 = February 1758, image 185 = June 1761** — about 2.5 frames a year. **Images 171 to 181 cover 1756 to 1760 continuously and contain no Defranceschi child of any Antonio.** A man dying aged 54 in November 1812 was born about 1758, and 1758 is read. *(doc, for the negative.)*

**What the same frames did give.** Carta 162, **7 November 1759**:

> *«**Antonia filia legitima Jacobi de Franceschi et Paschasiæ eius legitimæ uxoris**, amborum ex hac Parochia, nata die 5 currentis, Baptizata est … Patrini fuerunt ad Sacrum Fontem Gregorius Doblanovich, et Boneta Uxor Benedicti Fiorencis.»*

**A whole household of the name, with the wife's forename** — Giacomo de Franceschi and **Paschasia**, and a daughter **Antonia** born 5 November 1759. It is the first Defranceschi child this archive has read out of the Svetvinčenat baptism register for the eighteenth century. *(doc.)*

The same stretch shows the name constantly at the font but rarely at its centre: **Jacobus Defranceschi** godfather 6 August 1758, **Gasparo De Franceschi** godfather 6 July 1760, **Franciscus de Franceschi** godfather October 1759, and a **Pasqua** named as a Defranceschi wife in 1760 and 1761 whose husband's forename this reading will not guarantee — the abbreviation will not resolve between *Gasparo* and *Giacomo* even at full magnification, and it is left unread rather than guessed. *(doc for the appearances; the one forename is open.)*

**Why the index could not be used.** The volume has a contemporary alphabetical index at the back, and it was the obvious shortcut. **It stops around 1736.** The A page's last six lines run January 1735 to January 1736, and then the parish ruled off and reused the blank half of the same leaf for baptisms of 1763. Every entry the earlier sweep ever recovered from that index is 1732 or earlier. **The 1737–1764 baptisms are unindexed**, which is why this had to be a frame-by-frame read at all. *(doc.)*

**Still to read for the baptism: images 155–170 (1750–1756) and 182–196 (1761–1763).**

rows.src: Images 155–170 read: no child of Antonio in the whole decade, but Giacomo and Pascasia have four
rows.what: Svetvinčenat baptisms 1709–1764, film 005497885, images 155–170 read page by page
rows.got:
**Sixteen more frames, 1750 to 1756, read page by page. Antonio is still not a father anywhere in this register — and a different household came out of it almost complete.**

**The negative first, because it is now a wide one.** With images 155–181 read, **the whole of 1750 to 1760 has been searched and contains no Defranceschi child of any Antonio.** Vittorio, who died in November 1812 aged fifty-four and whose burial names his father as Antonio, was born about 1758 — and 1758 is inside the read stretch, twice over. **His baptism is not in this volume.** *(doc, for the negative.)*

**What is here instead is a family.** *«Jacobus Defranceschi»* and his wife *«Pascasia»* — Pasqua — appear as parents four times:

| baptised | child | frame |
|---|---|---|
| **25 March 1750** | forename not read — the leaf is flagged *razlivena tinta*, smeared ink, and it would not resolve at full magnification | 155 |
| **21 August 1753** | **Giacomo Battista**, *«natо die 19 currentis»* | 163 |
| **10 January 1756** | **Giovanni** | 169 |
| **7 November 1759** | **Antonia**, *«nata die 5 currentis»* | 179 |

> *«Die 21. Augusti 1753. **Jaco[bus] Baptista filius legitimus Jacobi Defranceschi, et Pascasia eius legitima uxoris**, amborum ex hac Parochia, nato die 19 currentis…»*

> *«Die 10. Januarij 1756. **Joannes filius legitimus Jacobi Defranceschi, et Pascasia eius legitimae uxoris**, amborum ex hac Parochia…»*

Both magnified and read letter by letter. **This is the first household of the name at Svetvinčenat that this archive can follow across a decade rather than meet once.** *(doc.)*

**And it probably reaches the 1772 wedding.** The marriage register has *«Giacobus filius Giacobi de Franceschi»* marrying Nicolina Teserati on **10 June 1772**. A Giacomo Battista baptised in August 1753 would be eighteen. The father, *«q. Jacobi»* in November 1771, would have died when that son was eighteen too. **The dates fit without strain — but a forename and a plausible age is exactly the evidence this archive has twice refused to treat as an identification, and it refuses again here.** *(inf.)*

**Two things left deliberately unread.**

**The wives do not agree with themselves.** The four baptisms give the mother as **Pascasia**. But entries of 1754, 1755 and 1756 style a godmother *«uxor Jacobi Defranceschi»* with what reads as **Veneranda**. Either there are two men called Jacobus at once, or one of the readings is wrong at scan resolution. **Nothing is claimed either way until those three lines are magnified.**

**And a Jacobus who cannot be the baby.** On **12 May 1754** a godfather is entered as *«Jacobus filius Jacobi Defranceschi»* — an adult son of a Giacomo, nine months after Giacomo Battista was born. **So there were already two generations of the forename at the castle before 1754**, which is the likeliest reason the wives look contradictory. *(inf, and the reason the identification above stays open.)*

**Gasparo runs alongside them throughout** — godfather in 1751, 1753 (twice), 1754, and his wife named as godmother repeatedly. He is a separate, contemporaneous household, not another spelling of the same man.

**Still unread in this volume: images 182–195 (1761–1763).** After that the search moves to Births 1764–1791, and to the question of whether Antonio was at Svetvinčenat at all before about 1770.

rows.src: Images 182–195 finish the volume — Gasparo turns out to be Giacomo's son, and the index gives up two more children
rows.what: Svetvinčenat baptisms 1709–1764, film 005497885, images 182–195 — completing 155–195
rows.got:
**The last fourteen frames, 1760 to 1763. No Defranceschi appears as a parent in any of them — and the single line that explains the last two days of confusion is on frame 191.**

**Gasparo is Giacomo's son.** Twice, in the same year, the clerk writes it out in full:

> *«…padrini furono **Gasparo figlio di M.o Giacomo de Franceschi**…»* — 1 August 1762, and again 15 December 1762.

Magnified letter by letter. **This archive has been treating Gasparo and Giacomo as two households running side by side through the 1750s. They are one household: a father and his grown son.** *(doc.)*

**And it matches something the archive already had.** The volume's own index carries *«Casparg, of **Jacobo De Franceschi and Anzola**, 26 December 1737»*. A Gasparo son of Giacomo, born at the end of 1737, is **twenty-four** when he stands godfather in August 1762 — which is exactly the age an adult godparent is. Two independent records, twenty-five years apart, saying the same thing. *(inf, and a strong one.)*

**Which reshapes the household this way** — stated as inference, because no single document says it:

> **Giacomo de Franceschi**, married twice — to **Anzola**, whose son **Gasparo** was baptised 26 December 1737; and to **Pascasia**, whose children are the four found yesterday: a child of March 1750, **Giacomo Battista** (1753), **Giovanni** (1756) and **Antonia** (1759).

**One thing still does not resolve, and it is recorded rather than smoothed.** A godmother formula recurs four times in these frames — *«Dona Pasqua moglie di M.o … de Franceschi»* — and the husband's name is **Gasparo** in November 1760, February 1761 and April 1761, and **Giacomo** in January 1762. Both were magnified; both readings are certain; the hand is the same priest's throughout. **Either father and son each married a Pasqua, or Simon Zadro wrote the wrong one of the two names he knew best.** Nothing here decides it. *(open.)*

**The index then gave up two more children.** Frames 194–195 turn out to be the start of the volume's alphabetical index — the **A** page — which the earlier sweep never reached. Two lines in it are ours:

> *«**Antonia fig.a di Gio Batta Defranceschi**, 1 7bre 1721»*
> *«**Andrea fig.o di Giacomo Defranceschi**, 5 marzo 1726 — c. 59»*

Both magnified. **Antonia of 1721 is a fourth child for the Gio Batta × Anzoletta household** the archive already knew from this index (Gasparo 1718, Cattarina 1728, Battistina 1731). **Andrea of 1726 is a child of a Giacomo a generation before Pascasia's** — which is the independent support for there having been two Giacomos, the thing that stopped the 1772 bridegroom being merged with the boy of 1753. *(doc for both entries; carta 59 has not been opened.)*

**Where the volume now stands.** Images **155–195 are read**, covering **1750 to 1763** continuously, plus the A index. **No Defranceschi child of any Antonio exists anywhere in it.** Images 1–154 (1703–1750) remain unread, and the letters I, L, M, N, O, P, R, S, T, V and Z of the index remain unread — **V is where a Vittorio would be listed, if the index reached his years, which it does not.**

rows.src: Antonio de Franceschi is a father at Svetvinčenat on 9 December 1769 — and half the proof was in this repository
rows.what: Svetvinčenat baptisms 1764–1791, film 005497885: volume mapped, waypoint 31 read — and fsrecords.json mined for its parents column
rows.got:
**The question three days of reading has been circling: was Antonio at Svetvinčenat at all before about 1770? He was, and he was a householder there.** Baptism volume 1764–1791, waypoint 31, carta 26:

> **«9 Xbre 1769»** — *«**Fran.ca figlia di D.no Ant.o De Franceschi** e Donna **Mattia** … **nata li 8 corrente** … Battezata … dal D. Ant.o Can.co Stancovich de L.P.»*

**Franca, daughter of Signor Antonio De Franceschi and Donna Mattia, born 8 December 1769, baptised on the 9th.** The father's name and the date were magnified and read letter by letter; the mother's forename was read at spread scale and is corroborated independently below. **He is styled *D.no* — Dominus, Signor — which the register does not give to everybody.** *(doc.)*

**And Mattia is the woman already on the page eleven years later.** The entry of **1 May 1780** names *«**Matthea uxor Antonij Defranceschi**»* as a godmother. Same couple, same parish, 1769 and 1780. *(doc for both entries; that they are one household is inference, and about as safe as inference gets.)*

**The other half of the proof had never been opened, and it is in this repository.** `fsrecords.json` — indexed FamilySearch records, ingested long ago for names and dates, never read for the **parents** column:

| child | born | parents, as the index gives them |
|---|---|---|
| **Franca De Franceschi** | 8 Dec 1769 | **Ano De Franceschi & Mattia** |
| **Pasqua Vitoria De Franceschi** | 16 Dec 1773 | **Giacomo De Franceschi & Nicoletta** |
| Felice Anto De Franceschi | 22 Sep 1778 | Bortolo De Franceschi & Zannetta |
| **Maria Matthia De Franceschi** | 3 Sep 1784 | **Victorii De Franceschi & Euphemię** |

**Two of those are the missing joins.**

**Pasqua Vitoria, December 1773, of Giacomo and *Nicoletta*.** The marriage register has *«Giacobus filius Giacobi de Franceschi, et **Nicolina** filia Nicolai Teserati»* marrying on **10 June 1772**. Nicolina and Nicoletta are the same name, and the child arrives **eighteen months after the wedding**. **That ties the marriage register to the baptism index for the first time at this parish.** *(inf, and strong.)*

**Maria Matthia, September 1784, of *Victorii* and Euphemia.** **Vittorio de Franceschi as a father**, at twenty-six — the same Vittorio who witnessed a wedding in February 1773 as *«filio Antonij»* and was buried in November 1812 aged fifty-four. *(index; the act itself has not been read.)*

**So the descent is now documented at every step:**

> **Antonio × Mattia/Mathea** *(a householder at Svetvinčenat by 1769, the parish bell-ringer in 1775)*
> → **Franca** (b. 8 Dec 1769, read on the page) and **Vittorio** (b. 1758)
> → **Vittorio × Euphemia** → **Maria Matthia** (b. 3 Sep 1784), and four more children buried 1804–1813

**The volume itself, mapped.** All 367 waypoints enumerated and pinned — **waypoint N = film frame N+214**. Waypoints 2–4 are the resolution target, the cover (*«1764 … 1764–1812»*) and a flyleaf; **5–134 are the 1764–1791 register**; **135 is the bound cover of the next volume**, *«1815–1854 · Liber Baptizatorum · IV»*; and 136–367 are the printed nineteenth-century register. **There is no index for the 1764–91 section** — the shortcut that worked on volume one does not exist here.

New date anchors, probed rather than assumed: **wp 28 = Mar–Apr 1769 · wp 30 = Sep–Oct 1769 · wp 31 = Oct–Dec 1769 · wp 32 = Feb–Jul 1770 · wp 36 = Mar–Apr 1771**. In this stretch the volume *is* in date order — but it is not throughout, and the earlier finding stands that waypoint 84 drops back to 1763 between two leaves of 1780.

**The lesson, for the second time today: the index in the repository was worth more than the film.** Three days went on hunting Antonio through two volumes frame by frame. The line that names him as a father was found on the film — but the line that would have told anyone where to look had been sitting in `fsrecords.json`, in a column nobody had read.

rows.src: Sixty frames of the 1764–91 volume read one by one — a second child for Antonio, and the 1772 marriage joined to its first baby
rows.what: Svetvinčenat baptisms 1764–1791, film 005497885 — waypoints 5–60 read opening by opening
rows.got:
**Sixty of the volume's 134 eighteenth-century frames have now been read opening by opening.** Three of them carry acts; the rest carry the name standing at other people's fonts, which is how a parish records a family that is present but not reproducing.

**A second child for Antonio and Mattea.** Waypoint 58, 21 January 1776:

> *«**Dom[enic]a filia legit[i]ma et natu[rali]s D[omi]ni Antonij Defranceschi, Matthæque ejus** [conjugis], **nata gemina** hac nocte elapsa. Baptizata a me Archip[res]b[yter]um Antonium Massalini.»*

**Domenica, daughter of Antonio Defranceschi and Mattea, baptised 21 January 1776 — and born a twin.** The word *gemina* is squeezed in above the line. Magnified and read letter by letter; her father is styled **D.ni**, Dominus, as he is in Franca's entry seven years earlier. **The second baby of that birth has not been located** and is the obvious next thing to look for. *(doc.)*

**And the 1772 wedding is joined to its first child, on the page.** Waypoint 48, carta 47:

> *«Adi 22 Xbre 1773. **Pasqua e Vitoria figlia di Giacomo de Franceschi, e di Nicoletta** jugali, **nata li 16** a ore dodici del corrente … Battezata da me D. Pietro Can.co Fabris.»*

The marriage register has *«Giacobus filius Giacobi de Franceschi et **Nicolina** filia Nicolai Teserati»* marrying on **10 June 1772**. Nicolina and Nicoletta are one name, and the child arrives **eighteen months later**. **This archive has joined the marriage register to the baptism register at this parish for the first time from two read acts rather than an index line.** *(doc.)*

**Gasparo's window closes.** He is godfather in 1768 — *«Domi.o **Gasparo di Franceschi**»*, magnified — and his wife **Maria** is named as godmother repeatedly through 1770, 1771 and into April 1772. The marriage register then has *«**Maria relicta q.m Gasparis de Franceschi**»* remarrying on **30 March 1773**. Same forename, same parish, eleven months later. **The Gasparo who died is this Gasparo — Giacomo's son, baptised 26 December 1737 — and the widow is the same Maria.** *(inf, and about as tight as this evidence gets.)*

**Antonio is on these pages throughout**: godfather on 4 March 1769 alongside Gasparo, on 25 December 1774, and his wife **Maria**— no, **Mattea** — as godmother in October 1775. **Domenico de Franceschi and a wife appear from 1775.**

**Two cautions this sweep produced, both now written into the method.**

**The volume has two decoys that a spread-scale scan cannot separate from this surname**: the officiating priest **«D. Anto Stancovich»**, who signs most entries, and the local gentry **«Sig. Francesco Fabris»**. Waypoint 7 produced a false positive that magnification killed. Every candidate needs a second, narrow look.

**And a render fault was silently eating frames.** A fixed two-second wait after loading a plate is not always enough: the crop fires before the JPEG finishes and the screenshot comes back black. Three frames were lost that way before it was noticed. The fix is to poll `img.complete && naturalWidth > 100` rather than sleep — the same lesson this archive already learned on Findmypast and had not carried across.

**Domenico's wife will not settle**: *Victoria* in 1775 and 1776, *Fosca* in 1780, *Jusca* in 1782. Either remarriages or the clerk's ear, and it is recorded as open rather than reconciled.

**Still unread: waypoints 61–80, 85–92 and 96–134 — about sixty-seven frames.**

rows.src: Frames 90-107 of the Svetvincenat baptism volume -- Vittorio named his father's son a second time, and five decoys caught
rows.what: Svetvinčenat baptisms 1764–1791, film 005497885 — frames 90–107 read opening by opening
rows.got:
**Eighteen more openings read one by one.** Every candidate below was magnified before it was written down, and **five were killed at magnification** — which is the more useful half of this entry.

**Vittorio is called his father's son a second time, nine years after the first.** Frame 98, **20 September 1782**:

> *«Patrini qui susceperunt fuere **Victorius filius Antonii de Franceschi**, et **Fosca Vxor Dominici Defranceschi**.»*

The February 1773 marriage-witness line said *«Victorio de Franceschi filio Antonij»*. The 1812 burial says `kin: Antonio`. **Three independent records, thirty-nine years apart, give the same man the same father.** *(doc.)* And by frame 103, **8 May 1784**, he needs no father at all: *«Patrini fuere **Victorivs de Franceschi**, et Constantia Vxor Antonij Fabri»*.

**Mattea gains two years of life.** Frame 98, **18 August 1782**: *«Martinus Merklem, et **Matthea Vxor Antonij Defranceschi**»*. She was last seen on 1 May 1780. *(doc.)*

**Two of the name stand at one font, and the clerk says so in one word.** Frame 101, **10 September 1783**: *«Patrini fuere **Antonivs de Franceschi, et Evphemia pariter de Franceschi**»*. ***Pariter*** — likewise, the same surname. Vittorio's wife was a Euphemia, which would make this Antonio beside his own daughter-in-law; **that is inference and is not written down as fact.** *(doc for the entry; inf for who she is.)*

**Domenico appears in the baptisms under his own name for the first time.** Frame 106, **13 October 1784**: *«Patrini fuere **Dnvs Dominicvs de Franceschi**, et Maria q.m Defuncti Antonii Bergamo»* — styled ***Dnvs***, the courtesy the register gives Antonio and withholds from most of the parish. Until now he was only ever «Fosca's husband». *(doc.)*

**And one man can now be struck off the list of who he might be.** Antonio's son Domenico was born **25 December 1777**. He is five years old when Fosca is already «uxor Dominici» in September 1782. **They are different men.** *(doc for the elimination.)*

**Fosca, wife of Domenico, is now attested seven times** across 1780–1784 — 9 September 1781, 20 September 1782, 10 December 1782, 16 December 1783 and 3 January 1784 are new here, all magnified. She is one of the parish's standing godmothers.

### The five that died at magnification

| frame | at spread scale it looked like | magnified, it reads |
|---|---|---|
| 86 | «Dominici **Defranceschi** et Euffemiæ» | «Dominici **Brasich**» |
| 91 | «Maria, Vxor Antonij **Defranczo**» | «Maria, Vxor Antonij **Bergamo**» |
| 99 | a de Franceschi godmother | «Joanna filia q.m **Francisci Zabrza**» |
| 104 | «Catharina filia Dominici **de Fra[nceschi]**» | «Catharina filia Dominici **de Paz ex Rubino**» |
| 98 | «**Fosca** …» (a bare forename) | a different Fosca — «**Fosca Vxor Martini Merklem**» |

**Frame 104 was the most valuable candidate of the day and it was false.** A daughter of Domenico would have been the best find of the sweep; the page instead says *de Paz*, a Rovinj family — three letters where the eye supplied eleven.

**The pattern in the failures is worth more than any one of them.** Four of the five sit in the **godparent or parent slot**, and three break the surname **across a line**, where the reader's eye finishes the word from expectation. **A hyphenated surname at a line break is the single most dangerous place on the page.** The fifth failure is different and nastier: frame 99's trap was the **forename** *Francisci*, not the surname at all.

**Still unread: frames 108–134 of this volume, and images 1–154 of the 1709–1764 volume.**

rows.src: Frames 108-112: the register names Euphemia as Vittorio's wife, and Antonio turns out to have a daughter Maria
rows.what: Svetvinčenat baptisms 1764–1791, film 005497885 — frames 108–112
rows.got:
**Two findings here are worth more than the eighteen frames that produced them.**

**The first moves a marriage from an index to a read act.** Frame 110, **22 August 1785**:

> *«Patrini fuere Antonius Radocovich, et **Evphemia Vxor Victoris de Franceschi**.»*

**«Vittorio × Euphemia» had rested entirely on one FamilySearch index line** — the 1784 baptism of their daughter Maria Matthia, *«parents Victorii De Franceschi & Euphemię»*. An index is a transcription of a page somebody else read. **This is the page.** *(doc.)*

It also resolves frame 101's *«Antonivs de Franceschi, et Evphemia **pariter** de Franceschi»*: the same parish, the same two years, the same woman. **Antonio stood at that font beside his own daughter-in-law.** *(inf — but the alternative needs two Euphemias married into one small family in one small parish.)*

**The second adds a person to the family.** Frame 112, **18 January 1786**:

> *«Antonius filius legitimus ac naturalis Thomae, et Catharinae jugalium Bercan natus heri … **Patrini fuere Matthaeus Doblanovich, et Maria filia Antonii de Franceschi**.»*

**Maria, daughter of Antonio** — a fifth child beside Vittorio, Franca, Domenica and Domenico, and **in none of this archive's files before this line.** *(doc.)*

**Her baptism is not where it ought to be.** A girl asked to stand godmother in January 1786 is rarely under fifteen, which would put her birth at or before about 1771 — **and frames 5–60, covering 1764 to 1775, have been read opening by opening with no Maria of Antonio in them.** Either she was born before 1764, in the volume whose first 154 images are still unread, or the sweep missed her. **No birth year is recorded for her**, because an age reasoned backwards from a godmother's minimum age is a guess wearing arithmetic's clothes.

**Antonio's children have taken over his office.** Through the 1770s it was Antonio the bell-ringer in the godparent line. By 1785–86 it is **Vittorio** (30 July 1785, 13 December 1785), **Euphemia his wife** (22 August 1785) and **Maria his daughter** (18 January 1786).

### A sixth decoy, and it is the forename again

Frame 112, 20 January 1786, two entries from our own: *«Antonius Zambiasio, et **Euphemia Vxor Matthei Bullesich**»*. **A second Euphemia on the same leaf** — exactly the trap that *«Fosca uxor Martini Merklem»* set on frame 98. **In this parish both Fosca and Euphemia are common forenames.** Only the full *«uxor + the husband's whole name»* form identifies anybody; the forename alone identifies a coincidence.

**One reading corrected inside this sweep.** Frame 112's 13 December 1785 godfather was read at spread scale as *Antonius* de Franceschi. Magnified, it is **Victorius**. Father and son have similar-length names in this hand.

**Still unread: frames 113–134 of this volume, and images 1–154 of the 1709–1764 volume.**

rows.src: The Svetvincenat baptism volume 1764-1791 read to its last leaf -- and what a complete volume is worth
rows.what: Svetvinčenat baptisms 1764–1791, film 005497885 — frames 113–131, completing the volume
rows.got:
**Every opening of this volume has now been read — frames 5 to 131, the whole of 1764 to 1791.** The register closes on 28 May 1791 with the archpriest's own tally; frames 132–134 are the microfilm's target boards, not pages.

**The completeness is the finding.** A negative from a volume read frame by frame is evidence. A negative from a volume searched by index is nothing at all.

### What the name does in this book

**It stands at other people's fonts, constantly, and it almost never appears as a parent.** In twenty-seven years there are **six baptisms** of the surname — Franca (1769), Pasqua Vittoria (1773), Domenica (1776), Domenico (1777), Giovanni (1778) and Maria Matthia (1784) — and well over **sixty** appearances as godparent. That shape is what a settled, respectable, and *small* family looks like in a parish register.

### The people this volume establishes

- **Antonio**, the bell-ringer, *Dnus*, alive from before 1769 to **12 October 1788** (magnified) — about fifty-eight at the last sighting.
- **Mattea**, his wife, 1 May 1780 to **18 August 1782** (magnified).
- **Vittorio, his son**, called *«filius Antonii»* in **1773, 1782 and 1787** — three independent entries, plus the 1812 burial's `kin: Antonio`. The most-named man of the surname in the book.
- **Euphemia, Vittorio's wife**, named in full — *«uxor Victorii de Franceschi»* — on 22 August 1785, four times in six weeks in early 1787, and last on **15 January 1791**.
- **Maria, Antonio's daughter**, 18 January 1786 and 30 September 1787, the second adding *«ex hac Parochia»*.
- **Domenico**, *Dnus*, and his wife **Fosca** — she is the parish's standing godmother, in eight-plus entries across 1780–1789.

### The act this sweep missed, and how it was recovered

**Reading all 127 openings, I did not see the one baptism that mattered most — and the index did.** The FamilySearch index entry for *Maria Matthia De Franceschi* carries the image ark **3:1:3QS7-L99X-K3FV**, which is **frame 106 — a frame this sweep had already read and passed over.** Going back to it with a narrow crop:

> *«**Anno Dni 1784 Die 4 Septembris.** Maria Matthia filia legitima, ac naturalis **Victorii, et Euphemiæ jugalium De Franceschi**, nata 3 currentis, hodie per me subscriptum baptizata. Patrini fuere Stephanus Dubglich a Dimino, et Dna Antonia Fachinetti.»*

**Maria Matthia, daughter of Vittorio and Euphemia De Franceschi, born 3 September 1784, baptised the next day.** *(doc — the act itself, not the index of it.)*

**This is the only baptism of Vittorio's line on these leaves**, and it makes the couple a documented marriage rather than an inferred one. The godmother, *Dna Antonia Fachinetti*, is of the parish gentry; the godfather comes from Dvigrad.

**The honest account of how it was found is the useful part.** A frame-by-frame sweep is not a guarantee. Eleven consecutive entries in one column at spread scale is exactly where attention fails, and this act sat in the eleventh. **The index caught what the reading missed; the reading then proved what the index only asserted.** Neither method was sufficient alone. See [/corrections/](/corrections/).

### What this volume genuinely does not contain

**There is no baptism for Maria, Antonio's daughter.** Frames 5–60 cover 1764–1775 continuously and she is not in them. She was likely born before 1764, in the earlier volume — **whose first 154 images remain unread.** *(open.)*

### The clerk's ear

Domenico's wife is written **Fosca, Fusca, Jusca, Justa** and **Julia** across ten years. One woman, one household. A reader in a hurry would make three of her.

### Eight decoys, and the pattern in them

| frame | looked like | reads |
|---|---|---|
| 86 | Dominici **Defranceschi** | Dominici **Brasich** |
| 91 | Antonij **Defranczo** | Antonij **Bergamo** |
| 99 | a de Franceschi | filia q.m **Francisci Zabrza** |
| 104 | Catharina filia Dominici **de Fra…** | **de Paz ex Rubino** |
| 98 | «Fosca» | Fosca **uxor Martini Merklem** |
| 112 | «Euphemia» | Euphemia **uxor Matthei Bullesich** |
| 112 | **Antonius** de Franceschi | **Victorius** de Franceschi |
| 122 | **Dominici et Euphemiae jugalium Franceschi** | jugalium **BROZINA** |

**Frame 122 is the one to remember.** At spread scale it read as a baptism of a child to *Dominicus and Euphemia* — the two exact forenames this family uses — which would have been a genuine act, the first in two hundred frames. The surname is **Brozina**. **The forenames did all the persuading; the eye supplied the rest.**

**And frame 120 taught the sharpest lesson of the sweep.** It appeared to read *«Dna Helena uxor Dni Dominici Franceschi»* — which would have **overturned** Fosca and implied a remarriage. Magnified, it is *«Dnus Sebastianus Defilipo, et Dna Aglaes uxor Dni Benedicti Fiorenci»*. Neither name is ours. **A reading that would overturn an established fact is not a discovery until it is magnified. It is a warning.**

**Still unread: images 1–154 of the 1709–1764 volume.**

rows.src: Ruža's parents are not reachable through FamilySearch — Fužine is not in the index for this surname
rows.what: FamilySearch record search — Hreljac at Fužine, and the 1918–1926 window, tested three ways
rows.got:
**Worklist item 71.** Ruža Hreljac was born at **Fužine on 13 February 1922**; her parents **Lovre Hreljac** and **Dragica Vlahović** are in David's live tree, both deceased, and neither is in this archive. The question was whether FamilySearch could supply them. **It cannot, and the reason is coverage rather than bad luck.**

| query (exact surname) | result |
|---|---|
| Hreljac · Croatia · born 1918–1926 | **0** |
| Hreljac · Croatia, no date filter | **340** |
| Hreljac · place Fužine | 9 — **and not one of them is a Fužine record** |

**The indexed Hreljac records sit at Grižane and Lussinpiccolo**, with the rest in emigration sets — US World War II draft cards, Ellis Island passenger lists. The nine that answer to «Fužine» are fuzzy place matches with the word appearing nowhere on the page. **Fužine's own registers are not in this index.**

**The zero was tested before it was believed, and this is the part worth keeping.** A stable zero from a record search is not evidence on its own: a signed-out session returns the same zero as a genuine absence, and the search says nothing about which it is. Deleting one parameter — the date range — turned 0 into **340**, which proves the service was answering at that moment. The absence is real. *(The test comes from the Lerena session, which lost most of an afternoon to zeros before catching that the surname González returned none in Uruguay.)*

**So the route changes.** Ruža's parents will not come from an index. They have to come from **the Fužine parish register itself**, or from the **Rijeka state archive**, which already holds an open request on this archive's list for the Klenovica and Ledenice books. Fužine belongs to the same archive and the same era, and should join that enquiry rather than starting a new one. *(doc, for the negative; the redirection is a judgement.)*

rows.src: Rotilio's marriage found at Trieste — and the archive owes the reunion album an apology
rows.what: FamilySearch full-text search — «Rotilio Defranceschi», which reached the Trieste marriage proclamations of 1928
rows.got:
**Work list item 125, and it went the opposite way to the one this archive expected.**

The question was *«the name of the woman Rotilio actually married»*, asked because [the Eleven](/the-eleven/) had concluded the 2012 reunion album gave him **his sister's husband's surname**. The answer came from **FamilySearch full-text search** — a service [item 87](/worklist/) records as never having been tried here — on the plain query *Rotilio Defranceschi*.

**Trieste, Marriage Proclamation Records 1928, Parte II Serie A, numero 132:**

> *«…il sottoscritto Ufficiale dello Stato Civile del Comune di **Pisino** … procedere alle publicazioni del matrimonio che sarà davanti a lui celebrato fra **Defranceschi Rotilo, celibe, di professione chauffeur, nato a Gallignana**, residente in Gallignana, d'età maggiore, **figlio di fu Antonio, di professione muratore**, residente in vita in Gallignana, **e di Valhart Maria**, di professione casalinga … **Cincopan Albina, nubile, di professione casalinga, nata a Gallignana**, residente in Gallignana, di età maggiore, **figlia di Giuseppe, di professione agricoltore** … **e di Trompich Maria**, di professione casalinga, residente in Gallignana…»*

**Rotilio married an Albina Cincopan of his own village.** *Cincopan* and *Chinkopan* are one surname. His sister Albina separately married Frank Chinkopan and died at Brooklyn in 1945. **Both marriages happened.** The album was right, David's tree was right to carry two Albinas, and [the inference published here](/corrections/) was wrong.

**What the document adds beyond the name:**

- **Rotilio was a chauffeur** — the first trade recorded for him.
- **His father Antonio was a *muratore*, a mason, and was dead by April 1928.** His mother **Maria Valhart** was alive, at Gallignana. Both match Albina's Brooklyn death certificate independently, which is what confirms this is the right Rotilio.
- **The bride's parents: Giuseppe Cincopan, farmer, and Maria Trompich** — two people new to this archive.
- **The wedding belonged to Pisino**, not Gračišće: the request came from the *Comune di Pisino*. The banns ran at Trieste as well *«ove la sposa ha avuto la residenza»* — **Albina had lived in Trieste.** That is a new place to search, and the reason this record exists at all.
- Dates: requested 27 April, posted at Trieste 29 April and 6 May 1928. The Gračišće register's **16 May 1928** sits exactly where a third banns and a wedding should.

**Argentina remains unevidenced.** The album's «left for Buenos Aires with two daughters» is the only part of its account still standing without a document, and David's tree's «died at Buenos Aires» with it.

**A note on where this came from.** Full-text search reads the handwriting of unindexed registers, which is why a plain two-word query reached a document no name index contains. It had never been run here. It should now be run against every open question on this list.

rows.src: What full-text search can and cannot reach — the boundary, measured rather than assumed
rows.what: FamilySearch full-text — coverage measured by sampling 97 collections, and the phrase-quoting rule
rows.got:
**Full-text search answered [item 125](/worklist/) on its first query, so the next question is how much else it can answer. The boundary turns out to be sharp, and it is geographic.**

**Sampling its own results.** The query *Defranceschi* returns **3,967** documents. Reading the collection line off 97 of them:

| region | collections |
|---|---|
| Emilia-Romagna | 70 |
| Friuli Venezia Giulia · Lombardy | 12 |
| Sardinia · Veneto · Marche | 11 |
| Piedmont · Sicily · West Virginia | 3 |
