rows.src: The pier's own construction file — and my best candidate for it got weaker
rows.what: Hungaricana + the City of Rijeka's port history — who is the «De Francescijev gat» named for? (item 157)
ev: The pier, and the candidate demoted
Ferencz Defranceschi of the Fiume Maritime Authority
Where the pier lives until a document ties it to somebody
rows.got:
**Asked properly for the first time. The pier gained a construction file; the best candidate lost ground.**

**Nil, with the exact terms named** *(on Hungaricana, where Fiume's officials actually live)*:

| term | hits |
|---|---|
| `"Defranceschi" móló` | **0** |
| `"Defranceschi" gát` | **0** |
| `"molo Defranceschi"` | **0** |
| `"molo De Franceschi"` | **0** |
| `"De Franceschi" móló` | **0** |
| *control* `Defranceschi révkapitány` | **5** |
| *control* `Defranceschi kikötő` | **1** |

**The controls pass in the same minutes**, so the zeros are real. *But they are **weak** evidence: this portal records pensions and salaries, not quaysides.*

**What was gained.** *The City of Rijeka's own port history places the pier in a single building programme: «**nasipavanjem zapadne obale izgrađeno je Istarsko, Bečko, Budimpeštansko i Praško pristanište te De Francheschijev i Visinov gat**» — to the designs of **Antal Hajnal**, chief engineer of the Hungarian royal port office. **Four wharves named for places, two gats named for people.** Warehouse 17 on the Visinov gat dates the set in use: **1906–07, Ferenc Pfaff**. ⚠ **The page does not say who either man was.*** *(doc for the grouping.)*

**⚠ What was lost.** *The **Budapesti utasító of 1848** (p. 70) shows the **Fiume harbour captaincy held by «Kapitány Sgardelli Alajos»**, while **«Főnök Defranceschi Ferencz»** ran the **quarantine institute at Martinšćica**. His «révkapitány» title appears only at his 1857 pensioning, filed under «**Fiumei tengerészeti hatóság**» — **the authority for the whole Hungarian Littoral, not a posting**.*

**So «port captain of Fiume» is withdrawn as a description of him**, and the intuition that carried him as the pier's eponym — the port official on the spot when the port was built — is not available: **Hajnal's programme is decades after he retired.** *He is not eliminated. He is no longer the comfortable answer.* **(open.)**

*Still unrun: Državni arhiv u Rijeci, the city's quay-renaming decrees, the Italian-era port plans 1924–45. The Lučka uprava chronology returned **HTTP 520** today.*

rows.src: The port authority's own chronology names no pier of that era
rows.what: Lučka uprava Rijeka — «Luka kroz povijest», the full chronology 1717–2025 (item 157, retried)
ev: The pier, and what the chronology does and does not give
rows.got:
**Retried at David's word, and it is a nil — but a clean, exhausting one.**

*The page returns **HTTP 520** to a fetcher, twice. **It loads normally in a browser**, which is how it was read: the whole chronology, **1717 to 2025**, is on one page.*

**⚠ It names no pier of the Hungarian era at all.** *Searched the full text for `gat`, `pristani`, `Zichy`, `Franceschi`, `Francheschi`, `Hajnal`, `Visinov`, `molo`, `lukobran`, `obal`. **The first quay the chronology names is «Orlandov gat», in 2013.*** *So the port authority's own public history does not carry the pier's name, and this route is now **exhausted rather than untried**.*

**What it gives instead is a frame, and one date that matters.**

| year | verbatim |
|---|---|
| **1855** | *«Započinju prvi radovi na izgradnji suvremene riječke luke premještanjem ušća Rječine u novo korito»* |
| **1867** | *the great basin begun; «Rijeka postaje glavna postaja za izlaz mađarskog gospodarstva u svijet»* |
| **⚠ 1941–45** | *«Njemačka vojska je prilikom povlačenja iz riječke luke **porušila sve vezove za prihvat brodova**… i više od 50% skladišnih kapaciteta»* |

**1867 opens the frame Hajnal's programme sits in — ten years after [Ferencz](/rijeka/) had already retired**, which is consistent with this morning's demotion of him.

**⚠ And 1941–45 sharpens the naming question.** *Every berth in the port was destroyed on the German withdrawal, and reconstruction followed in 1950. **A port rebuilt from nothing is exactly when quays get renamed**, and «De Franceschi**jev**» is a Croatian possessive — the form a post-1945 naming would take.* **Against it**: *the City of Rijeka attributes the gat name to Hajnal's Hungarian-era programme.* **Both are doc; neither inference is drawn.** *(nil for the name; the dates are the gain.)*

rows.src: Jacobo's son found, Antonia's death bracketed, and five Carnians counted
rows.what: Svetvinčenat marriages, film 005497886 frames 94–96 (1783–1784) — read frame by frame
ev: The Svetvinčenat line — 1784 in the story
Zuanne, son of the late Giacomo, m. 19 July 1784
rows.got:
**Resumed after the sign-out. Three frames, two findings, and a pattern that can now be counted.**

| frame | carta | date | what |
|---|---|---|---|
| 94 | 51 | Jul–Nov 1783 | nil for the name — *but a Carnian: **Giacomo Puspil q. Mattio, «nato nella Villa di Prato in Carnia Diocesi di Udine»**, 9 Oct* |
| 95 | 52 | Nov 1783 – Feb 1784 | nil; **«Fine dell'Anno 1783: Matrimonij N.o 26»** |
| **96** | 53 | **21 Feb 1784** | **Gio: Batta Steffanutto, «nativo della Carnia», «vedovo della q. Antonia nata de Franceschi»**, remarries |
| **96** | 53 | **19 Jul 1784** | **Zuanne figlio del q. Giacomo de Franceschi** × Antonia, daughter of the late Antonio |

**Zuanne is the first son of Jacobo's household the marriage book has named.** *This line knew it only through its women.* **⚠ But he is not assigned a father**: *the castle's Giacomo is the one this archive files as «at least two men», and the act does not decide which — only that his father was a Giacomo de Franceschi of this parish, dead by 1784.*

**Antonia is dead, and named.** *«**nata de Franceschi**» settles what the 1779 act left to a patronymic. **Bracket 7 Jan 1779 × 21 Feb 1784**, at thirty-six or younger; no year printable. Third woman on this line whose death is known only from her widower's next wedding.*

**⚠ Open, and deliberately not resolved:** *the new bride is «Angiola relitta q. Domenico **Galluzzi**»; Antonia's mother Pascasia had remarried a **Calluzzi**. One letter in one hand. Recorded, not claimed.*

**The Carnian count, read forward off this film: five in ten years** — *Corva (1774), Stefanuto (1779, and again 1784), Colla × Verona (1782), Puspil (1783). Two name the diocese of Udine; two name the village — **Muina** and **Prato**, both in the upper Degano, a few miles apart.* **That the parish kept marrying along the Carnian road is doc. That the Defranceschi came down it is not proved by these acts and is not claimed.**

**Frame 97 read 29 September — nil.** *Carta 54, October 1784 to January 1785; **«Fine dell'Anno 1784: Matrimonij N.o 14»**. ⚠ Two of its acts are again celebrated away from the parish church — one at **Castel S. Lorenzo** by licence to that pievano, one in **the church of S. Rocco** — which is the [rule this film has now earned twice over](/method/).*

rows.src: A database named as a route two weeks ago, opened at last — and a man of Gologorica died at Dachau
rows.what: Muzej žrtava genocida, Belgrade — the Yugoslav victims' census (baza.muzejgenocida.rs), every spelling of the name
ev: Anton Defrančeški of Gologorica, died Dachau 1944
rows.got:
**David asked whether this archive had ever searched it. It had not — and it had already written down that it should.**

*The [Arolsen search of 16 September](/searched/) for **Anka Nera Defranceski** ended by naming two remaining routes, «the Belgrade city registry and the **Yugoslav victims' census** at the Museum of Genocide Victims, **neither of which this archive has opened**». **It stayed unopened for a fortnight until the question was asked.*** *A route named in a search log is not a route run.*

**659,122 records. Three of the name, all new to this archive.**

| name | father | born | of | died | where | the register's «okolnost» |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Anton Defrančeški** | Anton | 1909 | **Gologorica** *(Pazin)* | **15.07.1944** | **Dachau** | **logor** — camp; perpetrator **nemci** |
| **Antonio Defranceschi** | Domenico | 1925 | **Vodnjan** *(Pula)* | 05.05.1944 | Sv. Foška, Vodnjan | NOB i savezničke vojne formacije; perpetrator **unknown** |
| **Armando Defranceschi** | Gonanni | 1928 | **Vodnjan** *(Pula)* | 05.05.1945 | Mune | NOB i savezničke vojne formacije; perpetrator **unknown** |

**⚠ Anton was born in the parish this archive begins in**, and on **6 April 1941**, the day the Axis invaded Yugoslavia, he was still living there. *He was thirty-two; he was dead at Dachau three years and three months later.* **No descent is claimed** — his father was also Anton, and joining him to the Gologorica household the archive holds is work for the Gračišće and Gologorica registers, not for a victims' index.

**⚠ The Vodnjan two are reported in the register's own words and not characterised further.** *«NOB i savezničke vojne formacije» is the compiling institution's classification, its perpetrator column says **unknown**, and the classification of Istrian deaths of 1943–45 is contested ground on which that institution is a party. **A one-name study records the entry and does not settle the argument.***

**The nil that matters: [Anka Nera Defranceski](/worklist/) is not in this database.** *Seven spellings tried, none returns her.* **One of item 53's two remaining routes is now closed, with a negative.**

**Terms tried, and the counts, on clean page loads:**

| term | hits |
|---|---|
| `Defranceski` | **1** — Anton, and the base stores him as «Defrančeški» |
| `Defranceschi` | **2** — Antonio, Armando |
| `Defranćeski` | **1** — Anton again |
| `De Franceschi` | 0 |
| `Franceschi` | 0 |
| `Franceski` | 0 |
| `Defrančeski` | 0 |

**⚠ Two traps in this database, both of which nearly produced a false result here.**

**·** **The surname field is exact, not substring.** *`Franceschi` returns **0** while `Defranceschi` returns 2 — so a search on the bare stem finds nothing and every prefix must be tried on its own.*
**·** **A query with Croatian diacritics silently returns the whole base.** *`Defrančeški` and `Franceški` both report **659,122** — the unfiltered total. **That is not a result, it is the query being ignored**, and read carelessly it looks like a spectacular hit. The base folds diacritics on its own side, so the ASCII form is the one to send.*
**·** *And the React front end races: reset-and-refill in a loop renders a **previous query's rows** under a new query's count. One run showed «Ante Frančeskini» under `Defranceski`. **Every count above was re-taken one query per page load.***

rows.got:
**The answer is no, and getting to it meant taking apart a match that looked perfect.**

**What Arolsen shows first:** *«**DEFRANCESCHI, ANTONIO — 31 January 1909 — prisoner 8165**», personal file at **Natzweiler**. Same surname, same birth year, the camp system, and this archive looking for a man who died at Dachau.* **Written up at that point it would have been wrong.**

**⚠ That record is an ITS cross-reference card, not a document about a person.** *Ref **01012902 008.453** — an *Ersatzkarte* reading «DEFRANCESCHI, Antonio 31.1.1909 — **see: DEFRANCESCO**», recto only, verso blank.*

**The real file is under DEFRANCESCO, and it disproves the match four times over:**

| document | what it says |
|---|---|
| Dachau file card, T/D **400385** | «DEFRANCESCO, Antonio · 31.1.1909 · **Moncalvo** · Häftl.-Nr. 98542/64488» |
| arrival card | «64 488 · **Sch.It.** · Defrancesco Antonio 31.1.09 · **Moncalvo** · **28.2.44**» |
| transfer letter, Dachau 1[?].3.44 | *«Der Vorbeugungsgefangene DEFRANCESCO Antonio … wurde am **13.3.44** … vom KL Dachau in das **KL Natzweiler** überstellt»* — copied to **Sipo Triest** |
| death report | **«Abgang durch Tod!»** — Häftlingskrankenbau, **7 February 1945**, «geboren 31.1.09 zu **Moncalvo**», Block 30, **gestorben 7. Februar 1945 um 6.45 Uhr**, myocarditis |

**Moncalvo is in Piedmont.** *Two hundred miles from Istria, written on four separate documents by different clerks.*

| | **the Gologorica man** | **the Arolsen man** |
|---|---|---|
| surname | Defrančeški | **Defrancesco** |
| born | 1909, **Gologorica** | 31 Jan 1909, **Moncalvo** |
| died | **15 July 1944** | **7 February 1945** |

**A birth year and a camp. That is the whole of the resemblance.** *(doc for the disproof.)*

**⚠ The detail that made him look right, recorded and not resolved:** *the Arolsen man's committing authority was **Sipo Trieste**, and the Dachau entry register gives his nationality as «**ITALIAN, YUGOSLAVIAN**» — markers of the Adriatic Littoral, not Piedmont. **The birthplace is written four times and governs**; the oddity is noted and left.*

**Terms tried on Arolsen, with counts:** *`Defranceschi` → **38 people, 9 archival units**; `Defranceski` → **79**; `Defrancesco Antonio` → **8**. **None is born in 1909 at an Istrian place.*** *The 79 under `Defranceski` were [catalogued on 17 September](/searched/) as one family, the Pfullingen household.*

**So the Belgrade victims' census remains the only record of Anton Defrančeški this archive has found.** *Question 2 of [item 160](/worklist/) — whether he descends from the Gologorica household — is untouched and stays open; it needs the Gračišće and Gologorica baptisms of about 1909.*

**⚠ And the search turned up something for a different item.** *The IRO «CM/1 files originating in Italy» hold a **Dignano — Vodnjan — household of the name**: **GIUSEPPE b. 1 Sept 1904 at Dignano**, **GIOVANNA née BORTOLUSSI b. 26 July 1911 at Dignano**, **GIORDANA b. 1937**, **MARIA b. 1939**, and **STEFANO**; with **LIVIO b. 4 Aug 1925 at Pola** and a Trieste group beside them. **[The two Vodnjan men found yesterday](/lines/) are not these people**, but they are the same town in the same decade, and this is where a Vodnjan line would be worked.*

rows.src: The Gologorica baptisms of 1909 are not online, and the book that holds them has an address
rows.what: Where a Gologorica baptism of about 1909 actually is — FamilySearch, DAPA, BA Poreč, Hrčak (item 160, question 2)
ev: Anton Defrančeški — the man this would place
rows.got:
**Asked to read the Gologorica baptisms of about 1909. They cannot be read from here, and establishing that corrected this archive's own claim of a few hours earlier.**

**⚠ First, the correction.** *Item 160 said the baptisms were «**on film** and readable the same way the Svetvinčenat marriages were». **They are not.** This archive's own `waypoints.json` records a walk of **FamilySearch's «Croatia, Church Books 1516–1994» in September 2026** and lists **Gologorica, Gračišće and Pićan** among the **absent** parishes. **The route was named without opening a file already held here.** [Recorded on /corrections/.](/corrections/)*

**Where the book actually is.** *From the DAPA register inventory this archive already holds:*

> **DAPA no. 1166 — Gologorica — MKR (rođeni, baptisms) — 1880–1948 — held at BA Poreč — digitised: yes**

*So a 1909 baptism sits in a volume at the **Biskupijski arhiv**, the archive of the **Poreč-Pula diocese** — not at Pazin, not at the parish. The **1880–1948** span means one book covers it.*

**What DAPA itself says**, read from its own page today: *it will **not** undertake «opsežna genealoška istraživanja» or searches where the requester lacks name, approximate period and place — **but this request has all three** — and it notes that «neke matične knjige su digitalizirane i dostupne su na stranici www.familysearch.org».* **For this parish that last sentence does not help**, which is the whole finding.

**The contact, so the errand is actionable:** *Biskupijski arhiv, **Dobrilina 3, 52440 Poreč**; archivist **Branka Poropat**, **ppbarhiv@gmail.com**, **+385 52 635 418**; ordinariate **biskupija@ppb.hr**. The diocesan archive's own description gives it registers **from 1827 onwards** plus an Istrian parish collection 1663–1825.*

**⚠ Two routes closed today and both are named rather than summarised.**

**·** **Hrčak — blocked by a bot check.** *The Trogrlić article «Gologorica u Kronici Župe (1892.–1918.)» covers exactly these years and is open access. `curl` gets **HTTP 418**; the browser reaches the PDF link and is served **«Confirm you're not a robot»**. **This archive does not work around bot checks.** It is [David's to fetch](/errands/), and it is a click for a person.*
**·** **The FamilySearch catalogue** returned **«Something Went Wrong»** on every query today — *a service fault, recorded as neither confirmation nor contradiction of the September walk.*

**⚠ And a small integrity fault found on the way.** *`sources.json` claims the Trogrlić PDF is **held** at `articles/Trogrlic - Gologorica u Kronici Zupe 1892-1918, VIA 32.pdf`. **There is no such file, and no `articles/` directory.** The claim is corrected to «not held».*

**So question 2 of item 160 — is Anton ours — cannot be answered from a desk.** *It needs one letter to one archive for one named person in one book.* **(blocked, on David.)**

rows.src: Two photographs from the Gračišće plot, and the stone disagrees with the chart
rows.what: The De Franceschi–Marfan plot at Gračišće, re-read from David's photographs of 29 September 2026
ev: The plot, and the three death years
Virginija — her death date finally on her own record
The withdrawn reading of Antonio's line
rows.got:
**David asked whether this plot had been seen. It had — in full, since the day it was first photographed. What the new pictures change is three things the old ones could not.**

**1 · The Marfan stone had been described without a single date. Now it has four.** *«**F. MARFAN — MAFALDA ✱ 3. II. 1928 ✝ 17. XI. 1974 — IVAN ✱ 23. VIII. 1904 ✝ 28. II. 1986**», dedicated «GENITORI, FRATELLO E SORELLE POSERO».* **(doc.)** *⚠ The relationships are **inference**: Ivan is the Croatian Giovanni and the chart says Virginija married a Giovanni Marfan; both she (d. 1981) and he (d. 1986) were alive when Mafalda died in 1974, and the chart gives her four children. **No document read here names Mafalda's parents.***

**2 · ⚠ Antonio's dates, and a correction to this archive.** *It had read the worn line as «185[5 or 6] – 19[2]4» and said it «does nothing to contradict» the American chart — **bracketing the illegible digits towards what it already believed**. **David read the stone on site: 1855 – 1921.*** **[Withdrawn.](/corrections/)**

*And withdrawing it surfaced something already on the page: the parish Status Animarum gives «Antonius Defranceschi … 6-8-1856 … **† 23-10-1929**», against the chart's **23 October 1924**. **Same birth, same death day, five years apart in the year** — the shape of a one-digit copying error, printed beside each other for weeks with no one remarking on it.*

| source | born | died |
|---|---|---|
| **the stone** *(David, on site)* | **1855** | **1921** |
| the American chart, 2012 | 6 Aug 1856 | 23 Oct **1924** |
| parish Status Animarum | 6 Aug 1856 | 23 Oct **1929** |

**Three death years. This archive asserts none of them.** *What settles it is the Gračišće death register, or the obelisk in raking light.*

*Maria's death day moves from **3 X** to **8 X 1945** — 3 and 8, the classic pair on worn stone. **Her birth of 6 April 1867 is confirmed three independent ways and is not in doubt.***

**3 · ⚠ A propagation failure caught by a photograph.** *Virginija's death, **28 December 1981**, had been published on [the eleven](/the-eleven/) for weeks. **Her roster record still carried `d = null`.*** *And **Nazarijo, Mafalda and Ivan had no records at all** despite being written about on that page.* **All four now have their own pages.** *A finding is not done until it is in every file that asserts it — [the archive's own rule](/method/), broken here by the archive.*

rows.src: The tomb at Gologorica, and the word that undid this morning's disproof
rows.what: The de Franceschi family tomb, Armella's cross and a broken Flegar slab in the cemetery at Gologorica — twelve photographs from David
ev: The tomb, the arms and the ouroboros
Maria Micheli — Carlo's wife, named at last
Silvia — a de Franceschi who married a de Franceschi
Franjo Flegar, on a broken Slovenian slab
Moncalvo is Gologorica — the disproof withdrawn
rows.got:
**Twelve photographs of the churchyard at Gologorica. Three people new, five pages corrected or filled — and one word that undid a piece of this morning's work.**

**⚠ THE WORD IS «MONCALVO».** *Three of the tablets use it: Silvia born there 1872, Pietro dead there 1884, Giulio dead there 1942. **Moncalvo is the Italian name of Gologorica** — this archive's own page says «Gologorica is the bare hill in Croatian; Moncalvo is the same thing in Italian», and the word is in **thirty-three** of its files.*

**This morning this archive used «Moncalvo is in Piedmont, two hundred miles from Istria» to disprove that Arolsen's «DEFRANCESCO, Antonio, born 31.1.1909 zu Moncalvo, died Dachau» could be [the Anton Defrančeški born 1909 at Gologorica](/person/anton-defranceski-of-gologorica-1909-1944-1909/).** **The disproof is withdrawn.** *And the two details recorded as puzzling — committed by **Sipo Trieste**, registered «**ITALIAN, YUGOSLAVIAN**» — stop being puzzling: they are what an Istrian looks like in a German camp register.* **[On /corrections/.](/corrections/)** *The death dates still differ, 15 July 1944 against 7 February 1945, and the archive now says «very probably one man» and not more.*

**NEW FROM THE TABLETS**

| | on the stone |
|---|---|
| **Maria Micheli** | *moglie di Carlo* — **Pisino 1828 – Parenzo 1880**. **The historian's wife, and this archive had never had her maiden name.** |
| **Pietro fu Carlo** | *magistrato* — **Rovigno 1854 – Moncalvo 1884**, dead at thirty |
| **Silvia de Franceschi fu Francesco** | *moglie di Camillo* — **Moncalvo 1872 – Pola 1938**; **a de Franceschi who married the de Franceschi Camillo** |
| **Franjo Flegar** | **✱ 2.3.1872 ✝ 19.10.1940**, on a slab broken across the top, closing «**LAHKA IN BILA ZEMLJA**» — **Slovenian** |

**FILLED OR CORRECTED**

*· **Carlo**'s own tablet: «STORIOGRAFO DELL'ISTRIA — STRENUO ASSERTORE DELL'ITALIANITÀ DELLA SUA TERRA — MDCCCIX–MDCCCXCIII».*
*· **Giulio** gains a death year, **1942**, and a trade — «**pittore accademico**». He is also the «marito Giulio» who raised **Armella's** cross.*
*· **Virginia** gains her birthplace, **Fiume**; the record had only Poreč, where she died.*
*· ⚠ **Faustina**: the tablet cuts **Parenzo 1864**, this archive carries **1863**. **Neither is overwritten**; the Parenzo baptisms settle it.*

**THE ARMS, DESCRIBED AND NOT BLAZONED.** *A shield with a **Latin cross**, a diagonal device behind it, a rounded charge at the foot below a horizontal division, under a **coronet of five pearls**. A second, far more worn version is cut on a stone urn in the same plot. ⚠ And set into the wall above the centre tablet, an **ouroboros** — a serpent biting its own tail. **No blazon is attempted**: [item 133](/worklist/) is the errand for the Wappenkopie of 13 May 1825 in the Austrian nobility archive, and a photograph describes, it does not blazon.*

**⚠ Four of Carlo's household died before he did** — *his wife and three children, on the two tablets flanking his own.*

rows.src: Thirty-seven Carnian stones turned into people — and two Isidoros
rows.what: The cemeteries of Ovaro, Mione, Muina and Agrons — thirty-five photographs from David, read and entered as records
ev: The Carnian stones, in the story
The elder Sebastiano Soravito de Franceschi
rows.got:
**David asked whether these were held. The names were; the people were not.**

*Checked first, as the rule requires: **every name in the photographs already appeared** somewhere in `carnia.json`, `walk.json` or `plates.json`. **Almost none of them had a record.*** *Mirai, Giorgis, Dell'Oste, Cecconi, Isidoro, Liduina — `roster: []`. Anzola, Regina and Vittorio matched only **different people** of those names.* **It was the [Marfan failure](/corrections/) at ten times the scale: described on a topic page, invisible as people.**

**Thirty-two entered, with their dates.** *Two Soravito de Franceschi and their wives; six daughters buried under husbands' names; two war dead; Agostino of 1833 whose stone is being lost under a newer one; and eleven more.*

**⚠ Three findings that are more than a transcription.**

**·** **Corrado and Egidio were both born 11 February 1944.** *Two stones, same surname, same day. **Twins**, as an inference and not a fact.*
**·** **A second Egidio heads the civilian list on both war memorials, killed 1–2 November 1944** — *nine months after the other was born, and very possibly the reason that child had the name.* **What happened on those two days is not characterised here.**
**·** **Isidoro is «disperso»** — *missing, under MILITARI. **No grave, no dates, no body.** Not in Arolsen under any spelling tried; the Yugoslav census would not hold an Italian soldier. **The Italian military records are the route and are unopened.***

**⚠ And one honest limit.** *David named four cemeteries — **Ovaro, Mione, Muina and Agrons** — and **the photographs do not say which stone stands in which**. Every record carries that caveat rather than a guess.*

*Two names run the length of this archive: **«Gio: Batta»**, the same contraction cut on the Gologorica lintel two centuries earlier; and **Corva**, the surname of the Carnian who married into Svetvinčenat in 1774.*

**⚠ Later the same day — five more, and a correction to the hour before.**

*A further photograph shows the **Muina** memorial: «IN MEMORIA DEI CADUTI IN GUERRA», sixteen names, «**INAUG. 22-8-1920 — I COMPAGNI DI MUINA POSERO**». **A First World War stone**, carrying **SOLD. DE FRANCESCHI VITTORIO** and **DE FRANCESCHI ISIDORO**.*

**So there are TWO De Franceschi Isidoro** — *this one dead by 1920, and the «disperso» of 1940–45 written up an hour earlier.* **A generation apart, and each now has his own page.** *A name on a war memorial carries no dates; where a family repeats a name, a memorial is the easiest place in the world to merge two people.* **⚠ And a Vittorio killed in that war, who is not the Vittorio of 1927–2006.**

*That stone also **names its village** — «i compagni di **Muina**» — **the only inscription in the whole set that says which of the four cemeteries it stands in.***

**Also added:** *[**Eufemia de Franceschi** 1889–1960](/person/eufemia-de-franceschi-1889-1960-1889/), on a tablet with **Augusto Pustetto 1921–1943**, photographed in uniform, and **Giobatta Pustetto 1922–1945** — **two young men dead two years apart in the war**, her sons by the order and the surname and by nothing the stone says outright. And **Maria Teresa de Franceschi ved. Fiorencis 1913–2001**, whose stone closes «**MANDI MIUTA**» — **Friulian**, the valley's own language, and a nickname.*

**Four languages now stand over this archive's graves** — *Italian at Gologorica and Umag, **Slovenian** on the broken slab against the Gologorica tomb, and **Friulian** here.* **Every one of them chosen.**

rows.src: The Kalanj graves of the Vinodol, and the question they raise about Anna
rows.what: Kalanj and Papić gravestones — Crikvenica, Novi Vinodolski and Klenovica, photographed by David
ev: Anna Kalanj — the join, given a record at last
The Defranceski grave that no longer exists
rows.got:
**David asked whether the Kalanj are any relation, and whether to store the pictures. Both answers are yes, with a boundary.**

**⚠ First, what this archive does NOT do with them.** *[`ancestors.json` already rules on it](/): «**the Kalanj line is kept in The Blažević Archive, not here**», and the same for **Papić**. **Building twenty Kalanj records here is precisely how an estate ends up with two versions of one person** — the rule this archive set for [Hedviga](/worklist/). **So: the stones are recorded, the photographs stored, and the line is not rebuilt.**

**What DOES belong here is the join — and the join had no page.** *[**Anna Kalanj**](/person/anna-kalanj-de-franceschi-1864-1936-1864/), born **3 January 1864 at Klenovica house 22**, daughter of **Josip Kalanj** and **Rosalia née Perković**, is this archive's own **great-great-grandmother** and generation four of [the direct line](/direct-line/). **She has appeared there as a wife and never had a record of her own.** It is the [Virginija failure](/corrections/) again, this time on the spine.*

**The stones, stored as five plates:**

| stone | names |
|---|---|
| **Mate** | MATE 1928–1992; and on a ledger slab beside it **KATA 1860–1942 · LUKA 1859–1944 · IVAN 1895–1957 · MARIJA 1904–1992** |
| **Albert** | MILAN 1932–1981 · MARIJA 1941–1977 · **ALBERT 1895–1945** · ANA 1899–1991 · IVICA 1926–1959 · EDUARD 1937–2012 |
| **Petar** | PETAR 1913–1971 · VERA 1917–2011 · **MILAN 1943–1944** — *an infant, about a year old* |
| **Franjo** | FRANJO 1933–2004 |
| **Kalanj–Rebrović** | MARIJA 1922–2000 · SLAVICA 1934–2000 · DUŠKO 1935–2004 |

**⚠ And one of them is worth a question rather than an answer.** *[**LUKA KALANJ 1859–1944**](/plates/) and **KATA 1860–1942** were born **five and four years before Anna**, in the same small stretch of the Vinodol.* **A brother and a sister-in-law is the obvious guess, and a guess is all it is** — *Anna's father was **Josip Kalanj**, and **no stone here names a father**.* **The Ledenice baptisms of the 1850s would settle it in an afternoon.** *(open.)*

**⚠ Papić: same boundary.** *A plaque «OBITELJI PAPIĆ — MILKA · NIKOLA · ANTONIJA» stands among Stipaničić and Vičić-Veljačić stones. **The Papić line is the Blažević Archive's** and is not built here.*

**⚠ A limit on the storing.** *Five photographs reached this session as files and are now plates. **The Papić stone, a sixth Kalanj stone (LOVRO 1906–1965 · ANA 1919–1971 · IVAN 1942–1996 · MARIJAN 1944–2009) and the Crikvenica photograph arrived inline and not as files**, so they could not be stored. **They want re-sending if they are to be kept.***

rows.src: Eleven Kalanj stones, and a sibling set around Anna's own year
rows.what: A second batch of Kalanj gravestones — Crikvenica, Novi Vinodolski and Klenovica
ev: The Kalanj page — the stones and the sibling question
rows.got:
**Five more stones, and together with the first five they make a question worth a name.**

**⚠ Four Kalanj now cluster on Anna's own generation.**

| on the stones | born |
|---|---|
| **Luka Kalanj** | **1859** – 1944 |
| **Kata** | **1860** – 1942 |
| **[Anna Kalanj](/person/anna-kalanj-de-franceschi-1864-1936-1864/)** | **1864** *(register)* |
| **Rozalija Kalanj** | **1865** – 1943 |

**⚠ And «Rozalija» is the name of Anna's own mother** — *Rosalia née Perković, of Klenovica house 22.* **A second daughter named for her mother is the commonest naming pattern there is.**

**So a sibling set is the obvious reading: Josip Kalanj and Rosalia's children, born 1859, 1860, 1864, 1865.** ⚠ *And it is still a guess. **No stone here names a father**, and this archive has spent today learning exactly what proximity is worth without a document — [a name, a year and a place are not an identification](/method/).*

**The test is cheap and specific: the LEDENICE BAPTISMS OF 1855–1870.** *Anna's own entry is number **2 of 1864**; her brothers and sisters would sit within a few pages of it, in the same book, in the same hand.* **An afternoon's reading settles four people.** *(open — the most tractable question on the Kalanj page.)*

*Rozalija's birth year is **damaged at the first digit** and was read at 5×; «865» is unambiguous and the shape before it is a 1.*

**Eleven stones are now stored as plates**, *and the line itself remains [the Blažević Archive's](https://blazevic.defranceski.com/kalanj/).*

**⚠ And a twelfth stone, with a national emblem on it.** *«**OBITELJ KALANJ — MARTIN 1905–1988 · MARTINA 1913–1995**» — a husband and wife under the masculine and feminine of one name — with a **pink stone plaque cut with the Croatian chequy shield, the šahovnica**, propped against the plot. **It is the only national emblem on any stone in this set**, and it is recorded as that and no more: a family put it there, and when or why is not on the stone.*

**⚠ Two of the twelve could not be stored.** *That one and **LOVRO 1906–1965** with Ana, Ivan and Marijan reached this session **inline rather than as files**. They want re-sending if they are to be kept.*

rows.src: Surname-distribution databases — Croatia (DZS 2011) and Italy (Cognomix)
rows.what: Item 162 said a surname atlas would decide Fernasar against Tornasar «from the armchair». Both spellings, plus Fernazar and Fornasar, tested against two national surname databases.
ev: The Fernasar page — what the databases decided and what they did not
rows.got:
**The terms tried, in full, because a nil is only worth as much as the list behind it.**

**Croatian Bureau of Statistics, «Imena i prezimena», 2011 census.** It suppresses any count below ten, so its nil reads *«manja je od 10 ili se ne pojavljuje»* — fewer than ten, **or none at all**, and it will not say which.

| tried | result |
|---|---|
| **FERNASAR** | fewer than 10, or none |
| **TORNASAR** | fewer than 10, or none |
| **FERNAZAR** | fewer than 10, or none |
| **FORNASAR** | fewer than 10, or none |
| *POROPAT* (control) | **757** |

The control matters: an Istrian surname of ordinary frequency returns a number, so the four nils are the database answering, not the database failing.

**Cognomix, «Mappe dei cognomi italiani» — about 180,000 surnames, over 90% of Italian families.**

| tried | result |
|---|---|
| **FERNASAR** | *«La ricerca non ha fornito risultati»* |
| **TORNASAR** | *«La ricerca non ha fornito risultati»* |
| **FORNASAR** | **about 25 families** |
| *DEFRANCESCHI* (control) | **about 93 families** |

**And where the 25 Fornasar families are:** Piemonte 11, **Friuli-Venezia Giulia 8**, Veneto 4, Liguria 1, Puglia 1.

**What this settles and what it does not.** It does **not** decide the letter the priest formed, and item 162's hope that it would was wrong: *neither* Fernasar *nor* Tornasar survives as a living surname in either country, so no atlas of the present can choose between them. What it does is take away Tornasar's last possible support — it exists nowhere, in either country, in any period these databases cover — while **Fornasar is real, and twelve of its twenty-five Italian families are in Friuli and the Veneto**, which is the corner of Europe whose dialect gives *fornasâr*, the man who works the kiln. That is the etymology this archive had already inferred from 49 issues of the Austrian press, and it now has a second, independent leg. *(The eleven in Piemonte are not explained here; north-western industrial migration is the obvious reading and is **inf**, not doc.)*

**This is verification, not discovery.** The question was already answered on [the married-in page](/married-in/) by the Austrian press test, which found «Tornasar» in not one issue and «Fernasar» in three, two of them casualty lists placing a Josef Fernasar at **Gračišće** — Maria's own village. Today's work is a second road to the same place.

rows.src: HDA — Zbirka dopunskih mikrofilmova matičnih knjiga (HR-HDA-1448), Brinje
rows.what: Whether the Brinje registers are filmed. ⚠ Asked here without checking the Blažević Archive first, which had located the films on 15 September and is reading them now. This is a second road to the same books, not a discovery.
ev: The Kalanj page — the Brinje door, now measured
rows.got:
**⚠ FIRST, WHAT THIS IS NOT. It is not a discovery, and the check that would have shown that was not run.**

The working rules say to grep this archive's own logs before claiming a find. They do not yet say to check the **other family archives**, and they should: [the Blažević Archive](https://blazevic.defranceski.com/kalanj/) **located the Brinje films on 15 September 2026** — *DGS 5498262*, births 1888–1900 and marriages 1888–1899, items 1–4 of roll 2121763; *DGS 5498263*, deaths 1888–1899 — recorded their dates as **1888–1900** exactly as found below, and had already drawn the same conclusion in the same words: **1888 is twenty-four years after the 1864 baptism.** On **29 September**, the same day as this search, that session read **images 493 to 622** of the marriage book and found **Kalanj at Brinje houses 231 and 249**, a **Perković** bride, and seven **Borić** men. *David had to point this out.*

**What the work below does add**, and the reason it is kept: **a second, independent road to the same registers, and one piece of evidence the film route does not carry.**

**Brinje IS filmed, and it begins twenty-four years too late.**

The Croatian State Archives' own register search covers **HR-HDA-1448, «Zbirka dopunskih mikrofilmova matičnih knjiga i popisa obitelji»** — registers of **all confessions** from the mid-sixteenth to the first half of the twentieth century, filmed from originals held in state archives, church archives, parish offices and registry offices. **This archive already knew the collection**: it is the one [the Crikvenica page](/crikvenica-house/) names for the post-1909 books. It had never been asked about Brinje.

**Place «BRINJE», confession «SVE KONFESIJE», all types. Five entries, and that is everything:**

| Vrsta | Razdoblje | Napomena | Signatura svitka | Topografska | Digitalni oblik |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **R** — births | **1888–1892** | PRIJEPIS | ZM-34C/681 | M-1278 | **Ne** |
| **R** — births | **1893–1897** | PRIJEPIS | ZM-34C/681 | M-1278 | **Ne** |
| **R** — births | **1897–1900** | PRIJEPIS | ZM-34C/681 | M-1278 | **Ne** |
| **V** — marriages | **1888–1899** | PRIJEPIS | ZM-34C/681 | M-1278 | **Ne** |
| **U** — deaths | **1888–1899** | ZM-34C/682 | M-1279 | | **Ne** |

All Roman Catholic, all filed under «RAZNE KNJIGE IZVAN POPISA HDA», and **all of them PRIJEPIS — transcripts, not the original books.**

**What that means for the Kalanj.** [Anna Kalanj was born 3 January 1864](/kalanj/) and her parents, **Josip Kalanj and Rosalia née Perković**, were married before that — the 1864 entry calls them country people *of the parish of Brinje*. **The filmed Brinje registers start in 1888.** They cannot contain her baptism, her parents' marriage, or any of her brothers and sisters. *(**doc** for the holding and its dates; the negative for 1864 follows from them.)*

**And none of it is digitised.** Every row reads *Digitalni oblik: **Ne***, so even the 1888–1900 books mean a microfilm reel in the reading room of the Hrvatski državni arhiv in Zagreb, or paid copies. The ordering route is specific and worth keeping: **info@arhiv.hr**, quoting the place, the type of register, the period, the **signatura svitka** and the **topografska oznaka** — all five of which are in the table above. Ten technical units a day, maximum.



**So the value here is narrow and real.** The Blažević route is FamilySearch film, reachable by DGS number and already being walked. This route is the **Croatian State Archives' own microfilm collection, HR-HDA-1448**, with reel signatures and an email ordering route — and it records something the film route does not: these are **PRIJEPIS, transcripts, not the original books**. That is the fact that matters for what is still missing. **Anna was born in 1864 and every filmed Brinje book begins in 1888**, so her baptism and her parents' marriage are in originals that are on neither road, and it is those originals — at the parish, the Senj-Modruš diocesan archive, or Gospić — that must now be asked for.

**⚠ AND A TRAP IN THE TOOL, WHICH NEARLY PUT NINE FALSE NILS IN THIS LOG.**

The search is a Telerik combo box on an ASP.NET page. **Setting it from script — `$find(id).findItemByText(x).select()` — changes what the box DISPLAYS and does not commit the value to the server.** The search then runs on an empty place and returns *«Nema zapisa za pregled»*, **which is exactly what a genuine nil looks like.**

Nine places were queried that way — Jezerane, Letinac, Stajnica, Prozor, Krivi Put, Vodoteč, Ogulin, Modruš and Crikvenica — and all nine came back empty. **Every one of those results is discarded and none is recorded as a nil**, because re-running **BRINJE** through the same code returned «Nema zapisa» too, when it demonstrably holds the five rows above. *The control is what caught it; without a known-positive re-run, nine invented negatives would have gone into this file and been believed.* **The neighbouring parishes of the Brinje area are therefore NOT tested, and are not claimed either way.**

The tool's own instructions also warn that a place may appear under several forms and that all of them must be checked — CRIKVENICA has four variants. **BRINJE has one**, so the table above is the whole of what that name holds.

rows.src: HDA HR-HDA-1448 — is Gologorica in it? The place list says yes; the search would not run
rows.what: Item 160 needs the Gologorica baptisms of about 1909 and has only one route to them — a letter to Poreč. Whether the HDA microfilm collection offers a second was tested.
rows.got:
**A lead, and deliberately not more than that.**

This archive records **Gologorica, Gračišće and Pićan as absent from FamilySearch's Croatian collection**, walked in September — which is why [item 160](/worklist/) has only one route to the 1909 baptism, a letter to the Poreč diocesan archive. **It had never asked the other collection.**

**What is established: the places are in HR-HDA-1448's index.** The register search offers **GOLOGORICA** as a selectable parish, and **GRAČIŠĆE** under **four** separate name forms — *GRAČIŠĆE*, *GRAČIŠĆE TRVIŽ KAŠĆERGA SV. PETAR U ŠUMI*, *GRAČIŠĆE-ŠKOPLJACI* and *GRAČIŠĆE-ŠKOPLJAK* — plus **PIĆAN**. That list is the page's own data, read directly, not a search result. *(**doc** for the list; it proves the names are known to the collection, and nothing yet about what it holds for them.)*

**What is NOT established: what any of them holds.** The search would not run. The place and confession were set and *Pretraži* clicked, and **no results table rendered at all** — the same behaviour that [the Brinje search](/searched/) recorded, where exactly one query succeeded and nothing after it did. **No holding, and no nil, is claimed here**, because this tool's empty state is indistinguishable from a real absence and its failures are not announced.

**It was not hammered.** Whether the obstruction is session state, a rate limit or a flaky application is not known, and a rate limit is not something to push against. *One query, on a cooperating day, would settle whether Gologorica's registers reach 1909 — and if they do, item 160's question 2 has a second road that needs no letter.* **That is the whole value of this row: a named, cheap thing to retry.**

**And a warning for whoever retries it.** Gračišće's four name forms are the trap the site itself warns about: *«u padajućem izborniku nude se različite inačice naziva, pa valja pregledati zapise za sve ponuđene»*. **Checking one and calling the parish absent would be wrong.**

rows.src: Svetvinčenat marriages, film 005497886 — frame 98, carta 55 (1785)
rows.what: Item 136's sweep resumed at frame 98 after the FamilySearch session was restored.
rows.pages: carta 55
ev: The house at Muina — the marriage, and the Istrian styling
rows.got:
**One entry, and it puts Gologorica and Muina in the same sentence for the first time.**

> **Anno Dni 1785 Die 14 Martii.** *Antonio q. Leonardo de Franceschi* **da Gollogorizza Diocesi di Pedena** *contrasse li primi sponsali per verba de presenti, con Maria figlia q. Giacomo Corva* **da Muina Diocesi d'Udine**, *soggetta però alla mia cura spirituale, ambi comunicati, e confessati…*

**The place name was read at 2.4× before anything was written.** «Gollogorizza» is unambiguous in the hand, and **«Diocesi di Pedena» settles it**: Gologorica sat in the diocese of Pedena, and no other Istrian place carries that name. The bride's line was magnified separately — «Mui-na Diocesi d'Udine», broken across two lines.

**Why it matters.** [The Carnia page](/carnia/) carries a household at Muina four generations deep, and its second generation is **«Antonio de Franceschi, son of the late Leonardo, and Maria née Corva», farmers of Muina** — with **no marriage found**. That entry's own text read: *«if his grandson was born in 1788 and his son was of age to marry by about 1785»*. **The marriage is 14 March 1785.** The guess named the year.

It also names **Giacomo Corva**, Maria's father, who was nowhere in this archive; and it dates **Leonardo's death before 1785**, twenty-three years earlier than the chain had it.

**And it describes Antonio as a man of Gologorica.** *A household this archive has always called Carnian is headed, at its own wedding, by a man styled of the Istrian parish the direct line comes out of.*

**⚠ The identification is INFERENCE, and it is said so on the page.** Name, patronymic «q. Leonardo», a Corva wife of Muina, and a son born at Muina in 1788 all agree — but no document yet links the Svetvinčenat groom to the Muina farmer in one breath. *(**doc** for the entry; **inf**, firmly held, for the identification.)* **The test named: Osvaldo's baptism at Muina, 14 March 1788, if it gives his mother's father.**

*Also on this frame, and not ours: Domenico Marmilla q. Antonio of Valle, 20 June 1785. The archpriest signing throughout is D. Paolo Cossaich, consistent with the change already recorded in this volume.*

*Surnames set in italic above are read with less confidence than the rest — the hand is the same D. Paolo Cossaich throughout and the formula is fixed, but these are single occurrences with no second construction to check them against.* **None of them is a candidate for this name; they are listed so the next reader can correct a reading rather than repeat the frame.**

**The witnesses were read too**, since the name has turned up as a witness twice already in this volume: Zuane Pridam, Mattio Bullesich, Antonio Fachinetti, Antonio Gionello *campanaro* (who witnesses four of these), Martin Ottocian, Zuane q. Mate Tonco, Vicenzo q. Zuane Cortich, Mattio di Martin Tomissich, Mattio di Tomaso Furlanich, Gaspara Peretich, the *giudice* Antonio Zambiasio, Zuanne Obrovaz, Antonio Giuritico, Piero Valentich. **No De Franceschi among them.**

**Nil for the name. Six marriages, all named.**

| date | groom | bride |
|---|---|---|
| 12 December 1786 | Antonio *Pocean* q. Giuseppe, **dalla Poveria, distretto di Dignano** | Vittoria q. Adamo Dolcanovich, *qui soggetta* |
| 6 January 1787 | Marco Simunovich q. Antonio | Ellena q. Vido *Civerich* |

| 21 January 1787 | Gregorio di Simon *Bicos* | Cattarina q. Martin *Ottozian*, figlia di Bartolomeo *Mazzon* |

*Italicised surnames are read with less confidence: single occurrences, no second construction to check them against. One groom's given name would not resolve and is left unread rather than guessed.*

**AND THE BOOK CHECKED THE WALK.** At the foot of the left column: **«Fine dell'Anno 1786 — Matrimonii al Numero ___ 10.»** *Magnified on its own line before it was believed, as the 1785 total was.*

**Counting what this sweep actually read for 1786: one on frame 99 (10 February), eight on frame 100, and one here (12 December) — ten.** The parish's own total and this archive's count agree exactly. *That is not a finding about the family; it is a finding about the reading.* **It says no entry of 1786 was skipped, and it is the first time this sweep has been able to prove that rather than assume it.**

*The archpriest is D. Paolo Cossaich throughout. Antonio Gionello, the bellringer, witnesses three more of these.*

rows.what: The seam continued. Seven marriages read entry by entry — and the hand changes mid-page, which in this volume has once already changed how the name is spelled.
rows.pages: carta 59
rows.got:
**Nil for the name. Seven marriages, all named — and a change of hand worth more than the nil.**

| date | groom | bride |
|---|---|---|
| 5 February 1787 | Antonio *Cherstanaz* q. Mattio | *Perpetua* q. Zuanne *Zacai* |
| 11 February 1787 | *Cristo* q. Piero Mazzon | Fosca q. Mattio Mazzon |
| 18 February 1787 | Zuanne q. Antonio *Zabrunich* | Antonia q. Tomaso *Lerbich* |
| 20 February 1787 | **Sig. Antonio Facchinetti**, *vedovo* | **Nob. D.na Elisabetta nata Rizzamano**, of the q. Sig. Iseppo Basilisco |
| 28 May 1787 | Ive Bianco q. Simo, *vedovo*, **del Territorio di Canfanaro** | Maria q. Mate *Laicovich* |
| 5 July 1787 | Ive *Giurzan* q. Simo | Cattarina q. *Mario Affrich* |
| 15 July 1787 | Mattio q. Stefano Petrovich, *vedovo* | Maria d'Antonio *Angelich* |

**⚠ THE REGISTRAR CHANGES ON THIS PAGE, AND THAT MATTERS FOR SEARCHING.** From the entry of **18 February 1787** the hand is different — rounder, more upright — and it signs itself **«Augustinus de **Caneva** Can[onicu]s et Oeconomus registravit» *(read «de Ceneda» at first from two instances; four clearer instances on frame 103, plus a layman «Lio: Batta de Caneva q. Daniele» witnessing there, settle it as **Caneva**. A hand is only legible against itself.)***, where every entry since 1782 closed **«Io D. Paolo D. Cossaich curato ed arciprete»**. *Verified across three consecutive entries, not one.*

**This volume has already done this once, with consequences.** When the archpriest changed in 1782 from D. Antonio Massalini to D. Paolo Cossaich, **the spelling of this family's surname changed with him**, from *Defranceschi* to *Franceschi* — which is why a name-indexed search loses the family mid-volume. **A third hand from February 1787 is a third spelling waiting to happen**, and the frames after this one should be read with that in mind rather than scanned for one form.

**And a false friend, already known here and worth restating.** The last witness of 15 July is **«Andrea Frane=cich»**, broken across two lines and magnified to settle it. It ends in **-cich**, the Italian rendering of Croatian **-čić**, and it is **not** a form of *Franceschi*. *This archive already carries Francich / Frančić as a distinct surname in [the Istrian sweep](/searched/) and the register file; nothing new is claimed. It is noted because in an index the two collide, and because this sweep now reads witnesses as well as parties.*

rows.src: Svetvinčenat marriages, film 005497886 — frame 103, carta 60 (1787–1788)
rows.what: The seam continued into 1788 — and produced two of the name on one page, plus the answer to how this volume spells it.
rows.pages: carta 60
rows.got:
**Two of the name in one entry, and the spelling question settled.**

**16 January 1788** — *«**Zuanne Contossich q.m Pietro** contrasse i primi Sponsali per verba de praesenti con **Maria figlia del S.r Antonio Defranceschi**, ambi di questa Parochia, confessati, e Communicati… dispensati dalla Curia di Parenzo dalle solite Conciliari trine Publicazioni, come appar da lettera di d. Curia segnata li 14 corr.»* — witnessed by *«Antonio Civitico, e **Domenico Defranceschi**»*.

*Both the bride's patronymic and the witness were magnified separately before being written down.*

**⚠ AND THE SPELLING HAS CHANGED BACK.** This volume dropped the «De» in 1780 when D. Paolo Cossaich took the book, which is why an indexed search loses the family mid-volume. **[Frame 102](/searched/) flagged a new hand from 18 February 1787; frame 103 shows what it did.** The roles are now split — **D. Giovanni Venica, parroco**, performs the marriages and **D. Agostino de Caneva, canonico ed economo**, registers them — and **«Defranceschi» is written in full again.** *So the spelling tracks the scribe, not the family, and it has now been seen to move in both directions.*

**A correction to the previous row while I am here:** that registrar was recorded as «de **Ceneda**» off two instances on frame 102. Frame 103 gives four clearer ones, and a layman witness *«D.no Lio: Batta **de Caneva** q. Daniele»*, so the name is **de Caneva**. *[The row is amended.](/searched/) A hand is only legible against itself.*

**Maria's father is «Signor» Antonio Defranceschi.** *The identification with the Antonio who «guidati da Antonio Defranceschi, nel 1780 avevano ottenuto l'esonero» — the man at the centre of [item 136](/worklist/), alive in 1783 as «Capo Antonio» — fits the parish, the period and the honorific.* **It is inf and is labelled so on the page; there may have been more than one Antonio.**

**The rest of the frame, nil and named:** 1 August 1787, Zuanne q. Mate *Lulcich* × Maria di Niccolò Millovan q. Antonio · 25 November 1787, Mate q. Zuane Vidulin × Vittoria di Zuanne *Bercovich* · 25 November 1787, Michiel q. Mattio *Puersich* **della Parrochia di Dignano** × Mattia q. Niccolò *Saverin* · 26 November 1787, Mattio q. Mattio Angelich × Maria di Stefano *Missan* · 5 January 1788, *Sive* Stocovich q. Matte × Maria r. Matte Percich · 17 January 1788, Martino q. Ive *Suticich* × Eufemia r. q. Antonio Paicovich · 6 March 1788, Gio. Battista q. Bernardo **Corretto di Dignano, diocesi di Pola** × the widow of **the late Sig. Antonio Facchinetti** *(who married on frame 102 in February 1787 and is «fu» by March 1788)* · 16 8bris 1788, Mate *Bercan* q. Ive × Lucia.

rows.what: The seam continued to 1790. Eleven marriages read entry by entry.
rows.pages: carta 61
rows.got:
**Nil for the name. Eleven marriages, October 1788 to June 1790, all named.**

**1788** — Michiel Mattias di Michiel × Maria di Mat[tio] *Palesca* · Antonio *Drandich* q. Matte, **della Parochia di Valle** × Maria di Tome Vidulin · Zuane Petrovich q. Stefano × Vittoria r. q. Martin *Dobrenovich*, **dispensed from the third degree of affinity** · 24 November, Ive *Stocovich* q. Giacomo × Maria di Vido Bilich.

**1789** — 17 May, Antonio *Prossen* × Elena r. q. Ive *Puh* · 15 June, Mattio di *Padre* Ban × Maria di Vido Mattias · 5 July, Mattio q. Bortolo *Zubanich* × Agata di Adamo *Paivovich* · 7 August, Matte q. Giacomo Stocovich × Maria q. Martin Bilich · October, Antonio *Grisanaz* × Biasia r. q. Nadal *Ucmir*.

**1790** — 10 January, Gregorio *Marzan* q. Giacomo × Vittoria di Domenico *Doblanovich* · 14 June, Matte di Vido *Bulesich* × Agata q. *Iure Dobrio*.

*Italicised surnames are read with less confidence. **The date of the first entry would not resolve** — it reads as «16» with a month abbreviation that could be 8bris, and it sits before an August entry, so either the reading or the book's order is out. It is left as read rather than tidied.*

**Three things worth keeping.**

· **The officiant now signs «D. Gio: Venica Can.co ed Arcip.»** — canon and archpriest, where on [frame 103](/searched/) he was simply *parroco*.
· **«Sig. Can.co Agostin Decaneva» stands as a WITNESS** at the wedding of 7 August 1789 — written as one word. *That is a sixth instance of the name and it confirms the correction made on frame 103: **Caneva**, not Ceneda.*
· **The bell-rope has moved twice more.** *Antonio Gionello is campanaro through 1785–86; Antonio Civitico from 1787 to 1790.* **[Written into the readings](/lines/)**, because this archive has followed that rope since it was in the family's own hands in 1773.

**Nil for the name. Eleven marriages, October 1790 to March 1791, all named.**

**1790** — 23 Oct, Mattio di Ive Petrovich × Maria r. q. Pietro Marzan · 4 Nov, Gregorio q. Adamo Doblanovich × Fosca di Stefano Missan · 4 Nov, Simon q. Matte Stocovich × Maria di Matte *Perich* · Nov, Vicenzo *Cherzan* q. Paulo × Maria di Vido *Paterich di Pedrianez* · 21 Nov, Gregorio di Zorzi *Stenta* × Catterina di Zorzi *Bolisanaz* · 24 Nov, Gasparo *Ferlin* × Cattarina r. q. Gregorio *Trebanich* · 24 Nov, Biasio *Sustianaz* q. Martin × Agata r. q. Matte Zubanich, **dispensed from the third degree of consanguinity** · 14 Nov, Martin q. Iure *Xivolich* × Oliva r. q. Zuanne *Smoglian*.

**1791** — 25 Jan, Gregorio Billich q. Pietro × Maria di Matte *Ruscovich* · 26 Jan, Marco di Vido *Bulesich* × Eufemia di Ive *Buicu* · 7 Mar, Domenico *Basanich* q. Marin × Maria q. Mattio *Sussich*.

**⚠ And that last bride comes from across the border.** *«della Parochia di **Carbune Austriaca**»* — **Krbune**, in the county of **Pazin**, which was **Austrian** Istria, while Svetvinčenat was **Venetian**. *Magnified before being written down.* **It is the first marriage in this stretch to reach into the Austrian half of the peninsula** — and Krbune sits in the same small cluster of villages as **Gologorica and Gračišće**, roughly ten kilometres off. *(**doc** for the entry. No connection to this family is claimed; it is recorded because this archive tracks the Venice–Austria line, and because it shows this parish's marriage catchment crossing it.)*

*Her father's surname is written with the register correcting itself — one form struck through and another written above, with «di Martino» inserted. Both readings are given as they stand rather than silently resolved.*

**Two officiants on one page.** D. Giovanni Venica signs *«Arcip. registrai»*, and the entry of 7 March 1791 records the couple interrogated by **«D. Agostino Decaneva Can.co»** — inserted above the line. *A seventh instance of **Caneva**.* And **Antonio Civitico** is campanaro at eight of these eleven.

rows.src: Svetvinčenat marriages, film 005497886 — frames 106–108: the register closes, and the loose slips
rows.what: The end of the bound marriage register, and the twenty-six marriages kept on loose slips after it.
ev: The Svetvinčenat readings — the book closes, and Maria is widowed
rows.got:
**Three frames, and the shape of the source changes underneath the sweep.**

**Frame 106 — the bound register ends.** The last act is 7 March 1791. What follows is a Latin note: *«Die 28. Maji 1791. In Castro S. Vincentii, in 2da Visitatione Generali … praesentatus ab Adm. Rev.do D. Can.co Plebanum; quo viso et reviso restitutus fuit»* — the book produced at the bishop's **second general visitation**, seen, reviewed and returned, signed by the Vicar General, marked *gratis*. **The rest of the leaf is cancelled with a single large X.**

**Frames 107–108 — loose slips, not pages.** Laid into the volume, in a hurried hand, each marriage one line: date, groom, bride. **No publications, no dispensations, no witnesses, no officiant.** *Twenty-six marriages, June 1791 to November 1792, all read.*

**⚠ AND ONE OF THEM IS OURS.**

> **Addì 30 [X]bre 1791** — *…incontrò matrimonio con **Maria relita q.m Contossich nata Defranceschi**.*

**[Frame 103](/searched/) has «Maria figlia del S.r Antonio Defranceschi» marrying «Zuanne Contossich q.m Pietro» on 16 January 1788.** Under four years later a Maria, widow of a Contossich, **née Defranceschi**, remarries in the same parish. *The slip gives both her married and her maiden name, which is what makes the two lock.* **(doc for each entry; inf, strongly held, that it is one woman.)** [Written into the readings.](/lines/)

*Her new husband's name and the word following «Defranceschi» would not resolve and are left unread.*

**The other twenty-five, nil and named** — Tonco, Stocovich, Mattias, Ferlin, Mazzar, Dulcesich, Calisca, Lenich, Millovan, Iurlanich, Sosich *(of Canfanaro)*, Petercich, Percovich, Sertich, Doblanovich, Vellovich, Xivolich, Marmilla *(of the Pieve di Valle)*, Bulcich, Crisman, Preden, Drosina, Bullesich, Suffich, Giuricich *(of Gimino)*, Vidolin, Salambat, Malusà, Bergamo.

**One slip entry is fuller than the rest and worth the note:** 25 October 1792, Mico q. Seco Mazzan detto Pecas married Lucia in **the church of the B.V. Maria** by **D. Marco de Vis, chaplain of S. Germano, «de licentia Parrochi»** — a marriage performed away from the parish church by a chaplain under licence, which is the kind of act that goes missing from a parish index.

*Also settled in passing: «**Padre**» is a personal name in this parish, not a title — «Padre Ban» appears as a bride's father here and as a groom's father on frame 104. A reading flagged as uncertain two frames ago is now resolved against a second instance.*

**⚠ Re-filed `walked: false` on 30 September 2026, and the reason is worth splitting.** *This row covers three frames of two different kinds.* **Frame 106 is a bound leaf and was wholly visible** — the visitation note and the cancelled remainder are not in doubt. **Frames 107 and 108 are the loose slips, and [frame 115 showed those are a layered pile](/searched/)**: a smaller sheet lies across a larger one and was moved between exposures, so one photograph does not show every entry. *The twenty-six marriages listed here were read. Whether more lie beneath them was not established, so the row cannot claim the whole.* **The Defranceschi widow of December 1791 is unaffected — she appears on both exposures.**

rows.src: Svetvinčenat marriages, film 005497886 — frame 109, the slips re-photographed
rows.what: Frame 109 turned out to be a SECOND EXPOSURE of the same loose slips as frame 108, with the backing card moved.
rows.got:
**Frame 109 is not a new opening. It is frame 108's two slips, photographed again.**

**And that is useful rather than wasted, because the film is doing something deliberate.** A card reading **«BLEED THROUGH · VIDLJIV TEKST S DRUGE STR.»** sits in both exposures — it is a **backing card**, slid behind a thin slip so the writing on its reverse stops showing through. *Between the two frames the card is in different positions, so each exposure makes a different part of the slip legible.*

**Two entries that would not resolve on frame 108 are plain here:**

· **30 September 1792** — **Iure Mazzan q. Ive** × Eufemia, widow of the late Domenico *Smosina*. *(On frame 108 only «…q. Ive incontrò matrimonio» could be made out.)*
· **26 October 1792** — **Matte, son of Adamo Paicovich** × Oliva, daughter of Vido Petercich. *(Not legible at all on frame 108.)*

**⚠ And a caution this sweep should carry from here on.** Where a backing card is in use, the leaf is thin enough for the reverse to read through. **Anything faint on these slips may be text from the other side, not from the side facing the camera** — and on a one-line entry with no witnesses to cross-check, that is a real way to invent a marriage. *Every entry recorded from frames 107–109 was taken from strokes that read left-to-right and sat on a ruled line; nothing faint or reversed was transcribed.*

**The Defranceschi entry is on both exposures**, in the same place on the left slip, reading the same way: *«Maria relita q.m Contossich nata Defranceschi»*. **A hit confirmed on two independent photographs of the same document is about as firm as this film gets.**

rows.src: Svetvinčenat marriages, film 005497886 — frame 110, the slips to 1794
rows.what: The loose slips continue to May 1794. Fourteen marriages read — and one of them names a daughter of Jacobo's house.
ev: The Svetvinčenat readings — Jacobo's third child
rows.got:
**Two more loose slips, November 1792 to May 1794, fourteen marriages, and the last of them is ours.**

> **Addì 19. Maggio 1794** — *Domenico **Martincich** incontrò matrimonio con **Pasqua figlia del q.m Giacomo Defranceschi**.*

*Magnified before transcription; one of the clearest lines on the film. Spelled **Defranceschi**, with the «De», consistent with every entry since the hand changed in 1787.*

**This is a third named child of Jacobo's house**, joining Antonia (married a Carnian, 7 January 1779) and Zuanne (19 July 1784) — all three styled *«di / figlia del q.m Giacomo»*, and their father dead before the first of the three weddings. [Told in the readings.](/lines/)

**⚠ Checked before claiming, and the check found something.** This archive already records a **Pasqua who was the widow of a q.m Giacomo de Franceschi**, remarrying on 22 October 1765. *A daughter named for her mother is the obvious reading* — but the archive also already holds that there were **at least two men called Jacobo at this castle**, and a widow of 1765 with a daughter marrying in 1794 is at the edge of one generation. **Recorded as inf, argued on the page, and not turned into a fact.**

**The other thirteen, nil and named** — Bullesich × Mattias · Marosin *of Canfanaro* × Tonco · Mazzar × Crisman *of Gimino* · Peterich × Obrovaz · Calisca × Drossich *of Canfanaro* · Ban × Crisianaz · Mazzar *of the Pieve di Barbana* × Bliscovich · Petercich × Gerobistrich · Bilisanaz × Millovan · Percovich × Preden · Laurin × Ban *of Dosan, dispensed in the fourth degree* · Drandich *of Carnè in the Pieve di Valle* × Obrovaz · Preden *of Canfanaro*.

*The parish's reach in these years is worth noting on its own: Canfanaro three times, Gimino, Barbana, Valle — and on [frame 105](/searched/) Carbune in Austrian Istria.*

**⚠ Re-filed `walked: false` on 30 September 2026.** *[Frame 115 showed the slips are a layered pile](/searched/): a smaller sheet lies across a larger one and was moved between exposures, so one photograph does not show every entry. This row recorded what could be **seen**; it cannot claim every entry was **read**. The entries listed were read; what may lie beneath them was not.*

Pizetta* × Sandrich · Calisca × Carij **della Pieve di Pisino** · Millovan × Stocovich *d. Culle* · Iursich q. **Padre** × Obrozan · Preden *d. Soldat* × Millovan · Vidolin × Afnich *di Carnè, Par. di Valle* · Doblanovich × Collich *of Valle* · Xivolich × *Maria figlia del q. Giacomo Godichia*.

It reads **Godichia**, not Defranceschi — and the bride's parish is struck through and rewritten in the slip itself.*

**The parish's reach keeps widening.** *Barbana, Canfanaro, Valle twice, Carnè — and **Pisino**, which is the district town of **Austrian** Istria and the district Gologorica and Gračišće sit in. With [Carbune on frame 105](/searched/) that is a second marriage in this stretch reaching across the Venice–Austria line.* **No connection to this family is claimed from either.**

rows.what: The loose slips continue to April 1797. Sixteen marriages read entry by entry.
rows.got:
**Nil for the name. Sixteen marriages, October 1795 to April 1797, all named.**

**1795–96** — Bullesich × Bullesich · Sigliar × Paicovich · Doblanovich × Millovan · Crossan × Mazzan *d. Bendech* · Smoglian × Drosina *(dispensed)* · Iugovaz × Bullesich · Salambat × Licovich.

**1797** — Lanchich × Benussio *da Dorigno* · Doblanovich × Hoglan **of Lupoglavo** · Percovich × Beran · Millovan × Vidolin · Vidolin × Millovan · Xivolich *d. Dolso* × Bercan · Zabronich × Balcich · **Xivolich × Dursich and Dursich × Xivolich, both on 24 April**.

**⚠ And the scribe hedges a surname in the register itself.** The entry of 5 February 1797 names the groom *«**Gherso Doblanovich, ò forsi Bullesich**»* — **«or perhaps Bullesich»**. *A parish clerk writing down that he is not sure which of two houses a man belongs to.* **That is worth more than its own entry**: it is the register conceding, in its own hand, that a surname in this parish could be uncertain to the man recording it — which is exactly the condition this archive keeps meeting from the other end, two centuries later. *(Recorded, not resolved. Neither name is ours.)*

**Two houses exchange on one day.** *24 April 1797: Martin, son of Matte Xivolich detto Dolso, marries Eufemia daughter of Pere Dursich — and Sime, son of Pere Dursich, marries Cattarina daughter of Matte Xivolich detto Dolso. Two weddings, four people, two households, one afternoon.* **Not our family, and recorded because a parish of this size shows its shape in arrangements like that.**

*Lupoglav is a fourth parish of **Austrian** Istria to appear in this stretch, after Carbune (frame 105) and Pisino (frame 111).*

**1797** — Matica × Vitolovich *of the Pieve di Pisino* · Mazzar × Preden *d. Tonca* · Angelich *d. Orese* × Bullesich *d.to Suvin* · Sigliar × Bilich · Bercan × Sguera.

**1798** — Mazzan *d. Lust* × Sigliar · Spelich × Iurlanich *d. Bucar* · Salambat × Salambat · Petercich × Paicovich · Mazzan *d. Bosco* × Lerich · Rulian × Castaner **da Rovigno** · Preden × Angelich · Ledizza *dai Sain* × Xivolich *d. Dolso* · Affrich × Bulcich · Missan × Ledizza *dai Lodolichi*.

**⚠ One entry is of a different order, and the archive should have it.**

> **Addì 12 Gen.o 1798** — *Il **Sig.r Giuseppe Fackinetti** incontrò matrimonio con la **Sig.ra Giuseppina Lagadopoli da Spalatro**, ed esso da **Montagnana**.*

**Two «Signori», and neither is from here.** *The bride is of **Split**, and her surname — **Lagadopoli** — is Greek, of the kind the Dalmatian cities carried. The groom is «da Montagnana».* **Facchinetti is a name this sweep already knows**: a Sig. Antonio Facchinetti witnessed weddings on these pages for years, married the Nob. D.na Elisabetta née Rizzamano on [frame 102](/searched/) in February 1787, and was dead by March 1788. *(Not this family, and no connection is claimed. Recorded because this archive follows the Adriatic gentry across Istria and Dalmatia, and because a Greek-surnamed bride of Split marrying into a Svetvinčenat house is exactly the kind of movement [the spines](/lines/) exist to show.)*

*Pisino appears again, and Rovigno for the first time in this stretch.*

rows.got:
**Nil for the name. Sixteen marriages, January 1799 to May 1802, all named.**

**1799–1800** — Paicovich × Vidolin · Gelsich *of Canfanaro* × Percovich *detto Corduch* · Bortolini **da Rovigno** × Giuritico · Spelich × Preden · Busaz × Obrozan *di S. Bricio* · Pelosa **di Mune** × Stocovich *d. Bacus* · Drandich *of Valle* × Vidulin · Lacapich × Stenta *of Valle*.

**1801–02** — Crisman × Rocada *(dispensed)* · Crisman × Ruvarich · Lasperia *of Canfanaro* × Percovich *(dispensed)* · Percovich *d. Pagna* × Bercan *of Valle* · Petrovich *d. Dromizar* × Ban *d. Dogna* · Bullesich × Bullesich *d. Suvin* · Vorich *d. Barbanaz* × Crisman *of Valle, detto Vidolin*.

**One entry of a different rank, and it dates the slip.** *A header «Addì 24 Xbre 1800» is struck through and the entry beneath it reads* **23 February 1801** — *«**Il Sig.r Marcello Manari, figlio dell'Ill.mo Sig. D.r Girolamo, medico fisico**, incontrò matrimonio con la Sig.ra Cattarina figlia di Sebastiano Dedracich **di Lindaro**»*. **A physician's son marrying a lady of Lindar** — which is another parish of **Austrian** Istria, near Pazin. *(Not this family. Recorded because the slip's struck-through date shows the keeper writing these up out of order and correcting himself, which is worth knowing before anyone treats the slips as a chronological series.)*

**Mune** — in the far north of Istria — is a fifth Austrian-side parish in this stretch, after Carbune, Pisino, Lupoglav and Lindar.
