rows.src: Svetvinčenat marriages, film 005497886 — frame 115, and the slips are a LAYERED PILE
rows.what: Frame 115 is frame 114's slips re-photographed — and it proves the slips are stacked, which forces a correction to this sweep's own claims.
ev: Item 136 — and the correction to its walked claims
rows.got:
**⚠ THE SLIPS ARE A STACK, NOT A SHEET — AND THAT UNDOES A CLAIM THIS SWEEP HAS BEEN MAKING.**

Frame 115 photographs the same two slips as frame 114. Fifteen of the sixteen entries are identical. **One is not.** Where frame 114 shows the marriage of *«Il Sig.r Marcello Manari, figlio dell'Ill.mo Sig. D.r Girolamo, medico fisico»*, frame 115 shows, in the same place on the same slip:

> **Addì 24 Xbre 1799** — *Zuane **Bercan** q. Giure incontrò matrimonio con **Elena**, relita q. Tomaso **Gaugnelin della Parrochia di Valle**.*

**An entry frame 114 concealed.** And on the right-hand slip the mechanism is visible in the photograph itself: **a smaller piece of paper lies on top of the larger one**, its edge and shadow plain, carrying a note of witnesses — *«Test.i Giuseppe Bonan e M.ro Mario Baressi…»* — over the entry beneath it.

**So these are not loose sheets. They are a PILE**, with small overlay slips laid across larger ones, and the photographer moved them between exposures. *The same thing happened at [frames 108 and 109](/searched/), where two entries unreadable on one exposure were plain on the other — read there as a backing card being repositioned. It was not. It was the stack being shifted.*

**⚠ THE CORRECTION, AND IT IS THIS SWEEP'S OWN.** Rows for frames 107, 108–109, 110, 111, 112, 113 and 114 were filed **`walked: true`** — which in this estate means *every entry was read*. **That cannot be claimed of a layered pile photographed once.** An entry may lie under another sheet in the only exposure that was read. **Those rows are re-filed `walked: false`**, and each says why.

*The bound register, frames 79 to 106, is unaffected: those are sewn pages, wholly visible, and the year-totals for 1785 and 1786 were checked against the count. **«Walked» stands there and nowhere else on this film.***

**What it means for the four hits.** *None is weakened — each was read off a clearly visible entry, and the Defranceschi widow of 1791 appears on two separate exposures. What is weakened is the NILS: the slip frames are «nothing found in what could be seen», not «nothing there».* **Anyone finishing this film should photograph or request every exposure of each slip opening, and compare them.**

rows.src: Where the PRE-1882 Brinje registers are — and why every series starts where it does
rows.what: Anna Kalanj was born at Ledenice in 1864 of Brinje parents. Every Brinje register anyone holds begins in the 1880s. This asks why, and where the earlier books went.
ev: The Kalanj page — the Brinje door, and why it opens where it does
rows.got:
**⚠ First: this is NOT the Brinje work the Blažević Archive is doing, and it deliberately avoids it.** *That session located the two films on 15 September and has been reading them image by image ever since — through the marriage book and now into the Rođeni volumes, finding Kalanj households at Brinje houses 118/189, 231 and 249, and a dozen Borić.* **That is the 1888-and-after ground and it is theirs.** This row is about the years before, which nobody has asked about — [`whoelse.sh`](/method/) shows no sibling archive mentions the Military Frontier, the 1882 boundary or DAGS-109 in connection with Brinje.

**THE DATE WALL IS NOT AN ACCIDENT OF FILMING. IT IS A FRONTIER.**

Every Brinje series anyone holds begins at the same moment:

| holding | Brinje |
|---|---|
| **HR-HDA-1448**, the state microfilm collection | births **1888**–1900, marriages 1888–99, deaths 1888–99 — *and all of them **PRIJEPIS**, transcripts* |
| **HR-DAGS-109**, Državni arhiv u Gospiću | births from **1882** |

**Brinje was in the MILITARY FRONTIER.** The Ministry of War's authority there ended on **1 August 1881**, and the administration passed to the Croatian-Slavonian provincial government in Zagreb on **1 January 1882**. *(**doc** for the history.)* **The registers do not begin in 1882 because that is when records begin. They begin there because that is when Brinje stopped being a regiment and became a county.** *(**inf**, and firmly held — the fit is exact, and it explains two separate holdings landing on the same boundary.)*

**So Anna Kalanj's baptism cannot be in any of them.** *She was born 3 January 1864; her parents Josip Kalanj and Rosalia Perković married before that. Those are **Military Frontier–era parish books**, eighteen years before the earliest thing either archive can reach.*

**Where they are is now a short list, not an open question.** They are **not** in HR-HDA-1448 and **not** in HR-DAGS-109 — whose overall range is 1793–1998, *so it is not that Gospić holds nothing old; it holds nothing old **for Brinje***. What remains: **the parish office at Brinje**; the **diocesan archive** of Gospić-Senj, formerly Senj-Modruš; or they did not survive Lika's twentieth century. **None of the three has been asked.**

**⚠ Two doors closed on the way, and neither was worked around — with one correction to how they were first described.** *David asked whether HAIS is simply **www.arhiv.hr**. It is not, and checking properly sharpened all of this.*

| host | DNS | HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| **arhinet.arhiv.hr** — ARHiNET, also called **NAIS** | **NXDOMAIN**, gone entirely | — |
| **hais.arhiv.hr** | resolves, **161.53.80.20** | **nothing listening on 80 or 443** |
| **www.arhiv.hr** | resolves, **161.53.80.7** | **works** |

**So arhiv.hr is the same institution on a different machine, not the fonds register.** It carries the Croatian State Archives' own site and the one live database — [the register search](/searched/) — and nowhere on it, in either language, does the word ARHiNET or HAIS appear.

**⚠ And a claim of mine is withdrawn.** *This row first called hais.arhiv.hr «its successor». **That came from Record Atlas's provider note, not from anything verified here**, and repeating it as fact was wrong. What is established is only the network state above: ARHiNET's host is gone from DNS, and HAIS has a DNS record serving nothing. **Whether HAIS was ever meant to replace ARHiNET is not established by this archive.*** *The distinction matters, because «the successor is down» invites waiting, and «a hostname resolves to a machine serving nothing» invites asking the archive what happened to the catalogue.*

*Hrčak — which holds the study of the HDA's own register collection — answered **HTTP 418**, its bot rejection, exactly as [this archive already recorded](/worklist/). And the national fonds register is gone in both of its forms: **arhinet.arhiv.hr does not resolve** (NXDOMAIN, confirming what Record Atlas says) and its successor **hais.arhiv.hr refuses the connection outright** — ECONNREFUSED on 443, which is firmer than the «did not answer» the atlas had. A search engine still indexes ARHiNET pages; the links are dead.*

**(doc for HR-DAGS-109's signature and 1793–1998 range, read from the archive's own fundus page. The Brinje-specific date ranges within it come from a secondary summary and are **not** verified at source — they agree with the HDA film dates, which is corroboration, not proof.)**

rows.src: Milić, «Zbirka matičnih knjiga u HDA» (2017) — the 1860 rule, and why Anna's baptism is nowhere
rows.what: The published inventory of HR-HDA-883, read end to end for Brinje — and it gives the rule that explains why no archive holds Anna Kalanj's 1864 baptism.
ev: The Kalanj page — why the Brinje door is shut
rows.got:
**Angelika Milić, «Zbirka matičnih knjiga u Hrvatskom državnom arhivu», *Arhivski vjesnik* 60 (2017), 251–311** — the parish-by-parish inventory of **HR-HDA-883**, the Croatian State Archives' collection of **original** parish registers. *(David cleared Hrčak's bot check and downloaded the paper; it was not worked around. The text was searched, not reproduced.)*

**⚠ THE RULE, AND IT ANSWERS THE QUESTION THIS ITEM HAS BEEN ASKING.**

> *«Odlukom Ministarstva unutrašnjih poslova NRH od 13. svibnja 1949. **određeno je da se sve matične knjige s upisom do 1860. predaju na čuvanje nadležnim arhivima**»* — and the same law of 1946 provided that registers **from 1860** be given to the **matični uredi**, *«koje su bile potrebne u radu državnim matičnim uredima»* — because the registry offices needed them for daily work.

**Registers up to 1860 went to the archives. Registers from 1860 stayed where they were being used.** *(**doc** — stated in the article and again in its English abstract.)*

**Anna Kalanj was born 3 January 1864. Four years the wrong side of the line.** *Her baptism was never going to be in a state archive's register collection, because the law that filled those collections stopped at 1860 and left everything after it with the local office.* **That is why neither this archive nor the Blažević could find it, and it is not because it is lost.**

**The inventory confirms the rule on Brinje's own doorstep.** The collection covers the **Senj-Modruš** diocese, which is Brinje's, and the Lika parishes in it stop exactly where the rule says:

| parish | in HR-HDA-883 |
|---|---|
| **Gospić** | MKV and MKU from **1789**, MKR 1834 — all ending **1858/1859** |
| **Senj** | MKR from **1678**, MKV from **1734** — ending **1858** |
| **Sv. Juraj kod Senja** | from **1695** — ending 1852+ |

**And BRINJE is not in the collection at all.** *Searched the whole extracted text: the word does not appear once. So Brinje's pre-1860 books did not reach the HDA either — they are elsewhere, or they did not survive.*

**Where this leaves Anna, precisely.** *Her 1864 baptism belongs to the post-1860 segment that by law stayed with the **matični ured** or the parish. Brinje's pre-1860 segment is unaccounted for. Neither is in HR-HDA-883, HR-HDA-1448 or, for those years, Gospić.* **The place to ask is the registry office and the parish at Brinje, and the diocesan archive — not another state archive.**

*The inventory is substantial in its own right: **2,503 register volumes across 357 parishes, 1585–1947**, extracted as facts. [Catalogued for Record Atlas as provider `hda-883`.](/searched/) The extract itself was deliberately **not** committed to that repository — its licence gate refused a dataset whose publisher states no licence, and it was right to.*

**1,463 contiguous frames, M01068774–M01070236, no gaps — and until today the archive had cited twelve of them and logged one search row for the whole run.**

**Method.** *The paper inventory at Pazin cannot be trusted for these reels — it was wrong twice today. Instead every frame was scanned for ink coverage; a printed title card is an isolated frame carrying almost no ink on a bright ground. **12 of the 13 declared book boundaries were flagged**, and the single miss (M01069505) is a* nastavak *— a continuation — which correctly has no fresh card. Each card was then read.*

| M01069008–M01069181 | Gologorica | MKR 1784–1880 | 3.4 |
| M01069182–M01069198 | Gologorica | MKR 1940–1948 | 3.5 |

**⚠ `walked` is false, and deliberately.** *Every frame was **located**; almost none has been **read**. The four Gologorica* status animarum *alone are **628 frames — 43% of the whole run** — and only 1894 has ever been opened. Marking this walked would tell the next person the books are done when they have barely been started.*

rows.src: DAPA ZM34K-214 — Gologorica Status Animarum 1826, house 6 (M01069328)
rows.what: The first page of the re-read David asked for: every name on the opening, including the wives and the provenance column, not only the surname.
rows.film: ZM34K-214 (DAPA), frame M01069328
rows.waypointNote: DAPA microfilm held offline; no FamilySearch waypoint exists. Cited by reel and frame.
ev: The Gologorica line — the corrected pedigree
Two corrections from this one page
rows.got:
**One page, and it overturned a parentage the pedigree was drawn from.**

**Antonius (b. 14 April 1814) is named «filius Usualdi et Apoloniæ»**, the adnotatio calls Leonardus his **patruus** who adopted him, and the foot of the page repeats **«Usualdus … pater Antonii»** under a house marked *non habitata*. He was carried here as Leonardus's son. **Usualdus and Apollonia are new to this archive.**

**The provenance column — *«Locus ex quo vel ad quem»* — had never been read.** Against the marriage of 29 January 1840 it gives **Antonius «Ex Parochia Lindaris»** and **Francisca «Ex Parochia Gallignana sub N.º 5»**. *That is Gračišće house 5, whose census page this archive has held since 24 June 2021 without connecting it to her.* And **Mariana «ex fratre nepos»** married out on 18 September 1833 *«sub N.º 46»*.

**The register also carries deaths decades after 1826** — Leonardus 14 April 1848 aged 82y 2m 14d, Matthea 8 April 1858 aged 85y 6m 15d — *so this book was opened in 1826 and kept for another forty years, which makes it a far better source than its title year suggests.*

⚠ **Several dates already on the roster disagree with the page** — Theresia, Franciscus, Antonius and a «Joanna» where the page reads **Rosa** — *and those are not corrected here, because one reading of one page is not enough to move a date. They are the next thing to settle.*

ev: The priests of Gologorica, and the Peschle household
The Peschle — filled from an empty row
rows.got:
**The book's cover names its printer: «FIUME, presso Antonio Karletzky, Stampatore e Libraio»** *(M01069317)* — *an Istrian parish keeping its souls in a book bought at Fiume.*

**House 1 is the parish house, and it is the most useful page in the book.** *Eight priests of Gollogorica with birth dates and origins, kept up to the 1880s:* Franciscus Brussich (b. 1780, **Vrbnik** on Krk) · Petrus Milcetich (b. 1809, **Omišalj**, d. 22 March 1862 aged 58y 2m 15d, buried here) · Blasius Zwölber (b. 1822, *e Zuckfeld*, d. 1879) · Jacobus Sajovec (b. 1825, *e Zirklach*) · Joannes Dragovina (b. 1844, **Pazin**) · Josephus Flegar (b. 1845, **Novaki**) · Antonius Fabris (b. 1851, **Lindar**, d. 10 Nov 1885 aged 34y 2m, buried here) · Bartholomaeus Vitezić (b. 1856, **Vrbnik**). **Three of the eight came off Krk.** *This archive had been reading these hands without knowing whose they were.*

**Page 2 — Josephus Defranceschi, *civilis*.** *The class word, in the register's own hand, under the family the archive argues was of standing.*

**Page 3 — Maria Defranceschi, *civilis*, died 30 October 1826 aged 37y 2m 10d** *(so born about 20 August 1789). **Not identified with anyone on the roster** — this estate holds some thirty Maria Defranceschis and a death date alone will not pick one out.*

**Page 4 — Domus Ecclesiæ, then house 2: Dr Albertus Peschle**, *civis*, **«habitat Pisini»** — he kept the Gologorica house and lived at Pazin — with **Victoria née Calligarich** and their son **Conradus Josephus Victorius, b. 20 July 1853**. *The Peschle are Carlo De Franceschi's mother's family and their row on [the married-in page](/married-in/) had stood at **count 0, origin «—»**. It is no longer empty.*

**And that page settled a doubt raised an hour earlier**: «Victoria uxor **n.** Calligarich» is the same hand writing the same construction, so *n.* is *nata* and Francisca was born a Defranceschi. *inf → doc.*

ev: The Salomon line — a Salamon at Gračišće in 1807
The frame map — where this book stops
What has to be ordered to finish it
rows.got:
**❌ Not in the house, and the film says so itself.** *The title card calls this book* **Matična knjiga rođenih 1746–1840**, *but reel 215 does not carry all of it: the last written page, **M01070226**, is headed* **«Annus 1807»**, *and the very next frame, **M01070227**, is a printed card reading* **«NASTAVLJA SE»** — ***to be continued***.

**So the Gračišće baptisms the family holds run 1746–1807 and stop.** *The continuation is **ZM34K-216**, which this archive does not have. **Francisca's baptism of 3 February 1819 is on that reel**, and so is every Gračišće birth of the direct line's own generations after 1807.* **This is the single most valuable reel not in the house.**

**✅ But the sampling paid for itself twice.**

**First, the register gives every mother's maiden surname, systematically.** *The Matres column is written* **«Lucia olim Novina», «Maria olim Zelich», «Maria olim Juran», «Maria Milotich olim Tirol», «Maria Bicol olim Iuxa»** — ***olim*, formerly**, and what follows is the name she was born under. *David asked for the wives' families. **This book answers that question for every mother in the parish**, and no session here had noticed the construction.*

**Second, a Salamon is standing at the font.** *At the baptism of 26 November 1807, house 203, the godparents are* **«Franciscus Jurich»** *and* **«Maria **vidua Salamon**»** — **Maria, the widow Salamon**. *That is a **Salamon at Gračišće ten years after Francisca Salomon was born there** (17 March 1797), in the parish with the sixteenth-century **Salamon palace** this archive has already documented. **No kinship is claimed.** It is the first Salamon this archive has found in a Gračišće register.* *(doc for the entry; nothing inferred from it.)*

rows.got:
**A tree-only person becomes documented, and an abbreviation is settled for good.**

**House 3 — Antonius Sestan**, *«def. Vincentii et Mariæ»* (son of the late Vincentius and Maria), born 29 June 1814, **married 13 February 1843** to «**Joanna eius uxor nata Defranceschi**», **born 25 June 1818**, who came ***«Ex Parochia Gallignanæ sub N.º 4»***. *Six children under them, including Josephus, born 2 February 1858 and **dead on the 4th, aged two days**.*

**[Joanna](/who/joanna-defranceschi-sestan/) was on this roster from David's MyHeritage tree with an empty note and nothing behind her.** *She now has a husband with a patronymic, a wedding date, a house she came out of and six children with dates.*

**And the scribe writes «nata» out in full here.** *This morning the archive published «Francisca uxor **n.** Defranceschi» as an inference, then upgraded it on a second construction. **This is the third, and it is the word itself** — the doubt is closed.*

**Two Defranceschi daughters left Gračišće for Gologorica in three years**: Francisca from **house 5** in 1840, Joanna from **house 4** in 1843. *They cannot be sisters — the births are seven months apart — and the register puts them in different houses, which agrees. **Gračišće house 5 is the direct line's own second generation.***

**Also on the page: Jacobus Defranceschi, *civilitas*, born 21 July 1761** — *which matches the bachelor Jacobus already on the roster to the day.*

rows.got:
**The parents named only as «def. Vincentii et Mariæ» on the page before are here in full.**

**House 1 — Vincentius Sestan**, *civis*, **b. 25 March 1780**, married **12 February 1805**, **d. 1 December 1842 aged 62y 8m**; his wife **Maria**, **b. 1 January 1781**, **d. 30 October 1843**. Three sons: **Vincentius** (b. 12 December 1805), **Joannes** (b. 20 June 1809) and **Antonius** (b. 29 June 1814).

**Against Antonius the register writes «matrimonium inivit ut hic retro»** — *he contracted marriage as shown back here*. **The book cross-references its own households**: that is [the Antonius who married Joanna Defranceschi](/who/joanna-defranceschi-sestan/) in house 3, one page earlier. *So the «def. Vincentii et Mariæ» of page 5 and the couple on page 6 are the same two people, joined by the register itself rather than by this archive.*

**House 4 — Vicentius filius Vicentii** (b. 12 December 1805) × **Maria uxor n. Udovicich** (b. 2 December 1805), **married 8 February 1830**; son **Antonius Felix** b. 19 November 1830, confirmed 12 October 1841, married 3 March 1862; a second son died 17 October 1839 **aged 6y 10m 23d**. *The archive already carries a **Maria Udovicich** married to a Leonardus Defranceschi. **No connection is claimed** — Udovicich is a common Istrian name and two women of it in one parish prove nothing.*

**⚠ ONE WORD IS NOT READ, AND IS LEFT UNREAD.** *Maria Sestan's maiden surname is written* «nata …» *and this archive cannot make it out: the capital is a **P** or an **R**, and the ending is **-pros**, **-pras** or **-prod**. **No candidate is published**, because the rule here is that a hand is only legible against itself and no second construction of this word has been found in the book yet. Staring harder settles nothing. It waits for a comparison pass.*

**Petrus Defranceschi**, ***civilitas***, **born 17 April 1768**, died **1829 aged 61** — *a bare year with an age and no day.* **He had been on the roster from the family tree with nothing behind him.** *He is **not** the Petrus Defranceschi of **Rovinj** who also died in 1829; [both rows are kept](/corrections/), and the reasons are written down.*

**House 6 — Antonius Sestan, *filius Vincentii et Mariæ*, *militaris***, born 19 November 1830, **married 3 March 1862**, *«In domo sub N.º 4»*; and his wife **Anastasia, *agricola*, born 10 December 1830**, entered as ***«filia Simonis Grismanjch ad Joannæ Flegar»*** — **daughter of Simon Grismanjch and Joanna Flegar** — who came *«Ex Parochia sub N.º domus 13»*. *Their daughter **Maria**, born 28 February 1863, **died 28 June 1863 aged four months**.*

**Two more married-in surnames off one line** — *Grismanjch and Flegar* — **and Flegar caught an error this archive published this morning**: *the sixth priest of Gologorica, given as «Josephus **S**legar», is **Flegar**. The capital is the same letter as the F of «Antonius **F**abris» two rows below him. [Corrected](/corrections/).*

ev: The Bembo marriage, now in Gologorica's own book
The Bembo — a detail block at last
rows.got:
**A verification, and it is worth saying so plainly: this marriage was already published here.** *It came from the* «Atti» *of the Centro di ricerche storiche di Rovigno, quoting the **Valle (Bale)** register for **22 January 1795** — a parish a hundred kilometres from Gologorica.*

**What is new is that the home parish agrees, and adds three things.** *House 1 of the 1826* status animarum *gives:* **Petrus Defranceschi**, *civilitas*, **born 17 April 1768**, married **21 January 1795**; **«Anna Mater nata Bembo»**, **born 5 July 1779**; and **«Hermenegildus Filius»**, **born 4 October 1803**.

· **Anna's birth year was on David's tree and is now confirmed**, with the day and month added.
· **Hermenegildus is new.** *He is **not** the Hermenegildus already on the roster, born 10 April 1865 — sixty-two years later, plausibly a grandson named for him. The two are kept apart.*
· **A brace against the wife and son reads** ***«In partibus Venetias … habitant»*** — **they live in the Venetian parts.** *The household was split across the border. That is the first thing known here about the marriage after the wedding day.*

**On the one-day difference** — *Valle says the 22nd, Gologorica the 21st. **The Valle date stands**, being the marriage register itself rather than a census copying it out thirty-one years later.*

⚠ *Both dates on this page were misread at page scale before being zoomed: Petrus's birth as 1765 (it is **1768**) and Anna's as 3 July 1770 (it is **5 July 1779**). **Neither wrong reading was published.***

ev: The Jablich — a new family, out of Bakar
rows.got:
**The Gologorica baptism book after 1784 is not narrative Latin — it is RULED IN COLUMNS**, *and one of the columns is* **«Nomen Cognomen Patrinorum»** *with the godmother's maiden name written into it as a matter of course.* **That makes this book a register of married-in women**, which is exactly the thing David asked for, and no session here had opened it.

**⭐ The find: «Joh: Bapt. Defranceschi m.p. · Cath. ejus uxor nata JABLICH ex BUCCARI»**, both *Cives Gollogoricenses*, standing godparents on **3 October 1786**. **Catharina, wife of Joannes Baptista Defranceschi, born a Jablich of Bakar.** *This archive had no Catharina as wife of any Joannes Baptista — only two daughters of the name — and **Jablich appears nowhere in it**. [The family now has a page](/married-in/).*

**And Bakar is an old unanswered question here.** *«Bakar's parish registers» has stood on this register as a pending request for weeks. **This is the first person who gives a reason to open them.***

**A reading already in the archive is confirmed on the same opening**: *«**Theresia** Defranceschi **nata Grach**» as godmother — and a **Defranceschi as the officiating priest**, entered in the Baptizans column as «Defranceschi Plebanus Loci», which the archive knew from his signature alone.*

⚠⚠ **[WITHDRAWN 11 Oct 2026 — there is no «Catharina Defranceschi nata Grach».](/corrections/)** *The opening gives* «***Theresia*** Defranceschi nata Grach» ***twice***, *and two separate Catharinas — one née* **Jablich**, *one née* **Deprato** — *which is what the reading fused.*

⚠ *The surname was read **Jaklich** at page scale and is **Jablich** at five times magnification — the letter matches the b of «Buccari» written beneath it in the same hand. The wrong form was never published.*

rows.src: DAPA ZM34K-214 — two Maria Defranceschi of Gologorica, tested and NOT joined
rows.what: Whether the Maria who died in 1826 and the Maria born 20 July are the same woman.
ev: Why the two rows are kept apart
rows.got:
**Two entries, one birthday, and this archive is not joining them on that.**

· **Page 3 (M01069321):** *Maria Defranceschi,* **civilitas**, *died* **30 September 1826**, *aged* **37 years 2 months 10 days** — *which computes to a birth of* **20 July 1789**.
· **Page 11 (M01069329):** *Maria Defranceschi,* **civis**, *born* **20 July 1780**, *house 22, struck through.*

**The day and month are identical. The years differ by nine.** *At fourteen times magnification the written year reads **1780**; the final digit is a closed round form and **1789 cannot be wholly excluded**.*

**The test was run and did not settle it.** *The Gologorica baptism book for 1764–1788 is on the same reel; its opening for the summer of 1780 (M01068940) runs* **«Die 2 Julij»** *straight to* **«Die 3 Augusti»** — *no baptism on 20 July 1780 on that page.* **That is one opening, not the year**, so it is evidence and not proof.

**Both rows stay on the roster, separately**, *and the reason is written on each. Joining two women on a shared forename and a shared birthday, across a nine-year gap in a parish that produced thirty Marias, is the error this archive has caught in its own work three times this week.*

**Next step, named:** *walk July 1780 in MKR 1764–1788 (M01068915–M01068952) and July 1789 in MKR 1784–1880 (M01069008–M01069181). **Both are on this reel.** Whichever year holds a Maria Defranceschi baptised on the 20th decides it.*

rows.src: DAPA ZM34K-214 — the baptism of Maria Rosalia, 20 July 1789 (M01069020)
rows.what: The test named in work-list 165: walk July 1789 in the Gologorica baptism book and settle whether two Marias are one woman.

ev: The story, with the register plates
The mother corrected, and four rows made one
rows.got:
**✅ SETTLED, and the arithmetic is exact to the day.**

> **«Maria Rosa=/lia Defrances=/chi ex Loco»**, *house* **36**, *baptised by* **a.R.D. Antonius Giacich ex abatia**; *father* **«Joh: Baptis[ta]»**; *mother* **«Catharina JOBLICH»**; *godmother* **«Rosalia Baxa uxor Petri, ex Lindar»**. *The child is named Rosalia after her godmother.*

**30 September 1826 minus 37 years 2 months 10 days is 20 July 1789.** *So the woman who dies on page 3 of the 1826* status animarum *is this child, and she was thirty-seven.*

**Four roster rows had grown around her** — *one from the tree with the birth three years out, one from the pedigree with no dates and the wrong mother, one raised that morning from the death entry and explicitly refusing to identify her, and this. **They are now joined with `sameAs`, not merged**: every pid is kept, because a moved id is a dead URL.*

**⚠ And her mother is corrected.** *The pedigree had her as a daughter of **Mariana**. The register says **Catharina Joblich** — the same wife entered three years earlier as* «**Cath. ejus uxor nata Jablich ex Buccari**». ***Only this child is moved***; *the other five of casa 36 keep Mariana, because no register has been read for them and a man may have two wives.*

**The images are published with it**: *[three plates](/gologorica-line/) cut from the family's own copy of the film — the entry, the parents' columns, and the 1786 Jablich entry — each captioned with its film and frame so a reader can go back to the page rather than trust the transcription.*

rows.src: INTERNAL AUDIT — how much of the two Pazin reels has actually been read
rows.internalWhy: An audit of this archive's own reading, not a search of a record set. Counted so the figure can be checked rather than felt.
rows.what: David, 30 September 2026: «have you finished all the other files before moving to other registers?»
rows.film: ZM34K-214 and ZM34K-215 (DAPA)
rows.pages: counted across all 1,461 mapped frames
ev: How this archive works, and where it slipped
The frame map the count is measured against
rows.got:
**The answer is no, and the number is 4.0%.**

*Counted by taking every frame number cited anywhere in this archive's data and testing it against [the frame map](/gologorica-line/):*

| župa | book | frames | cited | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cerovlje | Status Animarum | 139 | 2 | 1.4% |
| Gologorica | MKR 1764–1788 | 38 | 3 | 7.9% |
| Gologorica | MKR/MKU/MKV 1770s | 55 | 2 | 3.6% |
| Gologorica | MKR 1784–1880 | 174 | 9 | 5.2% |
| Gologorica | MKR 1940–1948 | 17 | 2 | 11.8% |
| Gologorica | MKU 1646–1806 | 25 | 2 | 8.0% |
| Gologorica | MKU 1784–1880 | 91 | 2 | 2.2% |
| **Gologorica** | **Status Animarum 1826** | **121** | **13** | **10.7%** |
| Gologorica | Status Animarum 1862 | 144 | 5 | 3.5% |
| Gologorica | Status Animarum 1894 | 246 | 3 | 1.2% |
| Gologorica | Status Animarum 1921 | 117 | 2 | 1.7% |
| Gračišće | MKR 1667–1745 | 188 | 9 | 4.8% |
| Gračišće | MKR 1746–1840 | 106 | 5 | 4.7% |
| | **total** | **1,461** | **59** | **4.0%** |

**And the 59 flatters it.** *A good many are title cards and book boundaries cited while building the frame map, not entries walked.*

**⚠ What went wrong is method, not effort.** *Every find pointed somewhere else and the reading followed it: 1826 census → 1786 baptisms → 1780 baptisms → 1789 baptisms → Gračišće 1807. **Each step was justified on its own and the result is thirteen books opened and none finished** — which is the state that makes a corpus look worked when it is barely touched.*

**The rule adopted in consequence: finish the book you opened before opening another.** *The 1826* status animarum *first — 119 written pages, the household census that names every soul in every house, and the one that answers the question about the wives' families.* **This figure is to be re-counted and published each time, so it cannot be felt instead of measured.**

ev: The Gologorica line, with the plate
rows.got:
**Page 14 is house 7, and it is Carlo De Franceschi's own household in his own parish's book.**

**Confirmed exactly, against what this archive already held:** *Jacobus Defranceschi, civis, born* **21 July 1761**, *dead* **3 December 1850 aged 88**; *and* **«Carolus»**, born **17 October 1809**, dead **8 January 1893**. *Both to the day. **A verification, and said so.***

**Sharpened:**

· **Lambertina, «uxor nata Peschle»** — *this archive had* «about 1786»; *the book gives* **17 September 1786**, *with* **«Ex Volosca»** *in the provenance column and her death on* **16 July 1863, aged 76 years 10 months**. *Both the Volosca origin and the death date were already here and are confirmed.*
· **Josephus, her husband and Carlo's father** — *this archive had* «about 1763»; *the book gives* **4 March 1765**, *married* **3 February 1807**, *dead* **12 December 1838**.

**⚠ Two things left open rather than settled.**

· *Josephus's age at death is given as* **74 years 9 months**, *which puts his birth in* **March 1764**, *a year before the birth column says.* **The written date is taken and the tension recorded.**
· *His daughter* **Maria** *is entered* **16 August 182?** — *the archive holds* **16 August 1811**. ***The day and month agree exactly*** *and the middle digit is ambiguous between* **1812** *and* **1822** *even at three times magnification.* **Nothing is changed**; it wants a comparison pass against the same scribe's other years. *The same goes for* **Franciscus Xaverius**, *held here as 19 February 1816 and read on the page as 25.*

**Page 12** is a **Crosgnach** household — *twelve souls, the wife entered* «n. Skorta» — *and* **page 13** a single struck entry, **«Josephus Defranceschi, civilitas»**. *No Defranceschi is added from either; they are recorded as walked.*

rows.what: David: «Have we ever gone through the volosca books?»
rows.waypointNote: Five Volosko waypoints were already in kvarner-books.json and had never been used. The marriages film is given here as the one that matters.
rows.got:
**Never. And the archive already had the waypoints.**

*`kvarner-books.json` holds* **Volosko (Opatija)** *with five films —* **Births 1791–1831 (`9R28-3YD`), Births 1831–1886 (`9R28-3Y7`), Deaths 1792–1831 (`9R28-PY8`), Deaths 1831–1902 (`9R28-PY7`), Marriages 1792–1906 (`9R28-3T1`)** — *with its* `books` *array empty and its* `why` *blank.* **Nothing read, and no reason recorded for not reading it.** *Across 474 searches Volosca appears in two, one of them written the same morning.*

**⚠ And the obvious target is out of range.** *Lambertina Peschle, entered* «Ex Volosca» *in the 1826 household book, was* **born 17 September 1786**; *the births film starts in* **1791**. **Her baptism is five years before the film begins** — *recorded here so the next person does not spend a sitting looking for it.*

**The marriage of 3 February 1807 is the target that IS covered**, *on `9R28-3T1`, and it would name her father. [Raised on the work list](/worklist/); held until the 1826 census is finished.*

ev: The Orlis / Ortis — a new family page
rows.got:
**Page 15 — house 7 again, the next generation.** *«Franciscus Xaverius Defranceschi», Cives, married* **10 October 1859** *to* **«Clotilda uxor Ortis, filia Joannis ac Franciscæ»**, *born* **12 October 1834**, *coming* **«Ex Parochia Novacis sub N.º 2»** — **out of Novaki, house 2**. *Their son* **Victor Josephus**, *born* **22 April 1862**.

**Her birth and the marriage were already held** *from the 1894 census and are confirmed. **What is new is her parents and her house** — and [her family now has a page](/married-in/), where it had none.*

**⚠ Two open readings, neither forced:**

· *The surname is* **Ortis** *here and* **Orlis** *in the 1894 book. **Neither preferred**; the same scribe has not been found writing both.*
· *Franciscus Xaverius's birth is written* **25 February 1815** *on this page and* **25 February [18]16** *on the page before, against the* **19 February 1816** *this archive holds.* **The register says the 25th twice.** *Nothing changed — his baptism is in MKR 1784–1880 on this same reel, and that is the thing that would settle it.*

**Page 16** is a **Terdoslavich** household of eleven — *wives entered* «n. Gasparich» *and* «n. Bariz», *with movements* «od Par. Novaki sub N.º 95» *and* «Ex parochia N.º 68». *No Defranceschi; recorded as walked.*

**Eleven pages, two Defranceschi entries, and both of them struck through with no dates:** *a* **Leonardus Defranceschi** *at house 34 (page 23) and, earlier in the batch, the pattern already seen on pages 2 and 13 —* **a head of house entered, then crossed out**, *which appears to be how this book handles a house changing hands.*

*Read at five times magnification the name is* **S-a-l-m-a-n**, ***not*** *Salomon or Salamon — there is no* o *between the* l *and the* m. **No claim is made that this is [the Salomon line](/maternal/salomon/).** *What is recorded is the proximity, because it is the sort of thing a later session should know: a **Salman** born October 1796 at Gologorica, four kilometres from Gračišće, where the **Salamon** palace stands and where **Francisca Salomon** was born in **March 1797**. **Five months and four kilometres apart, and the archive cannot join them.***

**The Flegar/Jacotich alias is confirmed twice more** — *«Antonius Flegar filius Josephi Jacotich»* (page 17), *matching «Thomas Flegar alias Jacotich» in the 1787 baptisms.* **The same pairing settled this morning's correction of the priest's name**, *and the parish clearly used the two interchangeably.*

**The book changes language mid-page.** *Page 20 runs Latin down to* «Mathaeus filius» *and then writes* **«Giovanna moglie di Matteo n. Udovicich»** *and* **«Catarina figlia di Matteo»** *in Italian, before returning to Latin. **A name-form audit that assumes one language per book will mis-file these.***

*Movements out of the parish on these pages:* **Novaki** (houses 95 and 2), **Vižinada** (*«ad Parochiam Vicinadae»*, 1845), *and several within Gologorica by house number.*

**⚠ ONE FINDING HERE MATTERS MORE THAN ANY NAME: THE HOUSE NUMBERS WERE RENUMBERED.** *This archive identifies its two eighteenth-century Defranceschi households as* **«casa 31»** *and* **«casa 36»**, *from the 1780s baptism register.* **In the 1826 *status animarum*, house 36 is a Udovicich household** *(page 44, «Josephus Udovicich def. Joannis», with the bynames «Sindar» and «Pinter»).* **So a house number in one book is NOT the same house in another**, *and any reasoning that carries a casa number across books — as several notes in this archive do — is unsafe until the renumbering is mapped.* **Nothing is corrected yet**; *the fact is recorded so it is not walked into.*

**A GRAH on page 40** — *«Marianna Grah… filia Mathiae et Justinae», born 19 September 1834, in the Bubich household.* **Grah/Grach is the surname of Theresia Defranceschi née Grach** *in this archive's own pedigree. ⚠⚠ **[WITHDRAWN 11 Oct 2026 — there is no «Catharina Defranceschi nata Grach».](/corrections/)** *The opening gives* «***Theresia*** Defranceschi nata Grach» ***twice***, *and two separate Catharinas — one née* **Jablich**, *one née* **Deprato** — *which is what the reading fused.*  **The family is local to Gologorica**, which was not established here before. No join is claimed.*

**The register is fully bilingual by this point** — *Latin column headings, entries drifting between Latin and Italian within a single household («Giovanni figlio» beside «Josephus filius»), and place names written* **«Gollogorizza»**.

**Two conditions worth noting:** *a* **«Miles»** *— a soldier — in the Udovicich household at page 46, and the byname* **«Gospod»** *(lord, master) carried by three generations of Udovicich.*

rows.got:
**⭐ THE BOOK IS ORGANISED BY HAMLET, AND IT SAYS SO IN A COLUMN NOBODY HAD READ.**

*Every page of this census carries a* **«Pagus»** *heading at the top left. For the first fifty-six pages it reads* **«Gollogoritia»**. *At page 57 it changes to* **«Gollogorizia JACOTICHI»** *and stays there.* **The parish is being enumerated hamlet by hamlet**, *and the hamlets are named on the page.*

**That explains the Flegar/Jacotich alias** *this archive corrected a priest's name against this morning: **Jacotichi is a place**, and the families in it are called after it — «Josephus Flegar Jacotich», «Antonius Flegar filius Josephi Jacotich», «Josephus Udovicich Jacotich». **The «alias» is a hamlet name, not a second surname.***

**And it is a practical instruction for the rest of this reading.** *The Defranceschi houses sit in the main village pages; the later pages are other hamlets and will be other families. **A search that stops when it stops finding the surname will stop in the wrong place** — the hamlet headings, not the names, are what say where you are.*

**Seven pages, no Defranceschi.** *Households: Canzianich · Ghersan ×* **Canciainich** · *Canzianich ×* **Ghersovich** · *«Defuncti Antonii Crismanich» (an empty house) · Udovicich ×* **Flegar**, **Zovich** · *Flegar Jacotich ×* **Brajaka**, **Ghersavaz** · *Flegar ×* **Marion**, **Rabar-Baron** · *Udovicich Jacotich ×* **Tulla**, **Vlahovich**.

*A daughter christened* **Foska** *(Fosca) on page 53 — worth noting for any name-form audit, since it is neither the Latin nor the Italian the rest of the page uses.*

**✅ `walked` IS ACCURATE HERE, AND SAID SO DELIBERATELY.** *Every page in this range was opened one at a time and reported in sequence; the households and their maiden surnames are listed above precisely so the walk can be checked. **Few frames are cited because most pages hold nothing for this family** — a page read and found to contain no Defranceschi leaves no citation behind it, which is why [the walked check](/method/) can flag a true walk and has to be answered in words.*

rows.got:
**⚠ THE FILM SHOOTS SOME OPENINGS TWICE, AND THIS ARCHIVE'S COVERAGE FIGURE DID NOT KNOW IT.**

*Frames* **M01069386** *and* **M01069387** *are the **same page** — page 68, the bare* «Joannes Sogar» *at house 56 — photographed twice. Both were read before the repetition was noticed.*

**So the count of 1,461 frames overstates the number of distinct pages by an unknown amount**, *and [the coverage figure](/method/) is measured in frames, not pages. **The caveat is now printed with the number on every build.***

**Two attempts to measure the overstatement failed, and both failures are worth recording** *because the next person will have the same idea:*

· **Ink coverage** — *flagged 294 «pairs», which is plainly wrong: pages of one register naturally carry similar amounts of ink.*
· **Pixel difference on downscaled images** — *flagged 926, also wrong. Calibrated against the one duplicate confirmed by eye, it gives* **9.2** *for the true duplicate and* **2.8 to 13.1** *for genuinely different consecutive pages. **No separation at all.***

*The reason is physical: **two exposures of one page differ in film position and lighting**, while **two sparse pages of one register look alike**. **A duplicate cannot be found by how the frame looks; it has to be read.** Recorded as a failed method so nobody spends the afternoon on it again.*

**The hamlet reading is refined too.** *«Gollogorizia Jacotichi» runs pages **57–60 only**; page 61 returns to* «Gollogoritia». **The hamlets are interleaved sections, not one block at the end** — *which is a correction to what was written this morning.*

**Eleven pages, no Defranceschi.** *Households: Udovicich Jacotich ×* **Udovicich**, **Gasparich** · *Ancich ×* **Rabar Baron**, **Udovicich**, **Ancich**, **Race**, **Rabar** · *Rade/Ancich ×* **Ancich** · *Ghersan* · *Rabar ×* **Crosgnach**, **Udovicich** · *Sogar*.

*Given names worth an onomastic note:* **Foska**, **Gregoria**, **Euphemia**, **Sancta** — *none of them the Latin or Italian the rest of the page uses. A second set of **twins**, «gemini», born 14 February 1845.*

**⭐ PAGE 89 IS THE WHOLE HOUSEHOLD ON ONE OPENING — «Dnus Josephus Defranceschi», *Civilitas*, born 4 March 1765, married 2 February 1807; «Lambertina uxor nata Peschle», born 17 September 1786; and TEN CHILDREN.**

**The correction it forces:** *the last child is entered* **«Aloysius … filius natus VOLOSCA»**. *This archive had him* **«natus Polonia» — born in Poland** — *in three files, with a conclusion drawn from it.* **He was born at his mother's own town on the Kvarner**, *two lines below her own* «Ex Volosca». *[Corrected](/corrections/).*

**What the page confirms:** *Maximilianus Antonius* **9 January 1828** *and* **Enrichus Jacobus 11 March 1830** *both match this archive to the day; and* **Maria Aloisia, 16 August 1811**, *confirms the archive's date and **refutes my own misreading of page 14** — recorded as a correction against myself.*

**⚠ Six dates differ and NONE is changed.** *Josephus 13/17 March 1808 · Carolus 17/19 October 1809 · Franciscus Xaverius 19/25 February 1816 · Clementina 3 October/6 September 1822 · and a child this archive calls* **Anastasia, 8 December 1824**, *whom the census calls* **Maria Adelgidis, 8 October 1824**. *The census is a household book copied from the baptism register; **the baptism register is the better source and it is on this same reel**. Until it is read, the archive's dates stand and the differences are listed.*

**Seventeen pages walked.** *The rest are the village: Selesco ×* **Jacovich** · *Seleso ×* **Boisich** · *Boisich ×* **Seleso** · *Udovicich · Androssich ×* **Crosgnach** · *Crosgnach ×* **Udovicich** · *Perchich ×* **Bonassin** · *Lucacich ×* **Udovicich**, **Zaiz** · *Zuich ×* **Lucacich**, **Ivich** · *Ghersan ×* **Lavrinovich**, **Seleso** · *Pavetich ×* **Lucacich** · *Marenich ×* **Pavetich** · *Chalagaz ×* **Rabar**, **Udovicich** · *Zaiz ×* **Udovicich** · *Crismanich ×* **Pavetich**, **Jurando**.

*A second illegitimacy recorded plainly —* «Josephus Marencich **filius illegitimus** Rosae», *16 February 1861 — and a second* **Fosca**.

rows.got:
**✅ THE FIRST BOOK OF THIRTEEN IS FINISHED.** *The closing frame, M01069435, is a printed card reading* **«KRAJ — END OF…»**. *Every written page between the title card and it has been read.*

**⭐ Page 114 is unlike anything else in the book: THREE FOUNDLINGS FROM TRIESTE.**

> **Angelus Maria Angiussi**, *«ex expositis Tergesti»*, exposed and baptised **7 October 1844**, taken ***«in alimenta»*** by **Maria Crosgnach, wife of Josephus**, on 19 October 1844.
> **Adalbertus Almann**, *«ex expositis Tergesti»*, baptised **13 August 1844**, taken ***«in nutrimento»*** by **Anastasia Rabar, wife of Joannes**, on 19 November 1844.
> **Emilia Olmerling**, *«ex expositis Tergesti»*, baptised **18 November 1846**, taken by the same **Anastasia Rabar** on 7 February 1846.

*Three abandoned children of the **Trieste foundling hospital**, put out to nurse with Gologorica families and entered in the parish's own household book with their hospital surnames —* **Angiussi, Almann, Olmerling** — *none of which belongs to this parish or this region.* **This is how foreign surnames arrive in an Istrian village without a migration**, *and it is worth knowing before anyone builds a family on one.*

**And a Friulian marriage in plain sight:** *«Antonius **Cocolet** × Joanna uxor nata **FURLAN**» at house 7.* **«Furlan» is simply «the Friulian»** — *a surname that records where a family came from. This archive's whole [Carnia argument](/carnia/) is about Friulian movement into Istria; here is the word itself, in the register.*

**A third Defranceschi house number.** *Page 107 gives house* **74 / 120** *as* **«Defti Joan: B. Defranceschi»** — *of the late Joannes Baptista, the house standing empty — and by page 108 the same number carries a* **Bratizza** *household. **Another datum for the renumbering problem**, and another reason not to carry a casa number between books.*

**Twenty-six more pages walked.** *Rade ×* **Rade**, **Crismanich Sporer** · *Rabar-Baron ×* **Rade** · *Rade ×* **Ancich**, **Rabar** · *Ghersan ×* **Udovicich**, **Canzianich**, **Saez**, **Lucacich** · *Saez ×* **Stoisich**, **Udovicich**, **Synderich**, **Gherbavaz**, **Picoli**, **Crismanich** · *Rimanich ×* **Saez**, **Bratich** · *Rabar ×* **Saez Covebar** · *Selesso ×* **Stoisich**, **Braticich** · *Selesco ×* **Peterugosaz**, **Valcovich** · *Bratizza ×* **Callegaz**, **Nicoletta Bachini**, **Brota**, **Ghersan** · *Udovicich* · *Cocolet ×* **Furlan**, **Petorin**.

*Four* **Fosca**, *two more* **miles** *(soldiers), and two households of orphaned siblings entered as* «Soror» *and* «Frater» *with no parent at all.*

**✅ `walked` IS ACCURATE HERE, AND SAID SO DELIBERATELY.** *Every page in this range was opened one at a time and reported in sequence; the households and their maiden surnames are listed above precisely so the walk can be checked. **Few frames are cited because most pages hold nothing for this family** — a page read and found to contain no Defranceschi leaves no citation behind it, which is why [the walked check](/method/) can flag a true walk and has to be answered in words.*

rows.waypointNote: DAPA microfilm held offline; no FamilySearch waypoint. Cited by reel and frame.
rows.got:
**The title card reads «ŽUPA: GOLOGORICA · MATIČNA KNJIGA ROĐENIH 1784–1880 · SIGNATURA 3.4»**, *matching [the frame map](/gologorica-line/).* **M01069009 is a resolution test target** *and M01069012 a loose certificate slip of 27 January 1824 bound in at the front — film furniture, not pages, and worth naming so the count is honest.*

**The book opens with a Defranceschi baptising his own parish.** *The Baptizans column of folio 2 reads* **«Math: Defranceschi Ecclesiae hujus Gollogoricensis»** — *confirming from the register what this archive knew only from a signature,* «Ego Joannes Mathias Franceschi Parochus».

**⭐ And the fifth entry on the first written page is ours.**

> **«Josephi Anton Defranceschi ex Loco»**, *house* **36**, **6 January 1785**; *father* **«Joh: Baptista»**; *mother* **«Catharina nata JABLICH … BUCARI»**; *godparents* **«Antonius Couaz»** *and* **«Maria ejus uxor»**, *both* **Cives Pisinenses**; *midwife* **Maria Chrismanich**.

**He had no dates at all in this archive**, *carried only as «listed in the name index». He now has a baptism, a house, a mother and godparents.*

**And it is the third sighting of Catharina Jablich, and the first in a baptism of her own child.** *She stands godmother in 1786 as* «nata Jablich ex Buccari» *and is the mother of Maria Rosalia in 1789 as* «Catharina Joblich». **This corroborates the correction made yesterday** *moving Maria Rosalia from Mariana to Catharina.*

*The godparents came from **Pazin**. A household that fetches its godparents from the county town is not a peasant household — which agrees with the* **Civilitas** *this family carries in the census.*

ev: The Jablich, the Grach and the Ortis
rows.got:
**⭐ THE TWO JOANNES BAPTISTA HOUSEHOLDS ARE NOW TOLD APART BY THEIR WIVES.**

> **casa 31 — Joannes Baptista × THERESIA née GRACH**: *«Franciscus Antonius Defranceschi ex Loco»*, **13 April 1785**; *«Joh: Bapt: Defranceschi in Loco»*, **13 August 1787**.
> **casa 36 — Joannes Baptista × CATHARINA née JABLICH of Buccari**: *Josephus Antonius*, **6 January 1785**; *Catharina*, **5 March 1786**; *Maria Rosalia*, **20 July 1789**.

*Four of these five had **no dates at all** in this archive.*

**And the mother of casa 36 is corrected for the household, not one child.** *Yesterday Maria Rosalia was moved from Mariana to Catharina on one entry, with the note that moving her siblings on that basis would be the same error reversed.* **Three entries later it is the household.** *[Correction filed](/corrections/); **Mariana is not deleted**, because the archive's own source for her has not been re-read.*

**Two findings about other families:**

· **The Grach produced an archpriest.** *Franciscus Antonius's godfather is* **«Archipresbiter Grach» of Cherbune** — *his mother's own kin, and a churchman. New here.*
· **The Novaki connection is seventy-two years older than the marriage.** *Joannes Baptista's godfather in 1787 is* **«Matth: ORTIS ex Novacco»** — *and [Clotilda Ortis of Novaki house 2](/married-in/) married into this family in **1859**. **The same line also writes «Orlich»** for the godmother's late husband, of Pisino, which is why neither spelling is preferred.*

*Also: **Josephus Defranceschi and Hellena his wife** stand godparents in 1785; a **Defranceschi is the officiating priest** on most of these folios; and* **Maria Chrismanich** *is the midwife on nearly every entry in the parish.*

rows.src: DAPA ZM34K-214 — Gologorica baptisms, folios 8–24 (M01069020–M01069036), 1788–1799
rows.what: Walking the baptism book on. No Defranceschi baptisms in this stretch, but seven Defranceschi godparent entries that carry new facts.
rows.waypointNote: DAPA microfilm held offline; no FamilySearch waypoint. Cited by reel and frame.
ev: The Grach — a new family page
rows.got:
**No Defranceschi child is baptised between 1788 and 1799 in this book** — *the two houses had their children in 1785–1789 and the next cohort comes later.* **But the family is on almost every page as godparents, and the entries carry facts the archive did not have.**

**· Josephus Defranceschi was dead by July 1795.** *Folio 18 enters* **«Dna HELLENA vidua Joseph. Defranceschi»** *as godmother —* **widow**, *and styled* **Domina**. *This archive had the couple but not his death.*

**· Leonardus's wife gets a patronymic.** *Folio 13:* **«Matthia uxor Leon: Defranceschi filia Antonij»** — ***daughter of Antonius***. *She has stood in this archive as «maiden surname not captured»; she now has a father. **A «Matthia Couacich» appears beside Leonardus on folio 17 and may be the same woman with her surname — not claimed on one reading.***

**· The byname is a patronymic.** *Folio 13 also writes* **«Joh: Bap. Defranceschi filius Leonardi»** — *which is what* «detti Leonardi» *means, in the register's own words.*

**· The Defranceschi priest is succeeded.** *From 1795–96 the Baptizans column reads* **«Felix Ant. Bobich, plebanus loci»** *in place of* «Defranceschi».

**· And «Cherbune» is identified.** *The 1785 godfather* **«Archipresbiter Grach ex Cherbune»** *places the Grach at* **KRBUNE**, *45.2569 N 14.0472 E, four kilometres from Gologorica —* **not Cerovlje**, *which this register writes separately as* «Cerougl» *and* «Cerouglie». *[The Grach now have a page](/married-in/) and [Krbune is on the work list](/worklist/) with its waypoint* **`9R2Z-92G`** *— one volume, 1803–1870, never opened.*

*Also standing godparents in these folios:* **Catharina Defranceschi** *(1790),* **Joseph Defranceschi** *(1790, 1793),* **Antonius Defranceschi** *(1793, 1795),* **Leonardus Defranceschi** *(1794).* *The midwife on nearly every entry in the parish is* **Maria Chrismanich**.

**No Defranceschi baptism between 1799 and 1806** — *the two Joannes Baptista houses had their children in 1785–1789, and the next cohort comes later in the book.*

**⭐ But one small column settles something this archive had only inferred.** *Where* **«Mathea Defranceschi uxor Leonardi»** *stands godmother in* **1805**, *her* **Conditio Patrini** *is written* **Rust.** — ***rustica***. *On the same pages the casa 31 and casa 36 Defranceschi are entered* **Civ.** — ***cives***.

**So the register itself separates the two branches by class.** *This archive has described a «rustic line» and a «titled (Dominus) genteel line», reasoning from the* «detti Leonardi» *byname and from the* Dominus *title. **It can now cite the conditio column instead**, which is written on the entries rather than inferred from them.*

**Leonardus Defranceschi** *stands godfather in* **1801**; **Matthea** *in* **1795** *and* **1805**. *Her* **patronymic** *— «filia Antonij», 1792 — is now on her record; **she still has no maiden surname**, and the «Matthia Couacich» who appears beside Leonardus on one 1794 entry is noted as a possibility and nothing more.*

**The book changes hand and format at 1806**: *a new ruled layout with wider columns, fuller Latin («fil. Ant. et Oliva ejusdem uxor nata Fabar»), and a new officiant,* **«Ant. Ferd. Llocovich»**, *after Felix Antonius Bobich. **Anyone reading this book by eye should know it stops looking like itself at folio 38.***

rows.got:
**⭐ CARLO DE FRANCESCHI'S OWN BAPTISM, folio 51, house 17.**

> **«Die 19na 8bris 1809 · CAROLUS JOSEPHUS DEFRANCESCHI *natus die 17ma hujus, vespere*»** — *born on the 17th of October in the evening, baptised on the 19th.* *Parents* **«Dnus Josephus Defranceschi et Domna Lambertina ejusdem uxor»**; *godfather* **«Dnus Gioanni Curelich, Petinensis»** — *of* **Pićan**. *And a later hand has written* **«† 8/I 1893»** *above his name.* **The day he died, entered in the book that recorded his birth.**

**⭐ AND HIS BROTHER'S, at the foot of folio 65.** *«Die 25ta Februarii 1816 ·* **FRANCISCUS XAVERIUS JOSEPH DEFRANCESCHI** *natus die* **19na** *hujus mensis», with* **«† 4 Januarii 1893»** *in the margin and a godparent entered* **Nobilis**, *«da Lindaro».*

**✅ TOGETHER THEY RETIRE TWO OPEN DISCREPANCIES AND EXPLAIN A THIRD THING.** *This archive held Carlo at 17 October and his brother at 19 February; the 1826 census gave 19 October and 25 February. **Nobody was wrong: the archive held the births and the census recorded the baptisms.***

**⚠ Which is a warning about every date taken from that census.** *Its* «Nativitatis» *column gave Carlo's **birth** on page 14 and his **baptism** on page 89 — **the same book, inconsistent with itself**. [The four remaining date differences](/corrections/) are most likely the same thing and stay open until each baptism is read.*

**⚠ And a claim published this morning is withdrawn.** *The «rustica / cives» split — offered as the register separating the two Defranceschi branches by class — does not hold: the same Matthea reads* **Rust.** *in 1805 and* **Civis** *in 1810 and 1815. The column is one cell serving two godparents. **Caught by reading five more folios**, and [withdrawn to a question](/corrections/).*

**One structural fact worth more than any entry:** *this baptism book carries* **death dates in its margins**, *added later in other hands — «† 8/I 1893», «† 4 Januarii 1893», «† 18/5 1900».* **It is a death source as well as a birth one**, *and nobody reading it for baptisms alone would notice.*

*Also: **Catharina Defranceschi**, «Dni Joan: Bapta filia» — the child baptised 5 March 1786 — stands godmother in **1812**, aged twenty-six; and* **Mathia uxor Leonardi Defranceschi** *in 1810 and 1815.*

**⚠ CORRECTED 1 OCTOBER 2026 — THIS WAS MARKED `walked` AND SHOULD NOT HAVE BEEN.** *The frames listed above are the ones actually opened; the rest of the range was **not read**. This archive's rule, and the [Record Atlas](../Record%20Atlas)'s, is that* `walked: true` *means **every entry read**, and that overstating it is the worst error available here — because it tells the next person a book is finished when it is not.* **Caught by auditing my own claims against the frames I had actually cited, not by anyone pointing it out.** *The findings recorded from these frames stand; what is withdrawn is the claim that the ranges between them were read.*

**Twelve of the thirty-three skipped frames opened, and they were not empty.**

**⭐ A three-generation Ortis line at Novaki, connected to this family across seventy-two years.** *1787: godfather* **«Matth: Ortis ex Novacco»**. *1813: godfather* **«Dominus Joannes Ortis, Dni Matthiae filius, ex Novacco»** — ***his son***, *and both now styled* **Dominus**. *1859:* **Clotilda Ortis of Novaki house 2** *marries Franciscus Xaverius Defranceschi. [The family's page](/married-in/) had one generation; it now has three.*

**⭐ And Maria Rosalia, styled *Domina*, at twenty-four.** *1813:* **«Dna Maria Rosaria, defti Joannis Baptae Defranceschi filia, ex hoc Loco»** — *standing godmother, **her father already dead**, which agrees with the 23 January 1813 this archive holds for him. In 1820 she is still* **«coelebs»** — *unmarried — and she dies in 1826 at thirty-seven.*

**More of the family at the font:** *Jacobus Defranceschi (1791,* Civ.*); Antonius Defranceschi with* **«Theresia uxor Joh: Bap: Defranceschi»** *(1793); Leonardus (1798); and* **«Petrus Defranceschi»** *with* **«Math: Defranceschi uxor Leonardi»** *(1798).* **«Theresia Grach Defranceschi uxor Joh: Baptistae»** *(1805) writes her maiden and married names together on one line.*

**⚠ The Palman question is sharpened, against my own lead.** *Folio 25 gives* **«Theresia Palman en Loco»** *(1799, house 43, of Stephanus) — and the conditio column on that row reads* **Sutor**. *The 1826 «Franciscus Salman» is also entered* **Sutor**. **One shoemaking family, written Palman in the older book and Salman in the newer** — *which makes the resemblance to [Salomon](/maternal/salomon/) weaker still, exactly as [the downgrade](/corrections/) said.*

**⚠ And a second duplicate exposure, this time in the baptism book.** *M01069030 and M01069031 are the same opening shot twice. **The frame count overstates the pages here too**, and [the only way to find these is to read them](/method/).*

**Twenty-one frames of the gap remain open**, *and are named so the next pass knows where to start: M01069034, 037, 040, 043, 044, 046, 049, 050, 052, 055, 056, 058, 059, 062, 063, 065, 067, 070, 071, 073, 076.*

rows.got:
**⭐ THE BOOK CARRIES ITS OWN INSPECTIONS, AND NOBODY HAD NOTICED.** *Twice in these frames the register is interrupted by a dean's certificate ruled across the page:*

> **«Revisus in Visitatione decanali die 17ma Julii 1804 · M. Franciscus Franovich, Canonicus, Co[adjutor?] Regius Parochus et Decanus»**
> **«Revisus et approbatus in Visitatione Decanali 25 Junii 1808 · Petrus Anicich, Canonicus, Parochus et Decanus»**

*So the parish books were **inspected and signed off by the rural dean**, at least in 1804 and 1808. **That is a second record series implied by this one** — a deanery kept visitation records, and they would name the parish, its priest and its condition. Nothing of the sort is in this archive.*

**⭐ And father and daughter stand together at the font.** *1808:* **«Gio: Batta Defranceschi + Catharina Defranceschi ejusdem filia»**, *Cives / Civilis — the casa 36 head and the daughter baptised 5 March 1786, then twenty-two.*

**More of the family as godparents in the closed frames:** *«Batta Defranceschi» (1802); Catharina Defranceschi to a **posthumous** child (1804); «Mattia uxor Leon: Defranceschi» in 1806, 1807 (written* **«De Franceschi»**, *two words) and 1810; a Defranceschi godparent at Sestan's in 1814.*

**⚠ The Palman household gains a second wife, and a caution.** *1800:* **«Stephanus Palman + Sancta ejusdem uxor»**. *1808: the mother of his daughter Lucia is* **«Catharina nata Jurich»**. *Either he married twice or one reading is wrong — **not resolved**, and recorded so the [Palman/Salman question](/maternal/salomon/) is not built on a household this archive has half-read.*

*Also in these frames: a* **«Joannes Peer posthumus natus»** *whose father is entered* **«Defunctus»**; *godparents from* **Gračišće** *(«ambo Gallignanenses»),* **Krbune** *(«Cherbunenses»),* **Gradinje**, **Cerovlje** *and* **Kranj** *(«Crainburghensis», a* coqua *— a cook).*

**Eight frames of the gap remain: M01069037, 044, 049, 052, 055, 058, 062, 070.**

ev: Maria Aloysia's entry, with its plate
Two registers disagree about her birthday
rows.got:
**⭐ A DEFRANCESCHI BAPTISM SAT IN A SKIPPED FRAME, AND IT IS CARLO'S SISTER.**

> **«Die 17ma Augusti 1811 · MARIA ALOYSIA DEFRANCESCHI nata die 14ta hujus hora 8va mane»**, *house* **17**, *of* **«Dnus Josephus Defranceschi et Dna Lambertina ejusdem uxor»**; *godfather* **«Joannes Ant. Torbulla, Parochus Paspergensis»** — *the parish priest of* **Paz**.

**This is the entire justification for going back.** *M01069070 was one of the frames the sampled pass jumped over. **Reading at every third frame missed a baptism of the household this archive is built on.***

**⚠ And it opens a new disagreement rather than closing one.** *The baptism register says she was born the* **14th**; *this archive and the 1826 census both say the* **16th**. **That is not the birth/baptism gap that explained her brothers** — *it is two registers differing about a birth, the primary one written three days after the event. **The date is flagged, not changed.***

*Her second name* **Aloysia** *is new; this archive carried her as* «Maria» *alone.*

**⚠ A near-miss worth recording.** *On folio 31 the conditio beside* «Josephus Defranceschi + Cathari: Defranceschi coelebs» *appeared to read* **Merc.** — *mercator, a **merchant**, which would have corroborated this archive's [Carnia argument](/carnia/) directly. **At five times magnification the word sits in the *Status Baptizati* column, not *Conditio Patrinorum*** — it describes the **Marion** child's household, not ours. *The same column ambiguity that produced [the withdrawn rustica/cives claim](/corrections/). **Caught before publishing this time.***

**Krbune keeps appearing.** *Folio 39's officiant is* **«Rdus Dnus Joannes Natalis …vich, Presbyter CHERBUNENSIS, de licentia Parochi»** — *a priest of Krbune baptising here by licence, with godparents also* «Cherbunenses». *[The village is on the work list](/worklist/) and is turning out to be woven through this parish.*

**⚠ CORRECTED WITHIN THE HOUR. This row was published saying «all thirty-three skipped frames are now read». THIRTY were.** *Three remained — M01069049, M01069055 and M01069062 — and were found by counting the list against itself rather than trusting the sentence. **[They were then read](/searched/), and the claim is true now; it was not true when it was made.** This is the second overstatement of coverage in two days, both self-caught, and it is left visible because a habit that keeps recurring is worth seeing.*

**⚠ First, the reason this row exists.** *An hour earlier this archive published that* **«all thirty-three skipped frames are now read»**. ***Thirty were.*** *The three below had been listed as remaining and then not opened. **Caught by counting the list against itself before reading on**, which is the only reason it is not still standing.*

**They were not empty either.**

**· Folio 49 (M01069062), 1809 — two Defranceschi at the font on one page.** *«**Dnus Ant: Defranceschi**», styled* **Dominus**, *godfather on 22 June; and* **«Maria Rosalia Defranceschi»** *godmother on 1 July — **at twenty**, seventeen years before she died.*

**· Folio 42 (M01069055), 1807** — *«**Mathia uxor Leonardi Defranceschi hujates**», conditio* **Civis**. *One more against the withdrawn* rustica *claim.*

**· Folio 36 (M01069049), 1805** — *no Defranceschi, but the officiant is* **«Rdus Dnus Casparus Juran, Curatus CEROUGLENSIS, ob infirmitatem Plebani»** — ***the curate of Cerovlje, standing in because the parish priest was ill***. *With the Krbune priest on folio 39 and the Cerovlje wife in the 1826 census, **three parishes are now documented lending each other clergy and brides**, and [Cerovlje's own census sits unread on this same reel](/gologorica-line/).*

**✅ All thirty-three are now genuinely read — and this time the count was checked before the sentence was written.**

rows.got:
**⭐ THERE WERE TWO CLEMENTINAS, AND THE NAME WAS REUSED.**

> **28 January 1821**, house **104** — *«Clementina nata hodie hora 4ta mane»*
> **3 October 1822**, house **17** — *«Clementina Maria nata die 3 8bris hora 10 pomeridiana»*

*Both of* **«Dnus Joseph Defranceschi»** *and* **«Dna Lambertina nata Pesle»**. **The 1822 date matches this archive exactly; the 1821 child is new and appears in no later record of the household.** *Families reused a name when a child died, and that is the likeliest reading — **no death entry has been found for her**, and the 1826 census date sat between the two, which is what made the figure look wrong in the first place.*

**⚠ AND A PESCHLE OUT OF VOLOSCA — THIS ROW SAID SILESIA.** *The 1822 godparents are* **«Pietro Ant. Defranceschi»** *and* **«Amalia PESCHLE ex VOLOSCA»**, *both Cives Gollogoricenses.* ⚠ ***This row first read the word as*** «ex SILESIA» ***and [worklist 170 was raised on it](/worklist/); re-read at four times magnification on 11 October 2026, [it says* «**ex Volosca**»*](/corrections/) and the item is withdrawn.*** **Volosca, Fiume, Gologorica, Pazin — and Volosca.** *[The family's page](/married-in/peschle/) had the Kvarner right all along.*

**⚠ Lambertina's maiden name is written *Pesle* twice here**, *against* «Peschle» *in the 1826 census. **No form is preferred**; the archive uses Peschle because it has used it longest, not because it is established.*

**Two register practices worth knowing:** *a godmother standing* **«per Procuratricem»** — *by proxy, 1819 — and a mother recorded* **«hucusque in famulatu in Sumbergh»**, *in service away from the parish, at an illegitimate birth.*

*«Mathia uxor Leonardi Defranceschi» continues at the font in* **1817**, *conditio* **Cives**.

**⭐ MAXIMILIANUS ANTONIUS DEFRANCESCHI'S BAPTISM, folio 85, house 17.** *«9 Januarii 1828 ·* **natus heri media nocte**» — ***born 8 January at midnight, baptised the 9th***. *Of* **«Dnus Josephus Defranceschi et Domna Lambertina ejusdem uxor nata Pesle»**.

**His godfather was a dean** — *«Joannes Ant. Tesak, Canonicus … et Decanus»* — **which is the second time the deanery has surfaced in this book** *and strengthens [the visitation-records item](/worklist/).*

**⚠ And his own baptism margin disputes his death date.** *«† 6/8 910» —* **6 August 1910** *in Austrian usage, against the* **6 October 1910** *this archive holds. [Flagged, not changed](/corrections/).*

**The two books corroborate each other on the clergy.** *From 1824 the officiant is* **«Franciscus Brussich, Parochus»** — *the first of the eight priests [the 1826 census parish house](/gologorica-line/) lists, born 15 November 1780 at Vrbnik on Krk. **The census list and the register hand change at the same moment.***

**Lambertina's maiden name is written both ways inside five years**: *«**Peschle**» in 1825, «**Pesle**» in 1821, 1822 and 1828. **Still no preferred form.***

*Also: an* **emergency baptism** *— «ob periculum in mora, statim post nationem fuit domi ab obstetrice baptizata», baptised at home by the midwife with the godparent column left empty (1826); and* **Matthaea Defranceschi** *standing godmother in 1828.*

rows.got:
**❌ THE SALMAN LEAD IS WITHDRAWN, AND THIS FRAME IS WHY.**

> *12 July 1825, house 28 —* **«Franciscus PALMAN filius Stephani, Sutor»** *and* **«Antonia ejusdem uxor nata Brusich»**, *at the baptism of their daughter Maria.*

**That is the couple the 1826 census enters as «Franciscus Salman, Sutor» × «Antonia uxor n. Brusich»** — *and here he is given a* **patronymic**, *which a spelling variant cannot explain away: he is* ***filius Stephani***, *son of the* **Stephanus Palman** *who runs through this register from 1799.*

*Three entries write **P** and name a father; one writes **S**. **There is no Salman at Gologorica**, and the resemblance to **Salomon** was one scribe's capital. The lead was [published 30 September](/searched/), [downgraded 1 October](/corrections/) and is now withdrawn in full — **three days, three states, all three left visible**.*

**Also on the frame: a Defranceschi daughter this archive cannot place.** *«**Elisabianna filia Dni Defranceschi**» stands godmother with Josephus Flegar Jacotich, conditio* **Cives**. *⚠ **The forename is not certain** — it reads as* «Elisa=bianna», *perhaps Elisabetta Anna compressed — **and she matches nobody on the roster**. Recorded as an open name, not added as a person.*

---

**⚠⚠ `walked` WITHDRAWN, 5 October 2026, same day.** ***The crop used to read these frames cut the page at 62% of its height, and the written area runs further down.*** *It was found at folio 124 (M01069138), where six numbered entries stood below the crop; checking back showed the same on earlier folios — folio 89 has a sixth entry (Martinus Zajez, 12 November 1830) this archive never saw, and folio 90's lower band carries the whole opening of 1831, including an eighth Palman child.*

**So «every entry read» was not true of this row and the flag is set to false.** *The surname findings above stand — they were read and cited frame by frame — but* ***the nils in this row cover only the part of each page that was cropped***, *and a nil over part of a page is not a nil.* **[The correction is published](/corrections/)**, *and the lower bands are being read now; this row will be replaced by one that names what was actually covered.*

rows.got:
**One Defranceschi baptism, one Defranceschi godmother, and a property of the book nobody had noticed.**

**The baptism.** *«Die 28va Martii [1830] ·* **ENRICHUS JACOBUS DEFRANCESCHI** *natus* **11ma Martii hora 5ta Mane**», *folio 89, M01069102 — of* «Dnus Josephus Defranceschi, Civilis» *and* «Domina Lambertina ejusdem uxor nata Pesle». **The birth date this archive already held, confirmed to the hour; the page, the priest, the godparents and the midwife are new.** *The register spells him* **ENRICHUS**, *without the H, as does the 1826* status animarum. *Verification, not discovery, and said so on the page.*

**⭐ The second series of house numbers.** *From 1830 the* Domus *cell routinely carries two figures, the upper struck through and a second written beneath — clean through 1829, scattered in 1830, universal by 1831. Eight pairs read so far (103→61, 13→8, 100→58, 76→41, 97→53, 48→23, 6→2, and the Defranceschi line's illegible→104). **What the second series is has not been established**; [worklist 171](/worklist/) holds it with the method for settling it.*

**An open name.** *«Marianna filia E—di Defranceschi» stands godmother on 19 November 1830 (folio 90). The father's given name will not resolve — Eustachii, Ewaldi and Euxaldi all fit the space and none fits the strokes — so it is [recorded as an open name, not a person](/gologorica-line/), beside «Elisabianna filia Dni Defranceschi» of 1823.*

**⭐ FOUR HANDS THE PARISH-HOUSE LIST DOES NOT CONTAIN.** *The 1826* status animarum *names eight priests of Gologorica, and this archive had taken that for the roll of hands that wrote the registers. It is not.* **Georgius Dobrilla** *(Administrator, 1831–32),* **Joannes Harbich** *(Administrator Baptismorum, 1832–33),* **Marussich** *(given name not legible) and* **Josephus Schopf** *(Cooperator, «impeditis administratore parocho») all sign baptisms here and none of them is in the list of eight.* **House 1 of the census records who LIVED in the plebania; the baptizans column records who stood at the font.** *Both are true; neither is complete.*

**⭐ AND AT THE END OF 1833 THE REGISTER CHANGES LANGUAGE.** *Folio 96 opens* **«1833 adì 23 Xbre»** *and the entries turn Italian —* **Giovanni, Giuseppe, Giovanna, agricoltore** *— under Latin column headings.* **⚠ This row first said they stay Italian «from there on». They do not** — *the book returns to Latin on 6 May 1835 under Petrus Milcetich, and [the claim is corrected](/corrections/). The language follows the hand, not the year.* **This is the Svetvinčenat trap again** *(where a new archpriest in 1782 turned «Defranceschi» into «Franceschi» mid-volume).* ***Any search of this book after 1833 must run the Italian forms***, *and any nil recorded across that boundary without them is worth nothing. The nils below were run with both.*

**Collected in passing:** *a fifth child of* **Franciscus Palman × Antonia née Brusich** *(folio 95, 1833), the father entered* **Artifex** *where 1825 gave* **Sutor** — *consistent, and [the Palman/Salman withdrawal](/corrections/) stands.* *Twenty-two more pairs for the doubled-house-number table, printed on [the Gologorica page](/gologorica-line/).* *Places named in godparent cells:* **ex Parochia Gallignanensi** *(Gračišće),* **ex Gradine**, *and* **ex Gollogorizza** *in its Italian form.*

rows.got:
**Three Defranceschi women in fourteen months, after ten folios of nothing — and all three are wives or godmothers, never daughters.**

**⭐ SANCTA ALEXANDRA DEFRANCESCHI gets her first document.** *Held until today from David's MyHeritage tree alone, with an empty note. Folio 102 (M01069115), 20 February 1840, house 2:* «**FRANCISCUS** natus hodie», *of* «**Joannes Sestan**, agricola» *and* «**Sancta Alexandra nata DEFRANCESCHI**». **A husband, a house and a son she did not have before.**

**⭐ CLEMENTINA DEFRANCESCHI stands godmother at that same baptism**, *entered* «ille clavium faber, **haec civis**» *beside the locksmith Franciscus Marciolin.* ***A Clementina Defranceschi alive and chosen as a godparent in February 1840*** *lands directly on [the archive's own open contradiction](/corrections/) about which Clementina died when — and does not settle it, because the entry gives no age, no household and no patronymic.*

**⭐ FRANCISCA DEFRANCESCHI, 14 April 1841**, *godmother at house 2 again, the surname squeezed onto the line below.* **Verification, not discovery** — *she is the Francisca who married Antonius of house 6 on 29 January 1840 and came «Ex Parochia Gallignanæ sub N.º 5».*

**⭐ FOUR MORE DEANERY VISITATIONS, and the deanery's seat.** *«Vidi. **PETINAE**» — Pićan — on* **7 May 1838, 14 January 1839, 13 January 1840 and 15 January 1841**, *all signed* **Franciscus Coverlizza, Decanus**. *Fifty years after the diocese of Pićan was suppressed, its deanery still sits there and the dean signs there. [Worklist 169](/worklist/) now carries a third named dean and an address.*

**On the register itself:** *the doubled house numbers stop. Folios 100–102 carry a single figure per entry again, where 1830–1835 carried two.* *Folio 101 is a **struck draft** of the 1840 entries and folio 102 their fair copy — **and they disagree**: the draft gives Joannes Sestan as* «sutor» *then* «lapicida», *both cancelled, where the fair copy says* **«agricola»**. *Neither trade is taken.*

**NIL, in the exact terms tried.** *M01069084 (folio 71, the year 1820) read entry by entry —* **Casparus Bosaz alias Scaccarin, Fusca Apolonia Cancinich alias Travpich, Helena Ancich alias Soldatich** — *for* **Defranceschi · De Franceschi · Defrancesco · Franceschi · Francesco**. *The surname is in none of its columns.* **That frame was the last hole in the 1820–1822 range, which is now contiguous.** *And the folios that would hold the three women's own baptisms — 1818 to 1822 — have therefore now been walked end to end:* ***none of the three is baptised in them***, *so they were either not born at Gologorica or born to a Defranceschi household this archive has not found.*
