Frames 6–49 (pages 2–89) were read earlier on 12 Oct; frames 50–88 (pages 90–148) the same day. ⚠ From frame 52 the film RE-SHOOTS every opening that carries a pasted slip, with the slip lifted — so frames 53, 64, 72, 75, 77, 79, 81 and 85 duplicate the opening before them. Every such pair was read in both states.
rows.got:
**EIGHT CHILDREN OF MARIA DEFRANCESCHI, where this archive had two.** *Petrus Kirac of Medulin and Maria Defranceschi «oriunda e Pomer» baptised* **Lucas** *(16 Aug 1874),* **Stephanus** *(23 Dec 1876, d. Pula 1966),* **Catharina** *(18 Feb 1879),* **Maria** *(13 Mar 1882),* **Thomas** *(7 Aug 1884, d. 13 Aug 1884),* **Agnes** *(8 Aug 1885, m. Antonio Fedel 1906, d. at* **Ližnjan** *1964),* **Antonius** *(25 Jan 1888, d. 4 Nov 1888) — and* **Fusca** *(1895), whom the archive already had from the deaths book.* ***Three of the eight died as infants.*** *Six are new people;* **Lucas's «about 1874» becomes a date**, *and the entry gives his death, 16 September 1930.*

**⚠ A NINTH IS NOT CLAIMED.** *December 1889, page 145: infant «Petrus Kirac», mother's cell «Maria … Defrancesco», godparents «Petrus Kirac et Agatha uxor ejusdem» — the same couple who stood for Antonius in 1888.* ***The father's cell is empty.*** *Not faint —* **empty**: *a contrast stretch at seven times magnification returns clean ruled lines and no ink.* *Recorded as an unconstrued entry naming the surname.*

**⭐⭐ THE PASTED SLIPS CONCEAL NOTHING, AND THAT IS A METHOD FINDING.** *A 1961 registrar's slip is glued over two entries on page 95, and more over pages 113, 127, 131, 133, 134, 136 and 137.* ***The film re-shoots every slipped opening with the slip lifted.*** *Confirmed five separate times; the two «concealed» entries on page 95 are* **Petrus Vojak** *and* **Nicolaus Grahalich**, *neither of the name.* **Where a film shows a pasted slip, look for the re-shot frame before recording a gap.**

**⭐⭐ ONE MAN, THREE STATES, TWO FORCED NAME CHANGES.** *Petrus Vojak, baptised 27 June 1871, is made* **Vogliacco** *by decree of the Prefect of Pola, 22·X·1937, and restored to* **Vojak Petar** *under art. 29 of the Law on Personal Names, Pula, 1961 —* ***the 1961 slip is pasted over his own baptism entry.*** *The book also carries an Austrian* «*Decreto I.R. Luogotenenza Tergestina*» *permitting Tomasich → Tomasić, and some forty Italian prefectural decrees of 1930–38 (Radossevich → Ardossi, Grahalich → Gracali, Lazarić → Lazzari, Privrat → Privato, Sirovich → Sironi …), each undone by a Yugoslav slip of 1961–75.* **For a study of a name spelled nine ways, this is the machinery itself, dated and numbered.**

**⚠ A NEAR-MISS WORTH RECORDING.** «**Maria De maschi**», *wife of Joannes Radossevich, appears on pages 125 and 129 and is* ***not*** *a Defranceschi.* *The same scribe writes* «*Maria De ___*» *for both surnames, and at page scale they are not distinguishable.* **Every «De» construction in this hand was magnified before it was accepted or rejected.**

**THREE CHILDREN, ONE HOUSE, ONE COUPLE.** *Lucia* **(b. 27 Sep 1844),** *Michele* **(b. 4 Oct 1847)** *and* **Maria (b. 1 Jun 1852)** — *all house 5, all to «Tommaso Defranceschi, gm Michele» and «Maddalena Buich, gm Paolo».* **Maria is the mother of the eight Kirac children baptised at Medulin.** *Each entry was magnified 2–5×; the 1847 hand wrote «Buich» in the patrini column of the next row, which settles the reading against the scribe's own pen.*

Matthaei, maritus Luciae Defranceschi, agricola», 62y 11m 20d, consumptio** *(frame 43)*.

**⭐ THE CHECK THAT MATTERS: Tomas's age at death (59, in 1858) and at marriage (43, in 1843) put his birth at 1799 and 1800 — two books, fifteen years apart, in agreement.**

**NOT FOUND:** *no Defranceschi decedent appears in 1867–1910 — Lucia's death, if before 1910, is not in the book, and she was alive in 1899. **Nothing for the surname in the 1904–1910 pages; the register's last page is 60, 1910.***

**⚠ AN INDEX LINE WITH NOTHING BEHIND IT:** *the old book's front index lists «Antonio Defranceschi d.º Mattulia — 22» and «Defranceschi Ant.º — 22». The index's numbers (33, 40, 113) run past the 11 pages the book holds, so they belong to an earlier book or numbering not on this film. **The earliest Defranceschi at Pomer is therefore an index line, and is recorded as one.***

**A pointer to correct:** *the book's pages 10–11 carry 1817–1820 entries beside 1863–1866 ones — the old book was re-used, so «page 11, 1866» is not the end of a continuous run.*

Every opening of images 4–13 read at the child and father columns (2–3 the cover and the flyleaf with 'Registro dei Battezzati 1820'; entries begin on image 4 and end on image 13 at 28 January 1821); **images 14–41 are the book's own index «Prenome e Nome» of the children, by tab C to Z, one page to a letter or two: A–B (images 19–20), C–D (21–22: Da Vera, Da Lauro, Dabalà, De Dea, Davero), F (24: Facco, Ferrari, Fedinelli, Fasan, Forza), G (25), L (30), M (31), N (32), P (34), R (36), S (37), T (38), V (40), Z (41) — all of it read: no Defranceschi, De Franceschi, Franceschi or Franceski.** The fathers are Marine seamen, sailors and gunners; no father or mother named Defranceschi. 42 is the end-of-item target. Terms tried by eye: Defranceschi, De Franceschi, Di Franceschi, De Francesco, Franceschi, Franceski. Reading depth: about 0.7× at the child, father and mother columns; the godparents were not read. Two years of 1820 baptisms are not our question, but this is the volume most nearly of the age of Antonio Defranceschi's generation.

rows.src: POLA MARINE BAPTISMS Nov 1866–May 1871 (9R2Z-K6P, «Geburts- und Tauf-Buch» of the k.k. Marine at Pola, Tom. second, with its own index of children) — walked end to end: NO Defranceschi
rows.what: The second Pola Marine baptism register in the printed German form, from 16 Oct 1866 to 3 May 1871 (70 images; five to six entries to the page: regiment or corps, place and date of birth and baptism, the child, religion, sex, legitimacy, the father with his rank, the mother with her father's name and rank; every entry signed by the chaplain «Joh. Germ(eck)» / «Adm. Capl.»). It is the direct predecessor of the book 9R2C-K68 (1863–76) in which Peter Nicolaus (1874) was found, and of the same series as 9R2C-928 (1846–67). Every opening of images 4–62 read at the child, father and mother columns (2–3 the film label, cover and flyleaf; image 62 a note in Italian of 25 Mar 1872 closing the book with the stamp of the chaplain Colomban Be…; 7 a loose receipt of 50 kr. stamp). The fathers are the Pola Marine's seamen, petty officers and officers, arsenal workers and gendarmes (Springer, Gamerith, Moro, Ferracini, Toncic, Wittek, Peter, Sarcich …). **The book's own index of the children's surnames («Geburts-Buch», A–Z, with the page) is on images 63–69 and was read: A (Amberger, Andriatius …), B (Bider, Bernardi, Bradamante, Baldini, Beizl, Bianchi …), C, D (image 63: Dotto, Danzinger, Doria, Dandolo, Dovich, Dellrat, Dennig, Daman, Dinesbergher), F (image 64: Tuscari, Franzlich, Fohr, Fuchs, Fagan, Franzlich), N–P (65), S (66–67) — none is Defranceschi, De Franceschi, Franceschi or Franceski.** 70 is the end-of-roll target. Terms tried by eye: Defranceschi, De Franceschi, Di Franceschi, De Francesco, Franceschi, Franceski, and Franceschi. Reading depth: about 0.65× at the child, father and mother columns; the godparents were not read. A child of Johann Defranceschi's would be here only if born 1866–71: his first child Raimund Johann (b. Oct 1871) falls after this book's last entry; K68 image 182 has him.

rows.src: MARINE BAPTISMS AT TRIEST, VENICE AND POLA 1848–1863, with a few later additions to 1881 (9R2C-VZ7, «Geburts- und Tauf-Buch» of the k.k. Marine, item 9 of the Zagreb archive's «Matična knjiga … rođenih», roll 47) — walked end to end: NO Defranceschi
rows.what: The k.k. Marine's first long baptism book in the printed German form (169 images; six entries to the page: regiment or corps, place and date of birth and baptism, the child, religion, sex, legitimacy, the father with rank, the mother with her father and birthplace, godparents, priest, and an «Anmerkung» margin). It begins with a few copied-in entries of 1848–50 and runs from Trieste (the Marine's headquarters until 1853), Venice (the Arsenal and the Marine barracks) and, from 1855, Pola, to the end of the Marine Corps year 1863; the last pages (images 164–167) are loose later additions of 1864–81 («Isolirte» = the isolated, i.e. children baptised outside the corps's usual parishes) — Baumol, Albanese, Fleischmann, De Paulay, Cada. Every opening of images 4–161 read at the child, father and mother columns (2–3 the film label, cover and flyleaf; image 162 a folded typed transcription slip of April 1859 headed «Copia», pasted over the next page; 163 a blank pasted sheet; 168 the end-of-item target). The fathers are the Marine's infantrymen, seamen, bandsmen, gunners, officers and arsenal workers (Springer, Zuanelli, Mohr, Scarpa, Bellemo, Corsaro, Bandera, Moro, Barry, Povich …). No father or mother named Defranceschi, De Franceschi, Franceschi or Franceski, and no child by any of the three of Johann's names. Terms tried by eye: Defranceschi, De Franceschi, Di Franceschi, De Francesco, Franceschi, Franceski. Reading depth: about 0.65× at the child, father and mother columns; the godparents and the «Anmerkung» margins (later notes of marriage and death) were read only where they ran into the mother's column, so a later note naming a Defranceschi would not have shown. Together with 9R2Z-KX7 (1856–66), 9R2Z-K6P (1866–71), 9R2C-K68 (1863–76), SPR, K6L and the later books it closes the Pola/Trieste/Venice Marine baptisms from 1848 to 1898 except two books (C6X, ZJ7, ZN5) not yet read.

rows.src: MARINA VENETA BAPTISMS AT VENICE 1820–1846 (9R2Z-C6X, Italian «Libro Battesimale» of the Imp. Reg. Marina, item 1 of the Zagreb archive's roll 48) — walked end to end: NO Defranceschi
rows.what: The long Italian «Libro Battesimale» of the Imperial Royal Marine at Venice (163 images; four entries to the page, the printed Italian columns for the date of birth and baptism, the child, the parents with their rank and trade, the godparents and the remarks; pages 1–158, the entries written at the Marine's parish church of San Biagio and the Marine chapel of S. Martino by the chaplains Gian'Antonio Mastrovich, Bonaventura Ramynack and later priests, and kept for the Marine's officers, clerks, arsenal workers, gunners and seamen of Venice). The first entries are of Feb 1820 (with a few earlier ones copied in: births of 1816–19); the book runs to Jan 1846 (image 161, page 158: the last entries — a Dalmatian infantry child baptised at Zara and loose later notes). Every opening of images 4–161 read at the child, parents and godparent columns (2–3 the film label, cover and flyleaf; 162 the end-of-item target of roll 48). The fathers are the Marine's ensigns, captains, surgeons, accountants, watchmen, caulkers, masters of the arsenal's sail-loft and the Venetian arsenal families (Molinari, Manao, Paulucci, Dieckes, Pisner, Eisner, Hochkofler, Doria, Dorigo, Scarpa, Zanetti, Cappelletti …); the near names «Doria», «Dorigo», «De Piero», «Degan» are different surnames. No father, mother or child named Defranceschi, De Franceschi, Franceschi or Franceski. Terms tried by eye: Defranceschi, De Franceschi, Di Franceschi, De Francesco, Franceschi, Franceski. Reading depth: from 1828 on the child's surname is written large and bold, and images 51–161 were read at 0.5×, images 4–50 at 0.65×; the godparents and the later «Osservazioni» notes were read only where they ran into the parents' column, so a later margin note naming a Defranceschi would not have shown.

rows.src: MARINA VENETA BAPTISMS AT VENICE (9R2Z-ZJ7, Italian «Libro Battesimale», item 5 of «Matična knjiga ratne mornarice rođenih 1821–1851», film-titled 1796–1827) — images 4–130 walked end to end: nil
rows.what: The Marina Veneta baptism ledger on the film (136 images; four entries to the page). Images 4–60 are in an ornamented chancery cursive in which the child's surname is legible only at high zoom; images 4–27 were first looked at at 0.9× (partial, not a nil) and then ALL of 4–130 were read again from DeepZoom level 13, the left-centre two thirds of each page, one tall panel per page at 0.38–0.62×, so that the child's name and the father's rank/surname line were legible entry by entry. From image ~61 the hand is a plainer round script. Every entry on images 4–130 was read; the book is NOT mostly blank after image 60 (an ink-density scan showed entries on almost every page 29–130), which corrects the first text of this row. Fathers throughout are corporals, sergeants, privates and gunners of the Marine Artillery Corps and the Marine Infantry Battalion («Marina Veneta»), with mostly Venetian mothers; marginal notes seen include «recte Bolobani» (order of 26 July 1847, image 79), a legitimation entry of 19 Feb 1838 (image 70), a pasted Venetian parish certificate of 1846 for a 1840 baptism (images 90–91) and a folded flap (image 101, opened out on 102). Surnames that recur and could be mistaken for the name: Fabris, Fortunato, Ghisetti, Bruttoloni/Brustoloni, Mazzobel, Mazzucato, Cecchini, Griffi, De Lorenzi, De Nobili, Dalzuffo — none is Defranceschi. Image 131 is the «CONTINUED ON ANOTHER ROLL / ROLL NUMBER 48» slate, 132 the Croatian State Archives «Nastavak» slate, 133 the resolution chart, 134 «END OF ROLL», 135 blank. Terms tried by eye on every entry: Defranceschi, De Franceschi, Di Franceschi, De Francesco, Franceschi, Franceski. Reading depth: images 4–130 entry by entry at 0.38–0.62× from level-13 tiles; no marginal index in this book. The book continues on another roll (not this waypoint).

rows.src: PULA BIRTHS 1896–99 (9R28-3YS, Latin «Liber Baptizatorum Ecclesiae Concath. Polensis», 296 images) — walked spread by spread, images 7–294: five baptisms of the name's households and people, seven sightings in all
rows.what: The civil-parish baptism book of Pola 1896–99; images 3–6 are the Croatian State Archives slate, the target and the cover, 7–294 are the entries (about a dozen to a spread, printed form, a clear hand), 295 the end slate; no index at the back (images 265–294 checked). Each spread read at DeepZoom level 11 in two halves; father's and mother's surname columns and the godparents read on every entry. Terms tried by eye: Defranceschi, De Franceschi, Di Franceschi, De Francesco, Franceschi, Franceski. Images 7–294 (July 1896 to 23 July 1899, mid-page, the last entries on the upside-down closing leaf, image 294; a few spreads carry loose Ordinariate letters of 1915 correcting other children's entries, lifted on the next frame; images 59 duplicates 58): **one entry of the name — Umbertus Antonius Eduardus, image 33.** Franceschini entries (Gotardus, images 23, 26; a godmother on 23) are the adjacent name and not counted. Book X ends there; the sequel (vol. XI, from 24 July 1899) is not on this film. From image 188 a translucent repair sheet lies over p. 810–812 and parts of 193–194; those leaves were re-read at level 13 and on the frames where the sheet lifts, and the upside-down frames 179–180 and 196–197 were rotated to read the entries the 1911 and 1901 protocol slips covered. Reading depth: each spread at DeepZoom level 11 in two halves (about 1,400 px a page); the parents' columns are clear at that size, the godparents' (patrini) column is smaller and was read less surely — godparent sightings found so far were each re-read at level 13, and a godparent surname in a cramped hand may have been missed on a spread where the parents' names were not ours. Later loose slips (1911, 1931 and 1993 Zagreb and Bolzano civil-registry extracts) lie over parts of images 146, 178, 195, 275–276, 281 and 290–292; each covered page was read on the frame where the slip lifts or at level 12–13 through the tissue. No marginal index at the back (images 265–294 checked).
rows.film: FamilySearch 9R28-3YS · Pula births 1896-1899
rows.got: **Seven sightings of the name in this book, on five baptism entries (two children, one mother, three sponsor entries):** (1) **Umbertus Antonius Eduardus Defranceschi, b. 8 Oct 1896, bapt. 15 Nov at house 34 — son of the chimney sweep Joannes (f. Francisci) and Dominica Clagnan (Angeli), both of Pola; godfather Voltolina Antonius; a margin note: «uxorem duxit Annam Zulian[i], Polae 31.X.1920».** Previously index-only in household h047; now `doc`. Told in [households](/households/). **Also: a godmother «Defranceschi Antonia», 17 July 1898 (book p. 823, image 200)** — at the baptism of Joachim Joannes Maria Valle; no age or parents given. Told in [the Pula section](/places/). **And, on image 204, a married Defranceschi woman: «Defranceschi Maria, qm Francisci, e Moncalvo [Gologorica]», wife of Salamon Aloisius of Gallignana, mother of Elda Maria Aloisia (bapt. 7 Aug 1898), with a second godmother «Defranceschi Lina».** Told in [the Pula section](/places/). **And, on image 210, a fifth child of h047: Julius Petrus, b. 19 May 1898, bapt. 11 Sept 1898 (house 34), son of Joannes (gn Francisci, camini scopator) and Dominica Clagnan (gn Angeli).** Told in [households](/households/) and [the Pula section](/places/). **Images 213–214: two godfathers of the name — «Defranceschi Antonius, faber murarius» (24 Sept 1898) and «Defranceschi Angelus, piscator» (28 Sept 1898).** Told in [the Pula section](/places/). **Everything else on images 7–294 — some three thousand entries (an estimate from about a dozen to a spread, not a count) — is clear of the name, and the book has no index.** The book ends on 23 July 1899; the volume that follows is not on this film.

XI, 9R28-3YS does not hold it); the other civil births books 9R2X-SP8 (1815–74), 9R26-BZQ (1874–87) and the rest of 9R2Z-3T1 (1887–96); the 1894 baptisms of Angela Regina (4 Nov 1894) and Francisca Angela (27 Sept 1891); the marriage of Aloisius Salamon × Maria Defranceschi.

rows.src: PULA BIRTHS 1874–87 (9R26-BZQ, 699 images) — walked spread by spread, images 6–384 and 390–698 (from p. 494 of Liber VII, 19 May 1874, the last pages of 9R2X-SP8 item 4, to the end of the book, 9 Jun 1887): four entries of the name — Ida Revelant's baptism (1876), Paula Poliak's (1884, mother «Franceschi» of the Trieste orphanage), a godmother «Defranceschi Aloysia» (6 Mar 1887) and a godfather «Defranceschi Antonius» (24 Apr 1887)
rows.what: The civil-parish baptism book of Pola for 1874–87, a printed form with a patrini column. Image 6 on is the first spread; images 70–72 are a tissue-mended leaf set. Each spread was read at DeepZoom level 11–12 in two page-halves (parents', godparents' and midwives' columns). Terms tried by eye: Defranceschi, De Franceschi, Di Franceschi, De Francesco, Franceschi, Franceski. Images 6–112 (19 May 1874 to 5 March 1876): none. Near-misses noted and not counted: «Defrangha» (image 90), a mother «Defanzer» (image 110) and several Franceschini. Reading depth: godparents' column at about 1,400 px a page, less sure than the parents'. Images 125–384 (May 1876 to 5 Aug 1881, end of the 1875–81 book at image 384; image 385 is its end-of-item slate and 386–387 the slates of the 1881–87 book (Liber VII), which starts at image 390 as a fair copy with no patrini column; loose Trieste ordinariate slips of 1941 and an ink blot at images 328–329 hide only patrini, and the same entries are read on the neighbouring frame): no further entry of the name. A smeared marriage note at entry 305 (image 225) was read at level 13 as «Del Fone Armando», not our name; a «Defrangha» (image 90) and «Defanzer» (image 110) are different names. Incidental: a Fornasar household of Gallignana (entry 345, image 227) is told on [the maternal page](/maternal/). Liber VII/VIII images 390–471 (Aug 1881 to 31 Dec 1882): nothing of the name. Loose slips and a Graz parish letter (images 439, 463, 464, 467) are lifted on the following frames. Liber VIII images 472–577 (Jan 1883 to 29 Dec 1884): one entry of the name — Paula Poliak, bapt. 28 Dec 1884, mother «Franceschi Francisca ex Orphanotrophio Tergesti» (image 577) — the same woman as the mother of the 1894 Joannes Antonius. A loose Italian birth-certificate form of the 1940s lies over p. 951 on image 576 and is lifted on 577. Liber VIII images 578–616 (Jan 1885 – 30 Dec 1885): nothing further of the name (Franceschini entries on images 579, 604, 611 and 614 are the adjacent name and not counted; a Vienna letter of 1891 lies over p. 1027 on image 615 and is lifted on 616). Liber VIII images 617–698 (Jan 1886 – 9 Jun 1887, pp. 1030–1151, the end of the book): read spread by spread in two page-halves. **Two sightings: (1) «Defranceschi Aloysia», godmother (with the mason «Detoma Antonius») at the baptism of Maria Catharina Ursula Dilena, 6 Mar 1887, p. 1117, image 669 — the surname split across a line, «Defranc-/schi», re-checked on the displayed image on 18 Oct 2026; (2) «Defranceschi Antonius», godfather (with «Bilus Catarina») at the baptism of Elvira Catarina, daughter of Carolus Scagnetti and Aloysia Tomsich, 24 Apr 1887, p. 1133, first entry, image 676 — zoomed at level 13 and re-checked.** Near-names not counted: Franceschini (pp. 1039, 1104, 1142 and others, the adjacent name), «Defranza Maria» (godmother, p. 1044, entry 179, image 627 — re-checked), «Fiandanese Gemma» (p. 1052), «De Angelis», «Delfabro», «Denardi», «Deperis», «Depreto», «Detoma», «Dilena». Loose papers: legal extracts of 1887 over pp. 1030–31 (images 618–620; both pages are read clear on neighbouring frames), slips over pp. 1064, 1080–81, 1091 and 1098–1101 (each page is read clear on a neighbouring frame, except that the foot of p. 1091 stays partly hidden on image 652), and a repair sheet over pp. 1137–38 (images 678–679) that covers part of the godparents' column on both pages and appears on no other frame — a nil for those two pages' patrini is not a fully read nil. The register's last entry is on p. 1151 (image 687, 9 Jun 1887). Images 688–693 are the back board with a 1907 Vienna Pfarramt letter; 694 is the «END OF ITEM» slate (roll 39); 695 the Croatian State Archives «KRAJ» card; 696 a resolution target; 697 a second end slate; 698 a blank. **A note on method, 18 Oct 2026:** part way through, the page images appeared in my transcript as «[media removed: request limit]» and I withdrew several passes as unseen; I then re-checked pages 627 (the Defranza godmother), 669 and 676 and the notes I had made earlier from them were accurate in every detail, so the reading was real and the withdrawal was mistaken. It is recorded here because it cost three corrective commits.

rows.src: PULA BIRTHS 1887–89 (9R2Z-3T1 item 1, Liber IX, images 7–187) — walked spread by spread from the first entry (19 Jun 1887) to the last (30 Dec 1889): three entries naming the name — Petrus Matthaeus Zuban (1888, mother Leopolda Defranceschi), a margin note on Maria Regina De Stefano (1888) of her marriage to a Franciscus Defranceschi in 1908, and a margin note on Ricardus Bearcco (1887) of his marriage to an Angela Defranceschi in 1914
rows.what: The civil-parish baptism book of Pola from 19 June 1887 (it starts where 9R26-BZQ stops), a printed form with a patrini column. Images 1–6 are slates, cover and target; the entries begin on image 8. Each spread read at DeepZoom level 11–12 in two page-halves (parents', godparents' and midwives' columns, every entry). Terms tried by eye: Defranceschi, De Franceschi, Di Franceschi, De Francesco, Franceschi, Franceski. **Images 7–72 (19 Jun 1887 – 12 May 1888, pp. 1–117): nothing of the name. Images 73–187 (12 May 1888 – 30 Dec 1889, pp. 118–340, the end of Liber IX): three entries — (1) entry 473, p. 143 (image 86, 15 Jul 1888): «Petrus Matthaeus», b. 29 Jun 1888, son of «Zuban Emericus, Matthaei e Pyrrhano, faber ferrarius» and «Defranceschi Leopolda, Antonii e Gallignana» — Leopolda's first child, with a margin note of his own marriage on 23 Feb 1914 to Anna Pecinić; (2) entry 464, p. 142 (same image, 19 Jul 1888): Maria Regina De Stefano, b. 7 Jun 1888, with a margin note «Juncta est matrimonio Polae die 5/8 1908 cum Franc… Defranceschi», and a second marriage on 17 Sep 1913; (3) p. 147, second entry (image 88, baptised 24 Jul 1888): Ricardus Franciscus Andreas Bearcco, b. 19 Oct 1887, with a margin note «copul. Polae … 21.XI.1914 cum Angela Defran-/ceschi». All read at level 13. Images 91–93 (5–25 Aug 1888, pp. 152–157): nothing further; «De Caneva», «Deangeli» and «De Angelis» are different surnames. Images 94–96 (25 Aug – 8 Sep 1888, pp. 158–163): nothing further; a foil patch over the foot of p. 162 (image 96) hides part of the last entry's godparents and the lower margin of two entries, with every parents' column legible; a repair slip over p. 163's margin. Images 97–187 (8 Sep 1888 – 30 Dec 1889, pp. 164–340): nothing further (a Franceschini, p. 178, is the adjacent name).** Franceschini (p. 29, p. 102 and others) is the adjacent name and not counted. Loose papers: a Venice birth certificate over p. 21 (image 18; p. 21 is read clear on the next frame), Graz and Zürich letters over p. 77 (images 49–50) and a 1909 Ordinariate letter over p. 87 (images 53–55, lifted on 56), a repair-tape stain across the godparents' column of p. 77; no entry's parents are hidden. A note on image 50 says pp. 79–80 are bound after pp. 81–96; they were seen on images 61–62. Image 18 re-checked on the displayed image on 18 Oct 2026. Before this walk only the births-index-targeted pages of the book were read (Joannes Antonius Franceschi, 1894). Near-names not counted in images 118–135: «Dignano»-born parents, «de Domini», «Delcaro», «Dorigo», «Delise» and a «Defranza»-type clerk's «Savorgnan»; none is the surname. A pasted Italian birth declaration lies over p. 301 on image 166/167 and is read clear on the next exposure; a repair patch covers the foot of p. 299 (image 165) without hiding any parents' column. Near-surnames not counted in images 172–183: «Deghenghi», «Delmestre», «Derin», «Dambrosi», «Degrassi», «Dorigo», «Dobrez», «Depase». A black repair patch covers the foot of p. 333 (image 183) and hides only the last entry's lower lines. Images 184–187 (14–30 Dec 1889, pp. 334–340): nothing further; the right-hand half of image 187 is the blank inner leaf, 188 the «END OF ITEM» slate (roll 40) and the title card «Matična knjiga rođenih 1890–1893, Item 2» (images 188–189). A black foil repair patch covers the foot of pp. 334, 339 and 340 and hides lines of the last entry of each; no parents' column is hidden. A «Franceschin» (p. 336) is the adjacent name.

Images 188–189 are the title card, 190 a resolution target, 191 the spine, 192 the cover; entries start on image 193. Terms tried by eye: Defranceschi, De Franceschi, Di Franceschi, De Francesco, Franceschi, Franceski. **Images 193–267 (2 Jan – 28 Dec 1890, pp. 342–469, the whole of 1890): one entry — p. 384, entry 261 (image 221, baptised 20 Apr 1890): «Joanna Maria», b. 11 Jan 1890, daughter of «Zuppan Henricus [Emericus struck through] Matthaei, faber lignarius, e Pyrrhano» and «Defranceschi Leopolda, Antonii, e Gallignana» — Leopolda's second child; read at level 13. Nothing else of the name.** (Incidental: on p. 369, entry 173, the baptism of Antonius Michael Destefano, a brother of Maria Regina De Stefano of [households h134](/households/) — told on her row.) rows.got: **One entry of the name so far: p. 31, 18 Apr 1869 (image 430), a godfather «Giovanni De-/franceschi, capo e […]» at the baptism of Giuseppe Giovanni Deola, a Belluno labourer's son (level 13); told in the Pula section and on the roster; possibly the navy servant Johann Defranceschi of h132 before his 1871 naval marriage (`inf`, undecided). New to the archive (no earlier entry of the name at Pola in 1869).** **A second entry, a re-read and not a discovery: p. 92, 26 Dec 1869 (image 461) — the baptism of Giovanni Battista (b. 15 Dec 1869), son of «Francesco De franceschi fu Giovanni da Galignano, Daziere» and «Eufemia Franca fu Giovanni da Parenzo» (h129, level 13): the index entry of the archive's own chimney sweep's baptism, now opened; adds the father's work in 1869 («daziere»).** **A third entry, found in a margin: p. 275, baptism of 31 Dec 1871 (image 554), «Giovanni Beniamino», b. 26 Dec, son of «Gregorio Mohorat di Francesco da Bogliuno, pittore in arsenale» and «Rosa Cheba di Giorgio da Barbana»; a later hand writes beside it «Die 14.IV.1911 cum Defran-/ceschi Domi-/nica matri-/monio est iunctus» (level 13): the groom married a Dominica Defranceschi on 14 April 1911; a stamp of the surname changed to «Ermacora». New to the archive (no Mohorat or Ermacora groom, no 1911 marriage of a Defranceschi bride, was held). The bride is not identified (the roster's Dominica Francisca Clagnan, h047, and the Dominica of 1865, h037, are the candidates; neither is merged); the 1911 marriage entry is not found: the margin does not say where it was made, FamilySearch's Pula civil marriages stop at 1901, and the naval marriage book 1866–1918 (9R28-VZN, read 16 Oct 2026) has one Defranceschi bride, of 1914, none of 1911; the next step is to ask where the entry is. Told in the Pula section and on two roster rows.** **The wife of h047's own family, found: p. 332, baptism of 18 Aug 1872 (image 583), «Antonio Giuseppe», b. 3 Aug, son of «Klagnan Angelo fu Pietro da Pedoglia di Monfalcone, muratore» and «Delise Maria fu Giovanni da Rovigno»; a margin note «Legittimato col matrimonio … 4/11 1872» (level 13, day and month only). The same couple as the parents of Dominica Francisca Clagnan (b. 1868, her 1868 baptism item 3 p. 428 entry 422, `doc`), the wife of Joannes Baptista Defranceschi (h047): her younger brother. Not a Defranceschi entry; told on the Pula page and on two roster rows. The parents' marriage of 4 Nov 1872 is not yet looked for (9R28-T3F, Pula marriages 1815–77, not read entry by entry).** **A plain «Franceschi» godmother: p. 350, baptism of 27 Oct 1872 (image 592, entry 468), «Gasparo Giovanni Antonio», b. 18 Oct, son of «Skoblar Gaspare di Giorgio, i. r. sergente» and Lucia Maria of Zara; the sponsors «Pancovich Giovanni» and «Maria, vedova di Domenico Franceschi» (level 13, the surname plain, no -ni, no De). The spelling is in scope; she is a woman named by a dead husband, undated. The archive's Franceschini household of Montona (Domenico q. Giorgio, muratore, wife Maria Miletich of Pola, four Pola baptisms 1857–63, items 2–3) is the candidate, `inf`, undecided, not merged. **A «Maria Franceschini» stands godmother twice more at the same font (p. 265, 23 Nov 1871; p. 369, 19 Jan 1873; p. 405, 21 Jun 1873, the last two at level 13): four times in nineteen months, which leans toward one woman, the widow Maria Franceschini (`inf`).** Told on the Pula page and one roster row; next: a Pola death of a Domenico Franceschi before Oct 1872 (9R2C-T3D).** **A fourth entry, a re-read that corrects a date: p. 378, baptism of 23 Feb 1873 (image 606, entry 91, house 87 Duomo), «Francesca Luigia», b. 1 Feb 1873, daughter of «Francesco Defranceschi fu Gio. Batta da Gallignana, distretto di Pisino, Daziere» and «Eufemia Franca fu Giovanni da Parenzo» (level 13); sponsors Matteo Potočnik, fornajo, and Angela Venezia; midwife Giovanna Chinol. It adds no person; roster row, h129 and the Pula page corrected (pid francisca-defranceschi-1872 stays frozen).** **Pp. 1–495 (1 Jan 1869 – 25 May 1874; images 414–668) read, every page image displayed, four entries of the name, above.** Near-names seen, none counted: **Pp. 494–495, none of the name** — no Franc… surname in any column; **Depolli** (a De-name, not counted): p. 494, 19 May 1874, entry 257 (Petrus Paulus Thomas, b. 17 May; father «Depolli Antonius Petri filius, faber lignarius navalis», mother Nicolini Antonia); **Franković, Franzin, Franceschini, Francovich, Franelić, Defranza, Delise, Demori, Decarli, De Caneva, Del Negro, Galignana, Gologorica, Visinada, Draguć: none**; the given name only: «Franciscus» as a patrinus, a father or an infant's name (p. 494, entries 256 and 261; p. 495, entries 264, 265 and 267); **Dobrez**: the midwife «Maria Dobrez/Dobretz» on p. 494 (21 May 1874, entry 260) and p. 495 (20 and 24 May 1874, entries 263 and 265; at entry 263 she herself baptises «necessitatis causa»); no «Franc…» surname in any column of pp. 494–495

Also listed for Crikvenica kind V: 1738–1793 (Župni ured, «O = Blagajnička knjiga», ZM-34J/249), 1800–1823, 1822–1855 and 1856–1858 (Hrvatski državni arhiv, ZM-34/043, digital), 1859–1908 (Državni arhiv u Rijeci, ZM-34J/028, not digital). **Verification, not discovery:** the signature was already on the HDA page and in errand 29 (searched 8 Sept 2026); the entry is now named in the errand. **Terms tried:** place «CRIKVENICA» (plain; the list also holds «CRIKVENA» and two «CRIKVENICA MJESTA…» forms, not run in the working form), confession RIMOKATOLICI, kind V. **Control:** Proložac, same settings, returned three marriage rows (1858–1885 Split ZM-34F/936; 1885–1935 and 1935–1949 Imotski ZM-34F/1118). **The trap:** selecting items by script or by clicking the list returned «Nema zapisa» for both Crikvenica and the control; only typing the place into the box and letting the search fire gave rows.
rows.next: Send errand 29 (it now names the 1912 entry).

rows.src: Belgrade — municipal death register for 3 November 1975 (Palilula) and the Historical Archives of Belgrade: web search of what is published
rows.what: How to reach Uršula Kovačina's Belgrade death entry; whether 1975 books are at the archive
rows.got: **Not established.** Terms tried (two web searches, Serbian): «izvod iz matične knjige umrlih Beograd opština Palilula istorijski arhiv Beograda … čuvanje rok 100 godina zahtev za pretragu»; «Istorijski arhiv Beograda matične knjige umrlih 1975 Palilula genealogija istraživanje porodice zahtev». They return the Law on Civil Registry Books (City of Belgrade and its municipalities keep the books; extracts are public documents; books are kept in two copies) and the archive's address and hours; none says where 1975 death books are, or how a descendant asks. A copy of the Law was fetched but not read to the retention clause. Nothing is claimed about access.
rows.next: Ask the Palilula registry office for an extract of the death entry of 3 Nov 1975, quoting the notice number 350 of 24 Feb 1976 on the Crikvenica baptism margin.

rows.got: **Found: 29 June 1849, «sina zakonitih Tome Kovačina, služitelja pri c. kr. financii, i Marie …» — «Petar»**, baptised by the «Kapelan Dražki»; godfather a corporal of the finance. Read at level 13 on the date and the father's line. The mother's surname is the index's «Škovich»; **not independently read**. It fits the death entry (born Draga, 55 in 1904). **David's family account has this Petar «of Rijeka»; the page gives Draga, kotar Sušak.** Index query that found it: `q.fatherSurname=Kovacina`, `q.surname=Kovacina`, country Croatia, 736 rows, filtered to forenames Petar/Pero/Pietro/Pedro. **Not walked:** pages 120–121 only were looked at; no sibling or earlier entry of the family was searched.

rows.src: FamilySearch — Uruguay collections (civil registration 1879–2020, parish books 1726–2000, passenger lists 1888–1980), index search for Kovacina and nine other spellings
rows.what: Petar Kovačina the joiner, said by the family to have died in Uruguay in 1910
rows.got: **Nil in the index; not a nil in the books.** **Terms tried:** surnames Kovacina, Covacina, Kovachina, Cobacina, Covacena, Kovacsina, Kowacina, Kovazina, Covasina, Kovasina, country Uruguay, each with and without a death-year filter of 1909–1911 (the filter was probably not honoured; the results did not change). The index returns neighbours only — Kovačić, Kovachich, Kovasi, Covacich, Cobaina — none a Petar or Pedro dead in 1910. **No register of 1910 was read page by page**, so a death under another spelling, or in a department whose books are not indexed, is not excluded. **Control:** the same endpoint returned Croatian rows for the same surname (736), so the search itself works.
rows.next: Browse the Uruguay civil registration of 1910 by department; or ask the family for the name the emigrant used abroad.

rows.what: The Crikvenica parish marriage book for 1859–1908 (item 1 of the roll, «Matična knjiga vjenčanih 1859–1908», Župa Crikvenica; images 0–2 the roll number, a blank and a resolution chart, 3 the start-of-film target, 4 the item target, 5 a chart, 6 the spine, 7 the cover, 8 the first leaf). Printed Latin table, five entries to the opening: the left page holds sponsi and sponsae with place, religion, ages and status, the right page the parents, witnesses, the priest and the banns. Every cell is read with the page images displayed; targets are the surnames Defranceschi in every form (De/Di Franceschi, Defranceski, Franceschi, Franceski), Kovačina, Kalanj, Hreljac, Jarmacki, Geiger, Oreščanin, Stipanić, Alafetić, Blašković, and Car and Stojčić only where tied to Marija Car's people (Vjekoslav = Vincentius, and Vinka) or to the Kovačina line. **Layout (from the images seen):** img 8 leaf 1 (entries 1–5, 26–31 Jan 1859;
